1:2.headline: תהו sounds like the word for being amazed
1:2.body: Rashi links תהו to the verb תוהא, 'is amazed': a person would stand amazed at the emptiness. Bereshit Rabbah pictures the earth itself sitting there תוהא ובוהא, bewildered.

sources.says: Rashi says תהו means astonishment and desolation, because a person is astonished at the emptiness in it.
sources.quote: תֹּהוּ לְשׁוֹן תֵּמַהּ וְשִׁמָּמוֹן, שֶׁאָדָם תּוֹהֵא וּמִשְׁתּוֹמֵם עַל בֹּהוּ שֶׁבָּהּ:

sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says the earth sat there תוהא ובוהא, bewildered.
sources.quote: כָּךְ יָשְׁבָה הָאָרֶץ תּוֹהָא וּבוֹהָא,

1:5.headline: 'One day' where the other days are 'second', 'third'
1:5.body: The verse says יום אחד, 'one day', where the pattern would give 'first day'. Rashi says 'one' fits because God was alone in the world then, before the angels were made.

sources.says: Rashi asks why it says 'one', and answers that God was alone in His world and the angels were made on the second day.
sources.quote: לָמָּה כָתַב אֶחָד? לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה הַקָּבָּ"ה יָחִיד בְּעוֹלָמוֹ, שֶׁלֹא נִבְרְאוּ הַמַּלְאָכִים עַד יוֹם שֵׁנִי,

sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah, in the name of Rabbi Yudan, says on that day God was alone in His world.
sources.quote: שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יְחִידִי בְּעוֹלָמוֹ,

1:10.headline: Why 'seas' in the plural when there is one sea?
1:10.body: Rashi asks why the verse says ימים, 'seas', and answers that fish from one water taste different from fish of another. Ibn Ezra says no single sea circles all the land.

sources.says: Rashi asks why 'seas' and answers that the taste of fish differs from one water to another.
sources.quote: וַהֲלֹא יָם אֶחָד הוּא? אֶלָּא אֵינוֹ דוֹמֶה טַעַם דָּג הָעוֹלֶה מִן הַיָּם בְּעַכּוֹ לְטַעַם דָּג הָעוֹלֶה מִן הַיָּם בְּאַסְפַּמְיָא:

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it says 'seas' because no single sea surrounds all the land.
sources.quote: ואמר ימים בעבור שאין שם ים שיקיף כל הארץ:

1:26.headline: וירדו can mean 'let them rule' or 'let them go down'
1:26.body: Rashi says this one word can mean 'rule' or 'go down'. If a person earns it he rules the animals, and if not he sinks below them.

sources.says: Rashi says the word carries both ruling and descending: one who earns it rules animals, and one who does not is ruled by them.
sources.quote: יֵשׁ בַּלָּשׁוֹן הַזֶּה לְשׁוֹן רִדּוּי וּלְשׁוֹן יְרִידָה; זָכָה, רוֹדֶה בַחַיּוֹת וּבַבְּהֵמוֹת, לֹא זָכָה, נַעֲשֶׂה יָרוּד לִפְנֵיהֶם וְהַחַיָּה מוֹשֶׁלֶת בּוֹ:

sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah, on the same word in the next verse, says: if he earns it, 'rule', and if not, 'go down'.
sources.quote: אִם זָכָה רְדוּ, וְאִם לָאו יֵרְדוּ.

1:28.headline: וכבשה is spelled so it can mean 'he conquers her'
1:28.body: The word is written without a ו. Rashi says it can be read as 'he subdues her', and draws two lessons from that: a husband keeps his wife from wandering, and the duty to have children falls on the man.

sources.says: Rashi says the missing ו teaches that the man subdues the woman, and that the duty to have children falls on the man, not the woman.
sources.quote: חָסֵר וָי"ו לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁהַזָּכָר כּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת הַנְּקֵבָה, שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא יַצְאָנִית, וְעוֹד לְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁהָאִישׁ שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לִכְבֹּשׁ מְצֻוֶּה עַל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וְלֹא הָאִשָּׁה:

sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says the word is written so it can be read as 'he subdues her', and that the man is commanded to have children.
sources.quote: וְכִבְשֻׁהָ, וְכִבְשָׁהּ כְּתִיב, הָאִישׁ מְצֻוֶּה עַל פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה

1:31.headline: The extra ה in 'the sixth day'
1:31.body: Rashi says the added ה on the sixth day, at the end of creation, hints at the five books of the Torah. God made the world on the condition that Israel would accept them.

sources.says: Rashi says God added a ה to the sixth day to show He made creation on the condition that Israel accept the five books of the Torah.
sources.quote: הוֹסִיף ה' בַּשִּׁשִּׁי בִגְמַר מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית, לוֹמַר שֶׁהִתְנָה עִמָּהֶם, עַל מְנָת שֶׁיְּקַבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲמִשָּׁה חֻמְּשֵׁי תוֹרָה.

10:9.headline: Nimrod's 'hunting': animals, or people's minds?
10:9.body: Ibn Ezra reads ציד plainly: Nimrod was a mighty hunter of animals. Rashi reads it as trapping people's minds with his words and leading them to rebel against God.

sources.quote: צד דעתן של בריות בפיו, ומטען למרד במקום
sources.says: Rashi says he trapped the minds of people with his mouth and loaded them with rebellion against God.

sources.quote: והוא החל להראות גבורות בני אדם על החיות, כי היה גבור ציד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he began to show human strength over the animals, for he was a mighty hunter.

10:19.headline: באכה means 'as you come to', like giving directions
10:19.body: Rashi says באכה is like a man telling a friend that the border runs until you come to the border of some other place. Ibn Ezra reads באכה גררה simply as 'to Gerar'.

sources.quote: ולי נראה כאדם האומר לחברו, גבול זה מגיע עד אשר תבא לגבול פלוני
sources.says: Rashi says it seems to him like a man telling his friend that this border reaches until you come to the border of so-and-so.

sources.quote: באכה גררה. אל גרר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says באכה גררה means 'to Gerar'.

10:21.headline: Shem is Japheth's brother, not Ham's: Rashi says why
10:21.body: Rashi says Shem and Japheth both honoured their father, so they are named together. Ramban adds that this marks Shem as the brother of the righteous one, not the wicked one.

sources.quote: שאלו שניהם כבדו את אביהם, וזה בזהו
sources.says: Rashi says those two both honoured their father, and one is linked with the other.

sources.quote: גם זה לומר שהוא אחי הצדיק ולא אחי הרשע
sources.says: Ramban says this also means he is the brother of the righteous one, not the wicked one.

10:25.headline: The verse itself says why he was named Peleg
10:25.body: The verse says Peleg was named because 'in his days the earth was divided'. Rashi says Eber was a prophet who named his son for what was coming. Rashi says the split was the languages mixing and people scattering across the world.

sources.quote: למדנו שהיה עבר נביא, שקרא שם בנו על שם העתיד
sources.says: Rashi says we learn that Eber was a prophet who named his son for what was to come.

sources.quote: נתבלבלו הלשונות ונפוצו מן הבקעה ונתפלגו בכל העולם
sources.says: Rashi says the languages were mixed up and the people scattered from the valley and spread across the world.

sources.quote: כשנולד היו מכינים הפלגה, לפיכך קרא שמו פלג
sources.says: Radak says that when he was born they were preparing the dispersion, so he called him Peleg.

11:3.headline: הבה is not just 'come': it means getting ready together
11:3.body: Rashi says הבה always means people preparing themselves and joining in a task, a plan or a burden. Ibn Ezra says it is like 'give' and comes from the root יהב.

sources.quote: כל הבה לשון הזמנה הוא, שמכינים עצמן ומתחברים למלאכה או לעצה או למשא
sources.says: Rashi says every הבה is a word of readiness, where people prepare themselves and join for a task, a plan or a burden.

sources.quote: ומלת הבה כמו תנה ושרשו יהב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הבה is like 'give' and its root is יהב.

11:4.headline: 'Make us a name': fame, or an idol?
11:4.body: Ibn Ezra reads שם as fame and praise: a tall tower for a sign and a name. Sforno reads it as an idol that would stand in the tower.

sources.quote: ולבנות מגדל גבוה להיות להם לאות ולשם ולתהלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they wanted to build a tall tower to be a sign, a name and a praise for them.

sources.quote: נעשה שם – עבודה זרה שתהיה במגדל
sources.says: Sforno says 'let us make a name' means an idol that would be in the tower.

11:8.headline: They built 'lest we be scattered', and God scattered them
11:8.body: In verse 4 they say פן נפוץ, 'lest we be scattered'. Here God scatters them. Rashi says what they feared came true. Rashbam says this is why God scattered them.

sources.quote: מה שאמרו פן נפוץ, נתקים עליהם
sources.says: Rashi says what they said, 'lest we be scattered', came true for them.

sources.quote: והם בחרו להם מקום לשבת שם, ואמרו "פן נפוץ". לפיכך הפיצם משם בגזרתו
sources.says: Rashbam says they chose a place to settle and said 'lest we be scattered', and therefore He scattered them from there by His decree.

11:2.headline: Why 'Shinar'? The verse is silent, and the sages say 'shaken out'
11:2.body: The verse does not say why the land was called שנער. Radak records the sages' answer: the dead of the flood waters were shaken out there, because it is a valley.

sources.quote: ולא ספר הכתוב למה נקרא שנער, ורבותינו זכרונם לברכה אמרו
sources.says: Radak says the verse does not say why it was called Shinar, and gives the sages' saying.

sources.quote: לפי שמתי מי המבול ננערו שם לפי שהיא בקעה
sources.says: Radak says the sages said it is because the dead of the flood waters were shaken out there, since it is a valley.

11:32.headline: Terah is called dead while still alive, to protect Abram's name
11:32.body: Rashi says Terah lived on after Abram left. The verse reports his death first so that no one would say Abram abandoned his old father. It also calls the wicked 'dead' even while they live.

sources.quote: שלא יהא הדבר מפרסם לכל ויאמרו לא קים אברם את כבוד אביו, שהניחו זקן והלך לו, לפיכך קראו הכתוב מת
sources.says: Rashi says it was so that people would not say Abram failed to honour his father by leaving him old, so the verse called him dead.

sources.quote: שהרשעים אף בחייהם קרויים מתים
sources.says: Rashi says the wicked are called dead even while they live.

11:32.headline: חרן hints at חרון, burning anger, until Abram came
11:32.body: A bracketed note in Rashi says the nun in בחרן is turned over, as a hint that until Abram came, God's anger (חרון אף) was in the world.

sources.quote: בחרן הנו"ן הפוכה לומר לך, עד אברם חרון אף של מקום
sources.says: The bracketed note says the nun is reversed to tell you that until Abram there was burning anger from God.

12:3.headline: Blessers are plural, but the one who curses is singular
12:3.body: The verse says 'those who bless you' in the plural and 'the one who curses you' in the singular. Radak says this is because few will curse him.

sources.quote: מברכיך. רבים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מברכיך is plural.

sources.quote: ומקללך. יחיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ומקללך is singular.

sources.quote: בקללה לא אמר לשון רבים, כי מעטים יהיו המקללים אותו ומבקשי רעתו
sources.says: Radak says for the curse He did not use the plural, because few will curse him or seek his harm.

12:8.headline: ויעתק needs an object: Abram 'moved' his tent
12:8.body: The verse does not say what Abram moved. Rashi and Radak supply 'his tent'. Ibn Ezra says the verb takes an object, and the object is אהלה.

sources.quote: ויעתק משם. אהלו
sources.says: Rashi says that what he moved was his tent.

sources.quote: העתיק משם אהלו ללכת אל ההר
sources.says: Radak says he moved his tent from there to go to the mountain.

sources.quote: והפעול אהלה וגם הוא פעול ויט
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the object of the verb is אהלה, and that it is also the object of ויט.

12:8.headline: אהלה is spelled 'her tent': Abram pitched Sarai's tent first
12:8.body: The word is written אהלה, with a ה, which can read as 'her tent'. Rashi says this teaches that Abram first pitched his wife's tent and then his own.

sources.quote: אהלה כתיב, בתחלה נטה את אהל אשתו ואחר כך את שלו
sources.says: Rashi says it is written אהלה, and that he first pitched his wife's tent and then his own.

12:8.headline: 'Called in the name of the LORD': prayer, or teaching others?
12:8.body: Onkelos translates it as 'he prayed in the name of the LORD'. Ramban says it means he called out God's name aloud before the altar, to teach people about Him.

sources.quote: וצלי בשמא דיי
sources.says: Onkelos says he prayed in the name of the LORD.

sources.quote: והנכון שהיה קורא בקול גדול שם לפני המזבח את שם ה', מודיע אותו ואלהותו לבני אדם
sources.says: Ramban says the right sense is that he called aloud before the altar the name of the LORD, making Him and His divinity known to people.

12:9.headline: הנגבה means 'south', and the word is linked to 'dry'
12:9.body: Ibn Ezra says נגב means the south. He says the name comes from an Aramaic word for 'dry', because the south is so hot that things dry out.

sources.quote: ונקרא כן בלשון ארמית "נגיבו מיא" כי צד דרום הם, ומרוב החום ייבש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is called so in Aramaic, 'the waters dried', because it is the south side and from the great heat things dry.

12:10.headline: לגור means to stay a while, not to settle
12:10.body: Radak says Abram went down to Egypt to stay as a guest, not to settle. He meant to stay only until the famine in Canaan passed.

sources.quote: לא להשתקע שם, אלא לגור שם עד שיעבר הרעב
sources.says: Radak says not to settle there, but to stay there until the famine passed.

12:13.headline: 'It will go well with me': gifts, or just staying alive?
12:13.body: Rashi says ייטב means they will give him gifts. Radak says the only good Abram meant was that they would not kill him.

sources.quote: יתנו לי מתנות
sources.says: Rashi says they will give me gifts.

sources.quote: והטובה שלא יהרגו אותו, כי לא נתכון אברם שיעשו עמו טובה אחרת
sources.says: Radak says the good was that they would not kill him, since Abram did not mean any other kindness.

12:17.headline: 'על דבר שרי': because of Sarai, or at her word?
12:17.body: Ibn Ezra reads על דבר as 'because of'. Rashi reads it as 'at her word': she tells the angel 'strike' and he strikes.

sources.quote: כמו בעבור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like בעבור, 'because of'.

sources.quote: על פי דבורה; אומרת למלאך הך, והוא מכה
sources.says: Rashi says it is by her word: she tells the angel to strike and he strikes.

12:20.headline: 'He commanded about him' means to escort and guard him
12:20.body: Rashi says ויצו עליו means 'about him': to send him off and guard him. Radak says it was so the Egyptians would not touch his wife or anything of his.

sources.quote: על אודותיו, לשלחו ולשמרו
sources.says: Rashi says it means about him, to send him off and to guard him.

sources.quote: לשמרו ולשמר אשתו שלא יגעו בה המצרים ולא בכל אשר לו
sources.says: Radak says it was to guard him and his wife, so the Egyptians would not touch her or anything of his.

12:20.headline: וישלחו means they escorted him with honour, not just sent him off
12:20.body: Rashi follows the Aramaic translation, 'they escorted him'. Ibn Ezra says it is the way of escorting someone with honour, as when Abraham walked with the angels to send them off.

sources.quote: כתרגומו ואלויאו
sources.says: Rashi says it is as the Aramaic translation has it, 'they escorted him'.

sources.quote: דרך ליווי בכבוד, וכן ואברהם הולך עמם לשלחם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the way of escorting with honour, as in 'and Abraham went with them to send them off'.

13:2.headline: 'Abram was very heavy': loaded with baggage, as well as rich
13:2.body: Rashi says כבד means loaded down with burdens. Ibn Ezra says Abram had much baggage, so he moved slowly, and he links כבוד, 'honour', to the word for weight.

sources.quote: כבד מאד. טעון משאות
sources.says: Rashi says כבד מאד means loaded with burdens.

sources.quote: שיש לו כבודה רבה, ומי שיש לו כן תנועתו כבדה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he had much baggage, and whoever has that moves heavily.

sources.quote: הלא תראה כי כבוד מגזרת כובד אבן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says you can see that כבוד comes from the word in 'the weight of a stone'.

13:3.headline: 'He went on his journeys': Rashi finds good manners in the route
13:3.body: Rashi says Abram stayed at the same inns he used on the way down to Egypt, which teaches that a person should not change his lodging. Radak says it just means short stages, because his herds slowed him.

sources.quote: היה הולך ולן באכסניות שלן בהם בהליכתו למצרים, למדך דרך ארץ, שלא ישנה אדם מאכסניא שלו
sources.says: Rashi says he went and lodged at the inns where he had lodged on his way to Egypt, teaching that a person should not change from his inn.

sources.quote: מסע אחר מסע מעט, לפי שהיה כבד מאד במקנה
sources.says: Radak says it was one stage after another, a little at a time, because he was heavy with livestock.

13:5.headline: Lot's wealth is credited to two words: 'who walked with Abram'
13:5.body: Rashi asks what gave Lot his flocks and herds. His answer is the phrase itself: his walking with Abram. Radak says Lot had this good fortune because of Abram, since he went with him and listened to him.

sources.quote: מי גרם שהיה לו זאת? הליכתו עם אברם
sources.says: Rashi asks who caused him to have this, and answers: his going with Abram.

sources.quote: בזכות אברם היתה לו הטובה ההיא, לפי שהיה הולך אתו ונשמע אליו
sources.says: Radak says that good was his through Abram's merit, since he went with him and obeyed him.

13:6.headline: 'Could not bear them': Rashi fills in a missing word, 'pasture'
13:6.body: The verb is masculine, though the word for land is feminine. Rashi says the sentence is short and means that the pasture of the land could not bear them, which is why the verb is masculine. Radak says the word for land is sometimes used as masculine.

sources.quote: ולשון קצר הוא, וצריך להוסיף עליו, כמו ולא נשא אותם מרעה הארץ, לפיכך כתב ולא נשא בלשון זכר
sources.says: Rashi says it is a short expression and needs something added, 'the pasture of the land did not bear them', and so it is written with a masculine verb.

sources.quote: בא ארץ בלשון זכר
sources.says: Radak says the word for land is used here in the masculine.

13:7.headline: Rashi: the quarrel was about grazing in other people's fields
13:7.body: Rashi says Lot's herdsmen were wicked and let their animals graze in others' fields. Abram's herdsmen scolded them for stealing. They answered that the land was promised to Abram, and Lot was his heir.

sources.quote: לפי שהיו רועים של לוט רשעים ומרעים בהמתם בשדות אחרים, ורועי אברם מוכיחים אותם על הגזל
sources.says: Rashi says it was because Lot's herdsmen were wicked and grazed their animals in other people's fields, and Abram's herdsmen rebuked them for the theft.

sources.quote: והם אומרים נתנה הארץ לאברם, ולו אין יורש, ולוט יורשו
sources.says: Rashi says they answered that the land was given to Abram, who has no heir, and Lot is his heir.

13:8.headline: 'We are brothers': relatives, or men who look alike?
13:8.body: Rashi says אנשים אחים means relatives. A midrash he adds says they looked alike in the features of their faces.

sources.quote: אנשים אחים. קרובים, ומדרש אגדה דומין בקלסתר פנים
sources.says: Rashi says it means relatives, and a midrash says they were alike in the look of their faces.

13:9.headline: ואימנה and ואשמאילה are verbs made from 'right' and 'left'
13:9.body: Rashi says ואימנה means 'I will turn myself to the right', like ואשמאילה, 'I will turn myself to the left'. Ibn Ezra says it comes from the word for 'right'. Radak says that if Lot goes north, Abram will stay south.

sources.quote: אימין את עצמי, כמו ואשמאילה אשמאיל את עצמי
sources.says: Rashi says it means I will turn myself right, like 'I will turn myself left'.

sources.quote: ואימינה. מגזרת ימין
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ואימינה comes from the word for 'right'.

sources.quote: אם תרצה אתה ללכת לצפון הארץ אני אהיה לדרום הארץ
sources.says: Radak says if you want to go to the north of the land, I will be in the south of the land.

13:10.headline: ככר here means a plain, as the Aramaic translation has it
13:10.body: Rashi and Radak say ככר means a plain, following the Aramaic translation. Ibn Ezra says it means a place of plants.

sources.quote: ככר. מישור, כתרגומו
sources.says: Rashi says ככר means a plain, as the Aramaic translation has it.

sources.quote: ככר. כתרגומו מישור
sources.says: Radak says ככר means a plain, as the Aramaic translation has it.

sources.quote: ככר הירדן. מקום צמחים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ככר הירדן is a place of plants.

13:11.headline: 'Lot moved מקדם': east, west, or away from the Ancient One?
13:11.body: Rashi says Lot travelled from the east to the west. A midrash he also quotes hears קדם as 'the Ancient One of the world': Lot moved away from God. Radak says the מ means he went toward the east.

sources.quote: נמצא נוסע ממזרח למערב
sources.says: Rashi says it turns out he was travelling from east to west.

sources.quote: ומדרש אגדה הסיע עצמו מקדמונו של עולם; אמר אי אפשי לא באברם ולא באלהיו
sources.says: Rashi says a midrash has him move himself away from the Ancient One of the world, saying he wanted neither Abram nor his God.

sources.quote: כלפי מזרח מהמקום שהיה בו, כי הירדן מזרח לארץ כנען
sources.says: Radak says it means toward the east from where he was, since the Jordan is east of the land of Canaan.

13:13.headline: Sodom's men were 'wicked' and 'sinners': Rashi gives each word a meaning
13:13.body: Rashi says רעים means wicked with their bodies, and חטאים means sinning with their money. Ibn Ezra says רעים is wickedness toward people.

sources.quote: רעים. בגופם
sources.says: Rashi says רעים means in their bodies.

sources.quote: וחטאים. בממונם
sources.says: Rashi says וחטאים means in their money.

sources.quote: רעים. לבני אדם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says רעים means toward people.

13:15.headline: 'I will give': a gift made now, by God's word
13:15.body: Ibn Ezra says the giving is by speech. Radak says it means 'I give you from now', as a gift, even though the nations hold the land for the time being.

sources.quote: לך אתננה. בדבור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says לך אתננה means by speech.

sources.quote: לך אתננה מעתה כי היא מתנה לך, אף על פי שהיא ברשות הגוים
sources.says: Radak says I give it to you from now, for it is a gift to you, even though it is in the hands of the nations.

14:1.headline: Amraphel is Nimrod, whose name sounds like "he said, fall"
14:1.body: Rashi says Amraphel is Nimrod, who told Abraham to fall (פל) into the fiery furnace. Bereshit Rabbah hears אמר and אפלה, "what he said was dark".

sources.quote: הוּא נִמְרוֹד, שֶׁאָמַר לְאַבְרָהָם פֹּל לְתוֹךְ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says Amraphel is Nimrod, who told Abraham to fall into the fiery furnace.

sources.quote: אַמְרָפֶל, שֶׁהָיְתָה אֲמִירָתוֹ אֲפֵלָה
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says he was called Amraphel because his saying (amira) was dark (afela).

14:2.headline: King Bera's name is heard as "evil"
14:2.body: בֶּרַע sounds like רע, "evil". Rashi says he was evil to heaven and to people.

sources.quote: רַע לַשָּׁמַיִם וְרַע לַבְּרִיּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Bera was evil toward heaven and evil toward people.

sources.quote: בֶּרַע, שֶׁהָיָה בֵּן רַע
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Bera was a son of evil.

14:2.headline: King Birsha's name is heard as "wickedness"
14:2.body: בִּרְשַׁע sounds like רשע, "wickedness". Rashi says he rose high through wickedness.

sources.quote: שֶׁנִּתְעַלָּה בְרֶשַׁע
sources.says: Rashi says he was lifted up through wickedness.

sources.quote: בִּרְשַׁע, שֶׁהָיָה בֵּן רָשָׁע
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Birsha was a son of wickedness.

14:2.headline: King Shinav's name: hates his Father, or draws in money
14:2.body: Rashi hears שונא אב, "one who hates his Father in heaven". Bereshit Rabbah hears שואב, "one who draws in money".

sources.quote: שׂוֹנֵא אָבִיו שׁבַּשָּׁמָיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the name means one who hates his Father in heaven.

sources.quote: שִׁנְאָב, שֶׁהָיָה שׁוֹאֵב מָמוֹן
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Shinav was one who drew in money.

14:3.headline: The Valley of Siddim is named for its fields
14:3.body: Rashi says the valley got its name because it held many fields. Radak notes that Onkelos translates the word as fields (חקליא).

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיו בוֹ שָׂדוֹת הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says it was named because it had many fields.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ ״חַקְלַיָּא״
sources.says: Radak says Onkelos translates the word as fields.

14:5.headline: The Rephaim: so frightening that seeing them felt like dying
14:5.body: Ibn Ezra links the name to the word for the dead. He says whoever saw them would lose heart, as if dead. Radak simply calls them the giants (הענקים).

sources.quote: שכל הרואה אותם ימות לבו ויחשב מהרפאים שהם מתים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says anyone who saw them would feel his heart die, and counts them with the Rephaim, the dead.

sources.quote: הִכּוּ אֶת הָעֲנָקִים שֶׁהָיוּ בְּעַשְׁתְּרוֹת קַרְנַיִם
sources.says: Radak says they struck the giants who lived in Ashteroth-Karnaim.

14:7.headline: Amalek is named here before Amalek was born
14:7.body: Rashi says the field is named for what would come later, because Amalek was not yet born. Radak disagrees: by the time Moses wrote, Amalek had already been born.

sources.quote: עֲדַיִן לֹא נוֹלַד עֲמָלֵק, וְנִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הֶעָתִיד
sources.says: Rashi says Amalek was not yet born, and the place is named for the future.

sources.quote: כִּי כְּשֶׁכָּתַב מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ זֶה כְּבָר נוֹלַד עֲמָלֵק
sources.says: Radak says that when Moses wrote this, Amalek had already been born.

14:13.headline: The "survivor" who told Abraham is read as Og
14:13.body: Ibn Ezra says הפליט simply means one who fled and escaped. Rashi says it was Og, who escaped. Bereshit Rabbah says he was called Og because he found Abraham busy with cakes (עוגות).

sources.quote: ופי' הפליט שברח ונמלט מבני סדום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means one who fled and escaped from the people of Sodom.

sources.quote: זֶה עוֹג, שֶׁפָּלַט מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is Og, who escaped from the war.

sources.quote: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ עוֹג שֶׁבָּא וּמָצָא אֶת אַבְרָם יוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בְּמִצְוַת עוּגוֹת
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says he was called Og because he came and found Abraham busy with the commandment of cakes.

14:13.headline: Why is Abraham called "the Hebrew"?
14:13.body: Rashi says it means he came from across (עבר) the river. Radak says it means he descended from Ever. Bereshit Rabbah has a third view: the whole world was on one side (עבר) and he on the other.

sources.quote: שֶׁבָּא מֵעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר
sources.says: Rashi says it means he came from across the river.

sources.quote: מִבְּנֵי בְנֵי עֵבֶר
sources.says: Radak says it means he was among the grandsons of Ever.

sources.quote: כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ מֵעֵבֶר אֶחָד וְהוּא מֵעֵבֶר אֶחָד
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah has Rabbi Yehudah say that the whole world was on one side and Abraham was on the other.

14:14.headline: Abraham's "trained men": trained in faith, or in war?
14:14.body: חניכיו appears only here. Rashi says it means Eliezer, whom Abraham trained in the commandments. Radak says they were taught the way of truth. Ibn Ezra says they were trained many times in war.

sources.quote: זֶה אֱלִיעֶזֶר שֶׁחִנְּכוֹ לְמִצְוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says this is Eliezer, whom Abraham trained in the commandments.

sources.quote: שֶׁלִּמְּדָם בְּדֶרֶךְ הָאֱמֶת לַעֲבֹד אֶת
sources.says: Radak says these were the young men he taught the way of truth, to serve God.

sources.quote: שחנכם פעמים רבות במלחמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Abraham trained them many times in war.

14:14.headline: "Dan" is a name from the future, and Abraham's strength failed there
14:14.body: Rashi says Abraham grew weak at Dan because he saw his descendants would set up a calf there. Radak says Dan got its name later, from the tribe of Dan. Bereshit Rabbah says Dan is a name of idol worship.

sources.quote: שָׁם תָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחוֹ, שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁעֲתִידִין בָּנָיו לְהַעֲמִיד שָׁם עֵגֶל
sources.says: Rashi says his strength failed there because he saw his descendants would set up a calf there.

sources.quote: וּכְשֶׁכְּבָשׁוּהוּ בְּנֵי דָן קָרְאוּ לוֹ דָּן בְּשֵׁם דָּן אֲבִיהֶם
sources.says: Radak says that when the sons of Dan conquered the place they named it Dan, after their father.

sources.quote: וַיִּרְדֹּף עַד דָּן, שֵׁם עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים הִיא
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Dan is a name of idol worship.

14:15.headline: Chovah is a nickname for Dan, from the Hebrew for "guilt"
14:15.body: Rashi says there was no place named Chovah. He says Dan is called this because idol worship would be there.

sources.quote: אֵין מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ חוֹבָה, וְדָן קוֹרֵא חוֹבָה, עַל שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁעֲתִידָה לִהְיוֹת שָׁם
sources.says: Rashi says no place is named Chovah, and Dan is called Chovah because of the idol worship that would be there.

14:18.headline: Malki-Tzedek: "king of righteousness", or a place that makes people righteous
14:18.body: Ibn Ezra says he was called this because he was king of a place of righteousness (צדק). Bereshit Rabbah says the place makes its people righteous. Rashi says, citing a midrash, that he is Shem, son of Noah.

sources.quote: נקרא כן בעבור שהוא מלך על מקום צדק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he was called this because he was king over a place of righteousness.

sources.quote: הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה מַצְדִּיק אֶת יוֹשְׁבָיו
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says this place makes its inhabitants righteous.

sources.quote: הוּא שֵׁם בֶן נֹחַ
sources.says: Rashi, citing a midrash, says Malki-Tzedek is Shem, the son of Noah.

14:19.headline: Does "owner of heaven and earth" mean bought, or made?
14:19.body: Rashi says קונה means makes, because by making heaven and earth He acquired them. Radak says it does not mean buying from someone else. Ramban allows that the word for owning can also mean making.

sources.quote: עַל יְדֵי עֲשִׂיָּתָן קְנָאָן לִהְיוֹת שֶׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that by making them He acquired them as His own.

sources.quote: אֵינוֹ לְשׁוֹן קוֹנֶה מֵאַחֵר
sources.says: Radak says the word does not mean buying from someone else.

sources.quote: שֶׁיָּבֹא לְשׁוֹן קִנְיָן בְּעִנְיָן הָעֲשִׂיָּה
sources.says: Ramban says it may be that the word for owning is used for the idea of making.

14:20.headline: Here מגן is a verb meaning "handed over", not the noun "shield"
14:20.body: Rashi and Radak read מִגֵּן as "delivered", like אמגנך ישראל in Hosea. Ibn Ezra reads it as "gave". So God handed Abraham's enemies into his hand.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר הִסְגִּיר, וְכֵן אֲמַגֶּנְךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says it means who delivered up, like I will deliver you, Israel.

sources.quote: כמו נתן, וכן עטרת תפארת תמגנך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means gave, as in a crown of glory will it give you.

sources.quote: מְסָרָם בְּיָדֶיךָ
sources.says: Radak says it means He handed them over into your hands.

14:20.headline: Who gave the tenth: Abraham, or Malki-Tzedek?
14:20.body: The verse does not say who gave to whom. Rashi says Abraham gave a tenth to the priest. Radak's father read it the other way: Malki-Tzedek gave Abraham the tenth that was his by right.

sources.quote: אַבְרָהָם מעשר מכל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה כֹהֵן
sources.says: Rashi says Abraham gave a tenth of all he had, because Malki-Tzedek was a priest.

sources.quote: וַאֲדוֹנִי אָבִי זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה פֵּרַשׁ כִּי מַלְכִּי צֶדֶק נָתַן לְאַבְרָהָם בִּשְׂכָרוֹ הַמַּעֲשֵׂר מִן הַדִּין
sources.says: Radak says his father explained that Malki-Tzedek gave Abraham the tenth, as his rightful reward.

14:23.headline: In an oath, אם can mean "not"
14:23.body: Sforno says אם in Scripture, when no condition follows, stands for שלא, "that not". So Abraham says he will not take even a thread.

sources.quote: כָּל אִם שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא כְּשֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא אַחֲרָיו פֹּעַל תְּנַאי יִהְיֶה בִּמְקוֹם מִלַּת שֶׁלֹּא
sources.says: Sforno says every אם in Scripture with no condition after it stands for the word שלא, meaning that not.

14:24.headline: Abraham says "they ate", not "we ate", and Rashbam says why
14:24.body: Abraham says only the young men ate, not himself. Rashbam says this is true, because Abraham ate from Malki-Tzedek's food.

sources.quote: שאמר אכלו הנערים ולא אמר אכלנו, כי הוא אכל משל מלכי צדק
sources.says: Rashbam says Abraham said the young men ate, not we ate, because he himself ate from Malki-Tzedek's food.

15:1.headline: "After" with and without a yod: close by, or long after?
15:1.body: Rashi says אחר means right after, while אחרי means a longer time after. Bereshit Rabbah records the opposite rule from Rabbi Yudan.

sources.quote: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶאֱמַר אַחַר – סָמוּךְ, אַחֲרֵי – מֻפְלָג
sources.says: Rashi says that wherever it says אחר it means close, and אחרי means far.

sources.quote: רַבִּי יוּדָן אָמַר בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחֲרֵי, סָמוּךְ. אַחַר, מוּפְלָג
sources.says: Rabbi Yudan says the reverse: אחרי means close and אחר means far.

15:1.headline: God's "shield" protects Abraham from punishment, not only from kings
15:1.body: Ibn Ezra says the shield saved Abraham from the kings. Rashi, following Bereshit Rabbah, says it shields him from punishment for the lives he took in the war.

sources.quote: אָנֹכִי מָגֵן לָךְ, מִן הָעֹנֶשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא תֵּעָנֵשׁ עַל כָּל אוֹתָן נְפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהָרַגְתָּ
sources.says: Rashi says God is a shield from punishment, so Abraham will not be punished for all the people he killed.

sources.quote: אנכי הייתי מגן לך והצלתיך מיד המלכים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says God was a shield to him and saved him from the hand of the kings.

15:2.headline: בן משק ביתי: the man who runs Abraham's household
15:2.body: משק appears only here. Rashi says the whole house is fed at his word, so he is Abraham's steward. Radak says it means the one who goes in and out of the house.

sources.quote: שֶׁכָּל בֵּיתִי נִזּוֹן עַל פִּיו
sources.says: Rashi says my whole house is fed by his word.

sources.quote: הַיּוֹצֵא וְנִכְנָס בְּבֵיתִי
sources.says: Radak says the one who goes out and comes in at my house.

15:2.headline: Eliezer's "Damesek" is read as "he draws and gives drink"
15:2.body: Rashi says the Talmud reads דמשק as an acronym: דולה ומשקה, one who draws and gives others to drink from his master's Torah. Radak says it more simply means a man from Damascus.

sources.quote: וּבַתַּלְמוּד דָרְשׁוּ נוֹטָרִיקוֹן דּוֹלֶה וּמַשְׁקֶה מִתּוֹרַת רַבּוֹ לַאֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says the Talmud read the word as an acronym for one who draws and gives drink from his master's Torah to others.

sources.quote: אֶפְשָׁר כִּי חָסֵר יוֹ״ד הַיִּחוּס, רוֹצֶה לוֹמַר דַּמַּשְׂקִי
sources.says: Radak says the letter yod of origin may be missing, so it means a man of Damascus.

15:5.headline: "Outside": out of the tent, or up above the stars?
15:5.body: Rashi's plain reading is that Abraham was taken out of his tent to see the stars. The midrash reads הבט, "look down", to mean he was lifted above the stars.

sources.quote: הוֹצִיאוֹ מֵאָהֳלוֹ לַחוּץ לִרְאוֹת הַכּוֹכָבִים
sources.says: Rashi says that on the plain reading God took him out of his tent to see the stars.

sources.quote: הוֹצִיאוֹ מֵחֲלָלוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְהִגְבִּיהוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִן הַכּוֹכָבִים, וְזֶהוּ לְשׁוֹן הַבָּטָה מִלְּמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: God lifted him above the stars, and הבטה means looking from above to below.

sources.quote: הֶעֱלָה אוֹתוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִכִּפַּת הָרָקִיעַ
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah has Rabbi Yehudah say God raised him above the dome of the sky.

15:8.headline: "How will I know?": a request for a sign, or for merit?
15:8.body: Rashi first says Abraham asked for a sign that he would inherit the land. Rashi then gives another reading, where he asked by what merit his children would keep it. Sforno says he feared his children might sin.

sources.quote: אֲבָל עַל יְרֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ שָׁאַל לוֹ אוֹת וְאָמַר לוֹ בַּמָּה אֵדַע
sources.says: Rashi says Abraham asked for a sign about inheriting the land, and said: how will I know?

sources.quote: לֹא שָׁאַל לוֹ אוֹת אֶלָּא אָמַר לְפָנָיו, הוֹדִיעֵנִי בְּאֵיזֶה זְכוּת יִתְקַיְּמוּ בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: he did not ask for a sign but asked by what merit they would keep the land.

sources.quote: כִּי אוּלַי יֶחֶטְאוּ הַבָּנִים וְלֹא יִזְכּוּ לִירַשׁ
sources.says: Sforno says he asked because the children might sin and not earn the inheritance.

15:10.headline: ויבתר: he cut them in two, as in a covenant ceremony
15:10.body: Ibn Ezra says it means he cut them and set the halves apart. Rashi says this is how a covenant was made: the two sides pass between the halves of the animal.

sources.quote: חתכם והפרידם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he cut them and separated them.

sources.quote: וְדֶרֶך כּוֹרְתֵי בְרִית לְחַלֵּק בְּהֵמָה וְלַעֲבֹר בֵּין בְּתָרֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the way of those making a covenant to split an animal and pass between its pieces.

15:11.headline: The bird of prey is named for how it swoops
15:11.body: Rashi says העיט is named for what it does, because it swoops (עט) and longs for carcasses. Radak says it is a general name for birds of prey.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהוּא עָט וְשׁוֹאֵף אֶל הַנְּבֵלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it is named for swooping and longing for carcasses.

sources.quote: הָעַיִט הוּא שֵׁם לָעוֹפוֹת הַדּוֹרְסִים
sources.says: Radak says העיט is a name for birds that tear their prey.

15:11.headline: Not "sat": Abraham blew the birds away
15:11.body: וישב here is from the root for blowing, not from ישב. Rashi says it means blowing and scattering, as in ישב רוחו. Ibn Ezra also allows that it means he put the carcasses back to keep the bird away.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן נְשִׁיבָה וְהַפְרָחָה, כְּמוֹ יַשֵּׁב רוּחוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of blowing and scattering, like he makes His wind blow.

sources.quote: או השיב הפגרים להבריח העיט
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says another reading is that he put the carcasses back to drive off the bird.

sources.quote: וְאַפְרַח יָתְהוֹן אַבְרָם
sources.says: Onkelos translates: and Abraham drove them off.

15:12.headline: A deep sleep: ordinary sleep, prophecy, or a stupor?
15:12.body: Bereshit Rabbah lists three kinds of תרדמה: sleep, prophecy and a stupor. Radak says this one came from the force of prophecy.

sources.quote: שְׁלשָׁה תַּרְדֵּמוֹת הֵן, תַּרְדֵּמַת שֵׁנָה, וְתַרְדֵּמַת נְבוּאָה, וְתַרְדֵּמַת מַרְמִיטָה
sources.says: Rav says there are three kinds of תרדמה: of sleep, of prophecy, and a stupor.

sources.quote: מִכֹּחַ הַנְּבוּאָה בָּאָה הַתַּרְדֵּמָה
sources.says: Radak says the deep sleep came from the force of prophecy.

15:13.headline: The 400 years are counted from Isaac's birth, not from Egypt
15:13.body: Rashi counts four hundred years from the birth of Isaac to the Exodus. Radak also counts from the day Abraham has a child. Ibn Ezra counts from the day of the vision.

sources.quote: מִשֶּׁנּוֹלַד יִצְחָק עַד שֶׁיָּצְאוּ יִשְֹרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is four hundred years from Isaac's birth until Israel left Egypt.

sources.quote: עַד תַּשְׁלוּם אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת, מִיּוֹם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ זֶרַע
sources.says: Radak says until four hundred years are complete, from the day he has a child.

sources.quote: עד סוף זה הקץ מהיום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it runs to the end of this term, from today.

15:15.headline: A "good old age": Ishmael repents, Esau not yet wicked
15:15.body: Rashi says the promise means Ishmael would repent in Abraham's days and Esau would not turn wicked yet. Radak reads a good old age more simply, as living to see children and grandchildren.

sources.quote: בִּשְּׂרוֹ שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה יִשְׁמָעֵאל תְּשׁוּבָה בְּיָמָיו, וְלֹא יֵצֵא עֵשָׂו לְתַרְבּוּת רָעָה בְּיָמָיו
sources.says: Rashi says God told him Ishmael would repent in his days and Esau would not go bad in his days.

sources.quote: שֶׁתִּרְאֶה לְךָ בָּנִים וּבְנֵי בָנִים
sources.says: Radak says it means that you will see children and grandchildren.

15:16.headline: Why does the Torah name the Amorites alone?
15:16.body: Ibn Ezra says the Amorites are named because they were the strongest of the nations. He adds that someone who derives the name from the root "to say" has said nothing.

sources.quote: והזכיר האמורי בעבור תקפו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Amorite is named because of his strength.

sources.quote: והמפרש האמורי מגזרת אומר לא אמר כלום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says whoever derives Amorite from the word for saying has said nothing.

15:17.headline: The accent shows the sun "had set", not "was setting"
15:17.body: Rashi and Radak say the stress on באה falls on the upper syllable, which makes it past tense. So the sun had already set. Ibn Ezra notes that earlier the verse said it was only about to set.

sources.quote: טַעֲמוֹ לְמַעְלָה, לְכָךְ הוּא מְבֹאָר שֶׁבָּא כְבָר
sources.says: Rashi says its accent is on the upper syllable, so it is clear it had already come.

sources.quote: מִלְעֵיל, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא פֹּעַל עָבָר
sources.says: Radak says the stress is on the first syllable because it is a past-tense verb.

sources.quote: בתחלה עודנה לא באה, וכן כתוב לבוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says at first it had not yet come, as it says earlier that it was about to come.

15:18.headline: "Cut a covenant": the covenant was sealed between cut animals
15:18.body: A covenant is called "cut" because of the cut animals. Ibn Ezra says passing between the pieces is the oath. Radak says it is the way covenant partners did it.

sources.quote: וזאת היא השבועה וכן העגל אשר כרתו לשנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this is the oath, as in the calf they cut in two.

sources.quote: רָמַז בּוֹ לִכְרִיתַת הַבְּרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁעוֹבְרִים בַּעֲלֵי הַבְּרִית בֵּין הַגְּזָרִים וְהַבְּתָרִים
sources.says: Radak says it hints at the cutting of the covenant, as covenant partners pass between the pieces.

15:18.headline: "I have given" speaks of a future gift in the past tense
15:18.body: The land is still to be received, but God says נתתי, "I have given". Rashi says God's word counts as if it were already done. Radak says the same: it is already given by His word.

sources.quote: כְּאִלוּ הִיא עֲשׂוּיָה
sources.says: Rashi says God's saying is as if it were already done.

sources.quote: כְּבָר נָתַתִּי לָהֶם בִּדְבָרִי שֶׁהוּא קַיָּם
sources.says: Radak says I have already given it to them by my word, which stands.

15:20.headline: The Rephaim stand in for a nation the list leaves out
15:20.body: Rashi says the Rephaim are the land of Og. Bereshit Rabbah and Radak notice that the Hivites are missing from the list, and the Rephaim may take their place.

sources.quote: אֶרֶץ עוֹג, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says the Rephaim are the land of Og, of which it is said that it is called the land of Rephaim.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַזְכִּיר כָּאן הַחִוִּי, לְפִיכָךְ הוּא מֵבִיא רְפָאִים תַּחְתֵּיהֶם
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says that since the Hivite is not named here, it brings the Rephaim in their place.

sources.quote: וְלֹא זָכַר הַחִוִּי, אוּלַי הוּא הָרְפָאִים שֶׁזָּכַר
sources.says: Radak says he did not name the Hivite, and perhaps he is the Rephaim that are named.

16:2.headline: "I will be built" plays on the word for son
16:2.body: Ibn Ezra and Radak link אבנה to בן, "son", because a son builds up the household. Rashi says a person with no children is not built up but in ruins.

sources.quote: אולי אבנה. מגזרת בן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אבנה comes from the word for son.

sources.quote: הַבֵּן נִקְרָא בֵּן, לְפִי שֶׁהוּא בִּנְיַן הָאָב וְהָאֵם
sources.says: Radak says a son is called בן because he is the building of the father and mother.

sources.quote: לִמֵּד עַל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּנִים שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָנוּי אֶלָּא הָרוּס
sources.says: Rashi says this teaches that a person without children is not built up but ruined.

16:2.headline: Abraham "listened to her voice": why not just "did as she said"?
16:2.body: Rashi says Abraham heard the holy spirit in Sarai's voice. Ramban says the verse stresses listening, because Abraham longed for children but still would not act without Sarai's permission.

sources.quote: לְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁבָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says he listened to the holy spirit that was in her.

sources.quote: אֲבָל אָמַר כִּי שָׁמַע לְקוֹל שָׂרַי, יִרְמֹז כִּי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאַבְרָם מִתְאַוֶּה מְאֹד לְבָנִים, לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן בְּלֹא רְשׁוּת שָׂרַי
sources.says: Ramban says the verse hints that, though Abraham longed for children, he did not do this without Sarai's permission.

16:3.headline: Sarai "took" Hagar: with words, not by force
16:3.body: Rashi and Bereshit Rabbah say the verb "took" means she won Hagar over with words. She told Hagar how fortunate she was to be joined to such a holy person.

sources.quote: לְקָחַתָּהּ בִּדְבָרִים, אַשְׁרַיִךְ שֶׁזָּכִית לִדָּבֵק בְּגוּף קָדוֹשׁ כָּזֶה
sources.says: Rashi says she took her with words: how fortunate you are to be joined to such a holy body.

sources.quote: לְקָחַתָּהּ בִּדְבָרִים, אָמְרָה לָהּ אַשְׁרַיִךְ
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says she took her with words and told her how fortunate she was.

16:5.headline: "My wrong is on you": wrong done to Sarai, or by Abraham?
16:5.body: Rashi says the wrong done to Sarai is Abraham's to answer for. Sforno says Abraham should have scolded Hagar. Bereshit Rabbah has Rabbi Yudan say Abraham wrongs Sarai himself, by staying silent when she is insulted.

sources.quote: חָמָס הֶעָשׂוּי לִי, עָלֶיךָ אֲנִי מֵטִיל הָעֹנֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says: the wrong done to me, I place the blame for it on you.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה עָלֶיךָ לִגְעוֹר בָּהּ
sources.says: Sforno says it was on Abraham to rebuke Hagar.

sources.quote: חוֹמְסֵנִי אַתָּה בִּדְבָרִים, לָמָּה, שֶׁאַתָּה שׁוֹמֵעַ בִּקְלוֹנִי וְשׁוֹתֵק
sources.says: Rabbi Yudan says: you wrong me with words, because you hear my disgrace and stay silent.

16:6.headline: "Sarai afflicted her": harsh work, a lesson, or a sin?
16:6.body: Rashi says Sarai made Hagar work hard. Sforno says it was so Hagar would remember she was a servant. Ramban says Sarah sinned by this affliction, and so did Abraham by letting it happen.

sources.quote: הָיְתָה מְשַׁעְבֶּדֶת בָּהּ בְּקֹשִׁי
sources.says: Rashi says she kept her in harsh bondage.

sources.quote: כְּדֵי שֶׁתַּכִּיר שֶׁהִיא מְשֻׁעְבֶּדֶת וְלֹא תְּבַזֶּה עוֹד אֶת גְּבִרְתָּהּ
sources.says: Sforno says it was so Hagar would see she was bound to Sarai and stop despising her mistress.

sources.quote: חָטְאָה אִמֵּנוּ בָּעִנּוּי הַזֶּה, וְגַם אַבְרָהָם בְּהַנִּיחוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
sources.says: Ramban says our mother sinned in this affliction, and Abraham also, by letting her do it.

16:11.headline: "You are pregnant": news she already knew, or a new pregnancy?
16:11.body: Hagar was already pregnant. Radak says the angel said it only to start the conversation. Rashi, following Bereshit Rabbah, says it means she would conceive again after losing the first child.

sources.quote: אָמַר לָהּ זֶה לִפְתִיחַת הַדְּבָרִים, כִּי כְּבָר יָדְעָה הִיא כִּי הָרָה
sources.says: Radak says he told her this to open the conversation, since she already knew she was pregnant.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁתָּשׁוּבִי תַּהֲרִי, כְּמוֹ הִנָּךְ הָרָה דְאֵשֶׁת מָנוֹחַ
sources.says: Rashi says it means: when you return you will conceive, as in the words to Manoah's wife.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִפִּילָה הֵרָיוֹן הָרִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says this teaches that she lost the first pregnancy.

16:15.headline: Who named Ishmael: the angel told Hagar, so how did Abraham know?
16:15.body: Rashi says Abraham had not heard the angel, but the holy spirit rested on him and he named the child Ishmael. Radak says Hagar told Abraham. Ramban says the angel told Hagar to name him.

sources.quote: שָׁרְתָה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ עָלָיו וּקְרָאוֹ יִשְׁמָעֵאל
sources.says: Rashi says the holy spirit rested on him and he named him Ishmael.

sources.quote: אָמְרָה הִיא לְאַבְרָהָם; וְהִיא קָרְאָה אוֹתוֹ יִשְׁמָעֵאל
sources.says: Radak says she told Abraham, and she named him Ishmael.

sources.quote: וְהַנָּכוֹן בְּעֵינַי כִּי הַמַּלְאָךְ צִוָּה לְהָגָר שֶׁתִּקְרָאֶנּוּ כֵן
sources.says: Ramban says the correct reading, to him, is that the angel commanded Hagar to call him this.

16:12.headline: "His hand is in everything": a robber, a merchant, or a dog?
16:12.body: Rashi says it means a bandit whom everyone hates and fights. Bekhor Shor says he buys goods everywhere and all buy from him. Bereshit Rabbah reads ויד כל בו as כלבו, "his dog", saying he and a dog are alike.

sources.quote: ידו בכל. לִסְטִים
sources.says: Rashi says ידו בכל means a bandit.

sources.quote: הַכֹּל שׂוֹנְאִין אוֹתוֹ וּמִתְגָּרִין בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says everyone hates him and fights with him.

sources.quote: שיקנה סחורה מכל המקומות ומוליך ממקום למקום והכל קונין ממנו
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says he buys goods from all places, carries them from place to place, and everyone buys from him.

sources.quote: קְרִי בֵיהּ כָּלְבּוֹ, הוּא וְהַכֶּלֶב שָׁוִים
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says to read it as כלבו, his dog, and that he and the dog are alike.

16:13.headline: "El Roi": the God who sees me, or the God of seeing?
16:13.body: Radak reads רֳאִי as "sees me". Rashi reads it as the God of seeing, who sees the pain of the downtrodden. Onkelos has "the God who sees all".

sources.quote: רֳאִי. רוֹאֶה אוֹתִי
sources.says: Radak says רֳאִי means sees me.

sources.quote: אֱלוֹהַּ הָרְאִיָּה, שֶׁרוֹאֶה בְעֶלְבּוֹן שֶׁל עֲלוּבִין
sources.says: Rashi says it is the God of seeing, who sees the insult of the downtrodden.

sources.quote: אֱלָהָא דְחָזֵי כֹלָּא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: God who sees all.

16:13.headline: A hard verse: "Have I even seen here after seeing?"
16:13.body: Ibn Ezra says הלם means "here". Bekhor Shor says it means "onward". Rashi reads the verse as Hagar's surprise that she saw an angel even here in the wilderness, after seeing angels in Abraham's house.

sources.quote: והנכון שהוא כמו פה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is that הלום means here.

sources.quote: הלום כמו הלאה
sources.says: Bekhor Shor says הלום is like הלאה, further.

sources.quote: וְכִי סְבוּרָה הָיִיתִי שֶׁאַף הֲלוֹם בַּמִּדְבָּרוֹת רָאִיתִי שְׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם אַחֲרֵי רֹאִי אוֹתָם בְּבֵיתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם
sources.says: Rashi reads it as a question of surprise: could I have thought I would see God's messenger here in the wilderness, after seeing them in Abraham's house?

17:14.headline: "Cut off": an early death, childlessness, or loss of his name?
17:14.body: Rashi says it means he goes childless and dies before his time. Ibn Ezra says some explain it as his name being cut off when his offspring die.

sources.quote: הוֹלֵךְ עֲרִירִי וּמֵת קֹדֶם זְמַנּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he goes childless and dies before his time.

sources.quote: כי כרת שיכרת שמו במות זרעו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says another view is that kareth means his name is cut off when his offspring die.

17:16.headline: Sarah is blessed twice: with youth, and then with milk
17:16.body: Rashi says the first blessing was that she was young again, and the second was that she could nurse. Sforno says the second blessing covers pregnancy, birth and raising the child without pain, undoing the curse on Eve.

sources.quote: שֶׁחָזְרָה לְנַעֲרוּתָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says the first blessing is that she returned to her youth.

sources.quote: בַּהֲנָקַת שָׁדַיִם כְּשֶׁנִּצְרְכָה לְכָךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the second blessing is nursing, when she needed it.

sources.quote: בַּהֵרָיוֹן וּבַלֵּידָה וּבְגִדּוּל הַבֵּן שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר, הֵפֶךְ קִלְלַת חַוָּה
sources.says: Sforno says it means in pregnancy, birth and raising the son without pain, the opposite of Eve's curse.

17:18.headline: "If only Ishmael": a wish, an "if", or "enough"?
17:18.body: Rashi reads לו as a wish: if only Ishmael would live. Ramban reads it as "if", with Abraham saying he would be content if Ishmael lives. Radak reads it as "it is enough what You gave me".

sources.quote: הַלְוַאי שֶׁיִּחְיֶה יִשְׁמָעֵאל
sources.says: Rashi says: would that Ishmael live.

sources.quote: וְאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אִם יִשְׁמָעֵאל יִחְיֶה לְפָנֶיךָ אֶרְצֶה בַּבְּרָכָה הַזֹּאת
sources.says: Ramban says Abraham said that if Ishmael lives before You, he would be content with this blessing.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹמַר דַּי בְּמַה שֶּׁנָּתַתָּ לִי, וְהוּא יִחְיֶה
sources.says: Radak says it means that what You have given me is enough, and may he live.

17:22.headline: "God went up from Abraham": a gentle phrase with a hint
17:22.body: Rashi says ויעל is a delicate way to speak of God. He adds that the righteous are God's chariot, since God "goes up" from them. The Guide says "going up" for God means the withdrawal of the divine presence, and lists this verse as an example.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן נְקִיָּה הוּא כְּלַפֵּי שְׁכִינָה, וְלָמַדְנוּ שֶׁהַצַּדִּיקִים מֶרְכַּבְתּוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
sources.says: Rashi says it is a clean expression for the divine presence, and we learn that the righteous are God's chariot.

sources.quote: וְאִסְתַּלַּק יְקָרָא דַיְיָ מֵעִלָּווֹהִי דְּאַבְרָהָם
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as: the glory of the Lord went up from above Abraham.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10:4
sources.quote: ואת הסתלקותו של מצב הנבואה מן האדם או סילוק השכינה
sources.says: The Guide says "going up" is said of the departure of the prophetic state from a person, or the removal of the divine presence.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10:8
sources.quote: וַיַּעַל אֱלֹהִים מֵעַל אַבְרָהָם
sources.says: The Guide lists this verse among its examples of the sense of revelation and glory.

18:1.headline: "In the heat of the day": why mention the time?
18:1.body: Rashi says God took the sun out of its sheath so Abraham would not be troubled with guests. Rashbam says it explains why Abraham did not invite them to stay the night. Radak says Abraham was dozing in the heat.

sources.quote: חַמָּה מִנַּרְתִּיקָהּ, שֶׁלֹּא לְהַטְרִיחוֹ בְּאוֹרְחִים
sources.says: Rashi says God took the sun out of its sheath so as not to trouble him with guests.

sources.quote: אבל אברהם לפי שבאו אליו כחם היום בבקר, שאין דרך אורחים ללון אלא לאכול ולעבור
sources.says: Rashbam says Abraham's guests came in the heat of the morning, and travelers do not stay the night then but eat and pass on.

sources.quote: נִרְדָּם הָיָה לַחֲמִימוּת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ
sources.says: Radak says he had fallen asleep because of the heat of the sun.

18:5.headline: "Your heart" is spelled short: angels have no evil impulse
18:5.body: Rashi, citing the midrash, says the verse says לבכם, not לבבכם. The short spelling has only one ב, with no double heart. This teaches that the evil impulse has no power over angels.

sources.quote: לְבַבְכֶם אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן אֶלָּא לִבְּכֶם, מַגִּיד שֶׁאֵין יֵצֶר הָרַע שׁוֹלֵט בַּמַּלְאָכִים
sources.says: Rashi says it does not say לבבכם but לבכם, which tells that the evil impulse does not rule over angels.

18:7.headline: "The boy" is Ishmael, being trained in the commandments
18:7.body: Rashi says the boy Abraham gave the calf to is Ishmael. Abraham was training him to do commandments.

sources.quote: זֶה יִשְׁמָעֵאל, לְחַנְּכוֹ בְּמִצְוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says this is Ishmael, to train him in commandments.

18:12.headline: Sarah laughed "in her inside", or "among her relatives"
18:12.body: Rashi says she looked at her own insides and wondered whether they could carry a child. Ibn Ezra says it means in her own mind. Bereshit Rabbah says one of the changes made for King Ptolemy was to write it as among her relatives.

sources.quote: מִסְתַּכֶּלֶת בְּמֵעֶיהָ וְאָמְרָה אֶפְשַׁר הַקְּרָבַיִם הַלָּלוּ טְעוּנִין וָלָד
sources.says: Rashi says she looked at her insides and said: can these organs carry a child?

sources.quote: וטעם בקרבה בנפשה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בקרבה means in her mind.

sources.quote: זֶה אֶחָד מִן הַדְּבָרִים שֶׁשִּׁנּוּ לְתַלְמַי הַמֶּלֶךְ, וַתִּצְחָק שָׂרָה בִּקְרוֹבֶיהָ לֵאמֹר
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says this is one of the things that were changed for King Ptolemy: Sarah laughed among her relatives.

18:13.headline: God repeats Sarah's words, but changes them for peace
18:13.body: Sarah said "my lord is old". God says to Abraham that she said "I am old". Rashi and Bereshit Rabbah say the verse changed her words to keep peace between husband and wife.

sources.quote: שִׁנָּה הַכָּתוּב מִפְּנֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁהֲרֵי הִיא אָמְרָה וַאדֹנִי זָקֵן
sources.says: Rashi says Scripture changed it for the sake of peace, since she had said and my lord is old.

sources.quote: גָּדוֹל הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאַף הַכְּתוּבִים דִּבְּרוּ בַּדָּאִית בִּשְׁבִיל לְהַטִּיל שָׁלוֹם בֵּין אַבְרָהָם לְשָׂרָה
sources.says: Bar Kappara says peace is great, since even Scripture spoke something untrue to put peace between Abraham and Sarah.

sources.quote: וּדְבָרָיו אֱמֶת אַךְ מִפְּנֵי הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא רָצָה לְגַלּוֹת מָה שֶׁאָמְרָה
sources.says: Ramban says the angel's words are true, but for the sake of peace he did not want to reveal what she said.

18:16.headline: "They looked down": a look that, in Scripture, usually means trouble
18:16.body: Rashi says every use of השקפה in Scripture is for harm, except "look down from Your holy dwelling". The look toward Sodom is then a bad sign. Radak notes the root can be active or passive.

sources.quote: כָּל הַשְׁקָפָה שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְרָעָה חוּץ מֵהַשְׁקִיפָה מִמְּעוֹן קָדְשְׁךָ
sources.says: Rashi says every looking down in Scripture is for evil, except Look down from Your holy dwelling.

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן הַשְׁקָפָה יָבוֹא פְּעָמִים בִּלְשׁוֹן הִפְעִיל וּפְעָמִים בִּלְשׁוֹן נִפְעַל
sources.says: Radak says the word for looking down sometimes comes in the active form and sometimes in the passive form.

18:18.headline: "Will be blessed through him", or "will bless themselves by him"?
18:18.body: Ibn Ezra says ונברכו is passive: they will be blessed because of him. The other form, והתברכו (Genesis 22:18), means they will bless themselves by him. Onkelos also says "through him".

sources.quote: וטעמו שיהיו מבורכים בשבילו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the sense is that they will be blessed on his account.

sources.quote: ומלת והתברכו (בראשית כב יח) איננה כן, רק הם מתברכים בו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word והתברכו is not so, they bless themselves by him.

sources.quote: וְיִתְבָּרְכוּן בְּדִילֵיהּ כֹּל עַמְמֵי אַרְעָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates: all the nations of the earth will be blessed for his sake.

18:19.headline: "I have known him": love, or foreknowledge?
18:19.body: Rashi says ידעתיו is a word of affection, like "known to her husband". If it only meant "I know", the word "in order that" would not fit. Onkelos translates it as "it is known before Me".

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן חִבָּה, כְּמוֹ מוֹדָע לְאִישָׁהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of affection, like known to her husband.

sources.quote: אֵין לְמַעַן נוֹפֵל עַל הַלָּשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says that if you read it as I know, the word in order that does not fit the sentence.

sources.quote: אֲרֵי גְלִי קֳדָמַי
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as: because it is known before Me.

sources.quote: וְהַנָּכוֹן בְּעֵינַי שֶׁהִיא יְדִיעָה בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
sources.says: Ramban says the correct reading, to him, is that it is real knowledge of him.

18:21.headline: "I will go down": God does not move, so what is meant?
18:21.body: The Guide says "going down" for God means bringing punishment on the lowly world. Rashi says it teaches judges not to decide a capital case without seeing it. Radak says the same, that people should not rush to judge.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 10:7
sources.quote: והעניין בכללו: החלת העונש על אנשי העולם השפל
sources.says: The Guide says the meaning in general is applying punishment to the people of the lower world.

sources.quote: לִמֵּד לַדַּיָּנִים שֶׁלֹא יִפְסְקוּ דִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת אֶלָּא בִרְאִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says this taught judges not to decide capital cases except by seeing.

sources.quote: נִכְתַּב זֶה לְלַמֵּד לִבְנֵי אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא יְמַהֲרוּ בְּמִשְׁפָּטָם
sources.says: Radak says this was written to teach people not to hurry in their judgments.

18:23.headline: "Will You also destroy?" or "in anger will You destroy?"
18:23.body: Rashi reads האף as "will You also". Onkelos translates it as anger. Ramban says God's אף, His anger, is His measure of strict justice.

sources.quote: האף תספה. הֲגַם תִּסְפֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says it means: will You also sweep away?

sources.quote: הֲבִרְגַז תְּשֵׁיצֵי זַכָּאָה עִם חַיָּבָא
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as: in anger will You destroy the innocent with the guilty?

sources.quote: אַפּוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא הִיא מִדַּת דִּינוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says God's anger is His measure of strict judgment.

18:25.headline: "Far be it from You" is read as "profane for You"
18:25.body: Rashi hears חולין, "profane", in חלילה: it would be an unholy act for God. Bereshit Rabbah notes the word is said twice, since the act would profane God's name. Ibn Ezra says it means something that cannot be.

sources.quote: חֻלִּין הוּא לְךָ, יֹאמְרוּ כָךְ הוּא אֻמָּנוּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is profane for You, they would say this is his craft.

sources.quote: חָלִלָה חָלִלָה שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים, חִלּוּל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם יֵשׁ בַּדָּבָר
sources.says: Rabbi Acha says חלילה is said twice, since there is a profaning of God's name in this thing.

sources.quote: חלילה. דבר שלא יתכן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says חלילה is something that cannot be.

18:27.headline: "I have taken it upon myself": wished, or began?
18:27.body: Rashi says הואלתי means "I wished", like ויואל משה. Ibn Ezra says it does not mean "I began", but "I wanted".

sources.quote: רָצִיתִי כְּמוֹ וַיּוֹאֶל מֹשֶׁה
sources.says: Rashi says it means I wished, like Moses was willing.

sources.quote: ואין מלת הואלתי כמו החילותי רק פי' רציתי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הואלתי does not mean I began, but I wished.

18:27.headline: "Dust and ashes": the two dangers Abraham was saved from
18:27.body: Rashi and Bereshit Rabbah read dust and ashes as two rescues: Abraham would have been dust if the kings had killed him, and ashes if Nimrod had burned him. Ibn Ezra reads it as the body's origin and end.

sources.quote: וּכְבָר הָיִיתִי רָאוּי לִהְיוֹת עָפָר עַל יְדֵי הַמְּלָכִים, וְאֵפֶר עַל יְדֵי נִמְרוֹד
sources.says: Rashi says I was already due to be dust through the kings, and ashes through Nimrod.

sources.quote: אִלּוּ הֲרָגַנִי אַמְרָפֶל לֹא הָיִיתִי עָפָר, וְאִי שְׂרָפַנִּי נִמְרוֹד לֹא הָיִיתִי אֵפֶר
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah has Abraham say that had Amraphel killed me I would not be dust, and had Nimrod burned me I would not be ashes.

sources.quote: כי עפר הייתי ואפר אשוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says: I was dust and to ash I will return.

18:33.headline: God left once Abraham fell silent: a judge waits for the defender
18:33.body: Rashi says that once the defender fell silent, the judge went away. Bereshit Rabbah says that a judge waits as long as the defender is speaking.

sources.quote: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּתֵּק הַסָּנֵגוֹר הָלַךְ לוֹ הַדַּיָּן
sources.says: Rashi says that when the defender fell silent, the judge went away.

sources.quote: הַדַּיָּן הַזֶּה כָּל זְמַן שֶׁהַסָּנֵיגוֹר מְלַמֵּד הוּא מַמְתִּין
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says this judge waits as long as the defender is arguing.

19:1.headline: Lot was "sitting" at the gate: sitting as a judge
19:1.body: The word is spelled ישב, "he sat". Rashi says that on that very day the people of Sodom had appointed Lot a judge.

sources.quote: ישב כְּתִיב, אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מִנּוּהוּ שׁוֹפֵט עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it is written ישב: that day they appointed him a judge over them.

19:2.headline: "Turn aside" hints at a secret, winding route
19:2.body: Rashi says Lot meant: take a winding path to my house, so the people of Sodom will not see you go in. Ibn Ezra says סור followed by אל means turning from where one is to go toward the one who calls.

sources.quote: עַקְּמוּ אֶת הַדֶּרֶךְ לְבֵיתִי דֶרֶךְ עֲקַלָּתוֹן שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּירוּ שֶׁאַתֶּם נִכְנָסִין שָׁם
sources.says: Rashi says: bend the road to my house by a winding way, so they will not see you go in there.

sources.quote: ואם אחריה אל"ף הפתוח בפתח קטן טעמה שיסור ממקומו וילך אל הקורא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says that when סור is followed by אל it means he leaves his place and goes to the one who calls.

19:3.headline: Unleavened bread: was it Passover, or just quick baking?
19:3.body: Rashi says it was Passover. Radak says Lot baked matzot because there was no time to wait for dough to rise.

sources.quote: ומצות אפה. פֶּסַח הָיָה
sources.says: Rashi says it was Passover.

sources.quote: וְאָפָה לָהֶם מַצּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא יַמְתִּינוּ עַד שֶׁיִּתְחַמֵּץ הַבָּצֵק
sources.says: Radak says he baked matzot for them so that they would not wait for the dough to become leavened.

19:8.headline: "The shadow of my roof-beam" means "my protection"
19:8.body: קורה is a roof-beam, so "under my beam" means under my roof. Rashi says Onkelos translates it with the Aramaic word שרותא. Ramban says Lot worked hard to protect guests who had come under his roof.

sources.quote: תַּרְגּוּם בִּטְלַל שָׁרוּתֵי, תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁל קוֹרָה – שָׁרוּתָא
sources.says: Rashi says Onkelos translates it as בטלל שרותי, and that the Aramaic for beam is שרותא.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה טוֹרֵחַ מְאֹד עַל אַכְסַנְיָא שֶׁלּוֹ לְהַצִּיל אוֹתָם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבָּאוּ בְּצֵל קוֹרָתוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says he labored greatly for his guests, to save them since they had come under his roof.

19:8.headline: האל here means "these", not "God"
19:8.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra read האל as האלה, "these". Ibn Ezra mentions a Gaon who said it was because the third man had not come, and calls that far-fetched.

sources.quote: האל. כְּמוֹ הָאֵלֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says האל is like האלה, these.

sources.quote: ויאמר הגאון, כי בעבור השלישי שלא בא אמר כן וזה הטעם רחוק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the Gaon's view that he said it because the third did not come, and says this reason is far-fetched.

19:11.headline: בסנורים: a rare word for a sudden blindness
19:11.body: בסנורים is used only here and in the story of Elisha. Rashi says it is a plague of blindness. Ibn Ezra says it means darkening of the eye and the heart.

sources.quote: בסנורים. מַכַּת עִוָּרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says בסנורים is a plague of blindness.

sources.quote: ופירושו מחשך העין והלב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says its meaning is a darkening of the eye and the heart.

19:12.headline: "Who do you have here?" is also "who gives you a mouth"?
19:12.body: Rashi's plain reading is: who do you have in the city besides your wife and daughters? The midrash reads מי לך פה as "who has a mouth", asking how Lot can still argue for such people.

sources.quote: מִי יֵשׁ לְךָ עוֹד בָּעִיר הַזֹּאת חוּץ מֵאִשְׁתְּךָ וּבְנוֹתֶיךָ שֶׁבַּבַּיִת
sources.says: Rashi says the plain reading is: who do you have in this city besides your wife and daughters at home?

sources.quote: מי לך פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה לְלַמֵּד סַנֵּגוֹרְיָא עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the midrash reads it as: what opening of the mouth do you have to defend them?

19:14.headline: "Who took his daughters": already married, or only engaged?
19:14.body: Radak says they had already taken Lot's daughters as wives. Rashi says the daughters still at home were only engaged to them. Ibn Ezra says Lot had two other daughters who died in Sodom.

sources.quote: שֶׁלְּקָחוּם כְּבָר
sources.says: Radak says they had already taken them.

sources.quote: שֶׁאוֹתָן שֶׁבַּבַּיִת אֲרוּסוֹת לָהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the ones in the house were engaged to them.

sources.quote: ב' בנות אחרות היו לו ומתו בסדום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he had two other daughters, and they died in Sodom.

19:15.headline: "The daughters who are found": in the house, or still alive?
19:15.body: Rashi says it means the daughters ready for you in the house, to save them. Ibn Ezra reads "found" as a hint that his other two daughters were already dead.

sources.quote: הַמְזֻמָּנוֹת לְךָ בַּבַּיִת לְהַצִּילָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means those ready for you in the house, to save them.

sources.quote: ב' בנות אחרות היו לו ומתו בסדום והעד הנמצאות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Lot had two other daughters who died in Sodom, and the proof is the word הנמצאות.

19:18.headline: Lot's second "Adonai": a holy name this time, or plain "my lords"
19:18.body: Rashi says the sages took this אדני as holy, because Lot says it is He who gives life. Ibn Ezra says it is plain, meaning "my masters", with a different vowel because it comes at the end of the verse.

sources.quote: שֶׁשֵּׁם זֶה קֹדֶשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת נַפְשִׁי
sources.says: Rashi says this name is holy, because it says of Him: to keep my soul alive.

sources.quote: חול ונקמץ בעבור שהוא סוף פסוק
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is plain, and the vowel is a kamatz because it is at the end of the verse.

19:20.headline: "It is a mitzar": small, or with few sins?
19:20.body: Ibn Ezra says מצער means small, from צעיר, "young". Rashi gives two readings: its sins are few, or the town is small with few people.

sources.quote: מצער. קטנה מגזרת צעיר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מצער is small, from the word צעיר.

sources.quote: וַהֲלֹא עֲוֹנוֹתֶיהָ מוּעָטִין
sources.says: Rashi says its sins are few.

sources.quote: הֲלֹא עִיר קְטַנָּה הִיא וַאֲנָשִׁים בָּהּ מְעַט
sources.says: Rashi says the plain reading is that it is a small city with few people.

19:20.headline: "Near" means recently settled
19:20.body: Rashi reads קרבה as near in time. The city was settled recently, so its sins were not yet complete.

sources.quote: קְרוֹבָה יְשִׁיבָתָהּ, נִתְיַשְּׁבָה מִקָּרוֹב, לְפִיכָךְ לֹא נִתְמַלְּאָה סְאָתָהּ עֲדַיִן
sources.says: Rashi says its settling is near: it was settled recently, so its measure was not yet full.

19:24.headline: גפרית ואש: rain that turned to brimstone and fire
19:24.body: Rashi says it began as rain and turned into brimstone and fire. Sforno says the land and its people were themselves turned into the nature of brimstone and fire.

sources.quote: בַּתְּחִלָּה מָטָר, וְנַעֲשָׂה גָּפְרִית וָאֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says at first it was rain, and it became brimstone and fire.

sources.quote: שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ הָאָרֶץ הַהִיא וְיוֹשְׁבֶיהָ לְטֶבַע גָּפְרִית וָאֵשׁ
sources.says: Sforno says that land and its inhabitants were turned into the nature of brimstone and fire.

19:25.headline: "He overturned the cities": flipped upside down, or changed into something else?
19:25.body: Rashi says the four cities stood on one rock and God turned them from top to bottom. Sforno reads it as the land and its people turned into another nature.

sources.quote: אַרְבַּעְתָּם יוֹשְׁבוֹת בְּסֶלַע אֶחָד וַהֲפָכָן מִלְמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה
sources.says: Rashi says all four stood on one rock, and He turned them from top to bottom.

sources.quote: שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ הָאָרֶץ הַהִיא וְיוֹשְׁבֶיהָ לְטֶבַע גָּפְרִית וָאֵשׁ
sources.says: Sforno says that land and its inhabitants were changed into the nature of brimstone and fire.

19:28.headline: A כבשן is a lime kiln, wherever it appears in the Torah
19:28.body: Rashi says כבשן is a pit in which stones are burned to make lime, and that this is true of every כבשן in the Torah. Ibn Ezra says it is a place of constant fire.

sources.quote: חֲפִירָה שֶׁשּׂוֹרְפִין בָּהּ אֶת הָאֲבָנִים לְסִיד, וְכֵן כָּל כִּבְשָׁן שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a pit where stones are burned for lime, and so is every kivshan in the Torah.

sources.quote: הכבשן. מקום אש דולקת תמיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הכבשן is a place of a fire that always burns.

19:31.headline: "No man in the land": the whole world, or just their region?
19:31.body: Rashi and Rashbam say the daughters thought the whole world had been destroyed, as in the Flood. Sforno says it means there was no fitting man in their region.

sources.quote: סְבוּרוֹת הָיוּ שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם נֶחֱרַב כְּמוֹ בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל
sources.says: Rashi says they thought the whole world had been destroyed, like the generation of the Flood.

sources.quote: סבורות היו שהעולם נהפך שהביא מבול של אש
sources.says: Rashbam says they thought the world had been overturned and that He brought a flood of fire.

sources.quote: אֵין אִישׁ בָּזֶה הַגָּלִיל רָאוּי לָבוֹא עָלֵינוּ
sources.says: Sforno says there was no man in this region fit to come to us.

19:33.headline: A dot over one letter: "when she rose", he may have known
19:33.body: In this verse the word ובקומה has dots over it. Rashi says the dots hint that he did know when she got up. Radak says the plain meaning is that he did not know even when she rose, because he was so drunk.

sources.quote: ובקומה. שֶׁל בְּכִירָה נָקוּד, לוֹמַר, שֶׁבְּקוּמָהּ יָדַע
sources.says: Rashi says the word for the elder is dotted, to say that when she rose he knew.

sources.quote: אֲפִלּוּ בְּקוּמָהּ מֵאֶצְלוֹ לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ בָּהּ מֵרֹב שִׁכְרוּתוֹ
sources.says: Radak says he did not sense her even as she rose from beside him, because of his heavy drunkenness.

19:37.headline: Moab means "from my father", spelled out without shame
19:37.body: Rashi, Radak and Ibn Ezra read מואב as מאב, "from a father". Rashi says the elder daughter, who had no modesty, announced it in the name.

sources.quote: זוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה צְנוּעָה פֵּרְשָׁה שֶׁמֵּאָבִיהָ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says this one, who was not modest, spelled out that he was from her father.

sources.quote: כְּלוֹמַר מֵאָב הָיָה לִי בֵּן זֶה
sources.says: Radak says it means: this son was to me from a father.

sources.quote: מואב. כמו מאב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מואב is like מאב.

2:2.headline: 'Finished' on the seventh day, though the work ended on the sixth
2:2.body: God finished on the seventh day, yet the work ended on the sixth. Rashi says the world still lacked rest, which came with Shabbat.

sources.says: Rashi says the world still lacked rest, and when Shabbat came, rest came and the work was complete.
sources.quote: מֶה הָיָה הָעוֹלָם חָסֵר? מְנוּחָה, בָּאת שַׁבָּת בָּאת מְנוּחָה, כָּלְתָה וְנִגְמְרָה הַמְּלָאכָה:

sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a view that the letter ב can mean 'before', as in 'לא תחסום שור בדישו'.
sources.quote: וי"א כי יש בי"ת שטעמו קודם,

2:4.headline: בהבראם can be read as 'with a ה' or 'through Avraham'
2:4.body: The letters of בהבראם can be split as בה' בראם, 'with the letter ה he created them'. They can also be rearranged to give באברהם, 'for the sake of Avraham'.

sources.says: Rashi reads the word as 'with a ה He created them'.
sources.quote: בְּהִבָּרְאָם, בְּה' בְרָאָם,

sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah reads בהבראם as 'through Avraham', in the merit of Avraham.
sources.quote: בְּהִבָּרְאָם בְּאַבְרָהָם, בִּזְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם.

2:5.headline: ה' אלהים: the name, and the word for ruler and judge
2:5.body: Rashi says ה' is God's name, and אלהים is the one who rules and judges everything. Together they mean 'ה', who is אלהים'.

sources.says: Rashi says ה' is His name and אלהים means the ruler and judge over everything.
sources.quote: ה' הוּא שְׁמוֹ, אֱלֹהִים שֶׁהוּא שַׁלִּיט וְשׁוֹפֵט עַל כֹּל,

2:7.headline: Two yods in וייצר hint at two creations
2:7.body: The verb for forming a person is spelled with two י letters. Rashi says this hints at two formings, one for this world and one for the revival of the dead, and an animal's forming has only one י.

sources.says: Rashi says the two forms are one for this world and one for the revival of the dead, and an animal's forming has no double י.
sources.quote: שְׁתֵּי יְצִירוֹת, יְצִירָה לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וִיצִירָה לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, אֲבָל בַּבְּהֵמָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת לַדִּין לֹא נִכְתַּב בִּיצִירָתָהּ שְׁנֵי יוֹדִי"ן:

2:7.headline: A 'living soul': Onkelos reads it as 'a speaking spirit'
2:7.body: Animals are also called נפש חיה, but Rashi says a person's is the most alive, since it adds knowledge and speech. Onkelos puts it into Aramaic as רוח ממללא, 'a speaking spirit'.

sources.says: Rashi says animals are also called a living soul, but a person's is the most alive because it adds knowledge and speech.
sources.quote: אַף בְּהֵמָה וְחַיָּה נִקְרְאוּ נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, אַךְ זוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם חַיָּה שֶׁבְּכֻלָּן, שֶׁנִתּוֹסֵף בּוֹ דֵּעָה וְדִבּוּר:

sources.says: Onkelos renders the living soul as 'a speaking spirit'.
sources.quote: וַהֲוַת בְּאָדָם לְרוּחַ מְמַלְלָא:

2:8.headline: מקדם: 'in the east', or 'from long ago'?
2:8.body: The word קדם can mean 'east' or 'long ago'. Rashi says God planted the garden in the east of Eden, while Onkelos puts it as מלקדמין, 'from the start'.

sources.says: Rashi says God planted the garden in the east of Eden.
sources.quote: מקדם. בְּמִזְרָחוֹ שֶׁל עֵדֶן נָטַע אֶת הַגָּן.

sources.says: Onkelos renders the word as מלקדמין, 'from long ago'.
sources.quote: גִּינְתָא בְעֵדֶן מִלְּקַדְמִין

2:14.headline: חדקל means 'sharp and swift'
2:14.body: Rashi reads חדקל as two words: חד, 'sharp', and קל, 'light'. He says its waters are sharp and swift.

sources.says: Rashi says its waters are sharp and swift.
sources.quote: שֶׁמֵּימָיו חַדִּין וְקַלִּין:

2:14.headline: פרת means 'fruitful and many'
2:14.body: Rashi says the river's waters are פרין ורבין, 'fruitful and many', and that they make a person healthy. The name plays on the verb for being fruitful.

sources.says: Rashi says its waters are fruitful and many, and make a person healthy.
sources.quote: שֶׁמֵּימָיו פָּרִין וְרָבִין וְמַבְרִין אֶת הָאָדָם:

2:15.headline: ויקח can mean 'took' or 'coaxed'
2:15.body: The verb means 'took'. Rashi, citing Bereshit Rabbah, says God took Adam with kind words and coaxed him into the garden.

sources.says: Rashi says God took him with pleasant words and persuaded him to enter.
sources.quote: לְקָחוֹ בִדְבָרִים נָאִים וּפִתָּהוּ לִכָּנֵס

2:18.headline: עזר כנגדו: a helper, or someone against him
2:18.body: The phrase can be read as 'a helper' and also 'opposite him'. Rashi and Bereshit Rabbah say if he earns it she is a helper, and if not she is against him.

sources.says: Rashi says if he is worthy she is a help, and if not she is against him, to fight.
sources.quote: זָכָה – עֵזֶר; לֹא זָכָה – כְּנֶגְדּוֹ לְהִלָּחֵם:

sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says if he earns it, a helper, and if not, against him.
sources.quote: אִם זָכָה עֵזֶר, וְאִם לָאו כְּנֶגְדּוֹ.

2:23.headline: The name אשה comes from איש
2:23.body: The verse itself says she is called אשה because she was taken from איש. Rashi says this plays on the sound of the two words, and proves the world was made in Hebrew.

sources.says: Rashi says the words play on each other, and that this shows the world was created in the holy tongue.
sources.quote: לָשׁוֹן נוֹפֵל עַל לָשׁוֹן מִכָּאן שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָעוֹלָם בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the dagesh in אשה stands in for the hidden י that is in איש.
sources.quote: ודגשות שי"ן "אשה" תמורת היו"ד הנח הנעלם שהוא באיש,

20:2.headline: In 'אל שרה' the word אל means 'about', not 'to'
20:2.body: Abraham did not say 'she is my sister' to Sarah. He said it about her, to the men who asked.

sources.quote: על שרה אשתו, כיוצא בו אל הלקח ארון
sources.says: Rashi says אל here means על, 'about', like the 'about the capture of the ark' in I Samuel 4.

sources.quote: אל שרה אשתו, כמו על
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אל here is like על.

sources.quote: בעבור שרה אשתו, אמר לשואלים אותו עליה אחתי הוא
sources.says: Radak says Abraham said 'she is my sister' for Sarah's sake, to those who asked him about her.

20:4.headline: Abimelech says 'the nation' and means himself, his people and his land
20:4.body: A king stands for his whole people. Radak says that if God kills the king, it is as if the nation dies with him.

sources.quote: אם תהרגני כאלו נהרג עמי, כי אני מלך מנהיג אותם במשפט
sources.says: Radak says that if God kills him it is as if his people are killed with him, since he is the king who leads them by law.

sources.quote: גוי גם צדיק תהרוג, בעד נפשו וביתו וממלכתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the phrase is said on behalf of Abimelech himself, his house and his kingdom.

sources.quote: שמא כך דרכך לאבד האמות חנם
sources.says: Rashi has Abimelech ask whether it is God's way to destroy whole nations for nothing.

20:6.headline: The sages hear 'your sin' and 'what makes you sin' in מחטו
