20:6.body: Radak says the ו at the end stands for the א of the root חטא, 'sin'. The midrash reads מחטו לי as מחטונך לי: the urge that makes you sin is in God's hand, so the credit is God's.

sources.quote: מחטונך לי, יצרך המחטיאך בידי הוא מסור
sources.says: Rabbi Yitzchak reads מחטו לי as מחטונך לי, 'the urge that makes you sin is handed over to Me'.

sources.quote: מחטו. הוי״ו במקום האל״ף למ״ד הפועל
sources.says: Radak says the ו in מחטו takes the place of the א, the last letter of the root.

20:7.headline: וחיה here means 'and be healed', not only 'and live'
20:7.body: The word usually means 'live'. Sforno and Radak read it as 'be healed', as in עד חיותם in Joshua 5:8, where the men healed after circumcision.

sources.quote: וחיה. תרפא, כמו עד חיותם
sources.says: Sforno says וחיה means 'you will be healed', like עד חיותם in Joshua 5:8.

sources.quote: ופרושו ותרפא, כמו עד חיותם
sources.says: Radak says it means 'and you will be healed', like עד חיותם.

20:12.headline: Sarah is Abraham's 'sister', but she is really his niece
20:12.body: Rashi and Rashbam say grandchildren count as children, so Haran's daughter counts as the daughter of Terach. That makes Sarah Abraham's 'sister'.

sources.quote: בני בנים הרי הן כבנים, והרי היא בתו של תרח
sources.says: Rashi says grandchildren count as children, so she is Terach's daughter.

sources.quote: כי בני בנים הרי הם כבנים והיא היתה בת הרן בן תרח
sources.says: Rashbam says grandchildren count as children and she was the daughter of Haran, Terach's son.

20:13.headline: אלהים takes a plural verb here. Is it God, or many gods?
20:13.body: Rashi says words for God and for masters often take a plural verb. Radak adds that Abraham spoke this way because his listeners spoke of their gods in the plural.

sources.quote: הרבה מקומות לשון אלהות ולשון מרות קרוי בלשון רבים
sources.says: Rashi says that in many places a word for God or for a master is spoken of in the plural.

sources.quote: ואמר התעו לשון רבים כנגד השומעים שקוראים אלהיהם בלשון רבים
sources.says: Radak says Abraham used the plural 'they made wander' because his hearers spoke of their gods in the plural.

sources.quote: והוה כד טעו עממיא בתר עובדי ידיהון
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as 'when the nations strayed after the work of their hands', so he does not read אלהים as God here.

20:13.headline: אמרי לי means 'say about me', not 'say to me'
20:13.body: Abraham asks Sarah to say 'he is my brother' about him, to whoever asks. The little word ל means 'about' here.

sources.quote: אמרי לי. עלי, וכן וישאלו אנשי המקום לאשתו
sources.says: Rashi says אמרי לי means 'about me', like 'the men of the place asked about his wife'.

sources.quote: אמרי לי. בשבילי וכן ואמר פרעה לבני ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'on my account', like 'Pharaoh will say about the children of Israel'.

20:16.headline: ונכחת: 'you are put right', or 'you have an answer'?
20:16.body: The root means to argue or to be set right. Rashi reads it as Sarah now having an answer for the world, and Ibn Ezra and Radak read it as Sarah being rebuked, so she never again said 'he is my brother'.

sources.quote: יהי לך פתחון פה להתוכח ולהראות דברים נכרים הללו
sources.says: Rashi says you will have an opening to argue and to show these plain facts.

sources.quote: וטעם ונוכחת דברי משה שלא אמרה עוד שרה על אברהם אחי הוא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means Sarah was rebuked and never again said of Abraham 'he is my brother'.

sources.quote: נוכחה ונוסרה שרה מכאן ואילך שלא אמרה עוד
sources.says: Radak says Sarah was rebuked and corrected, so from then on she did not say it again.

20:17.headline: וילדו may mean 'gave birth', or 'were relieved'
20:17.body: Ibn Ezra says it refers only to Abimelech's wife and maids, so it is ordinary birth. Rashi, following Onkelos, says it means their blocked openings were opened.

sources.quote: כתרגומו ואתרוחו, נפתחו נקביהם והוציאו
sources.says: Rashi says it is as Onkelos translates, 'they were relieved': their openings opened and they discharged.

sources.quote: וילדו. שב אל אשת אבימלך ואמהותיו לא אל אבימלך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the verb refers to Abimelech's wife and maids and not to Abimelech.

sources.quote: וענינו הוצאת זרע
sources.says: Radak says its meaning is the bringing out of seed.

20:18.headline: The doubled 'he shut up' counts every kind of blockage
20:18.body: The verse says עצר עצר, with the verb twice. The midrash lists blockage of the mouth, throat, ear, and above and below. Rabbeinu Bahya says the doubling is for the two kinds of blockage, large and small.

sources.quote: נאמר עצירה בפה, עצירה בגרון, עצירה באזן, עצירה מלמעלה, עצירה מלמטה
sources.says: The midrash says the stoppage was in the mouth, throat, ear, above and below.

sources.quote: זה עצירת נקבים גדולים וקטנים, ועל כן נכפל הלשון
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says this was the blocking of large and small openings, and that is why the word is doubled.

20:18.headline: על דבר שרה: 'because of a word of Sarah'
20:18.body: דבר can mean 'matter', but Rashi reads it as 'word': this happened on account of what Sarah said.

sources.quote: על דבר שרה. על פי דבורה של שרה
sources.says: Rashi says על דבר שרה means 'by the word of Sarah'.

21:7.headline: Sarah says 'children' although she had one baby
21:7.body: Rashi says the plural is because the noblewomen brought their babies to the feast, and Sarah nursed them all. Radak says it may also mean she could nurse other children later.

sources.quote: ביום המשתה הביאו השרות בניהן עמהן והניקה אותם
sources.says: Rashi says the noblewomen brought their children to the feast and she nursed them.

sources.quote: כי אם מניקה, אחרי כן תניק בנים אחרים אם תרצה
sources.says: Radak says that if she nurses now, she could later nurse other children if she wished.

21:8.headline: ויגמל means weaned, and the sages also read it as weaned from evil
21:8.body: Plainly it means the child stopped nursing. One sage in the midrash says Isaac was weaned from the evil urge.

sources.quote: נגמל מיצר הרע. רבנן אמרי נגמל מחלבו
sources.says: One rabbi says he was weaned from the evil urge, and the other rabbis say he was weaned from his milk.

sources.quote: נבדל מן הדדים
sources.says: Rashbam says it means he was separated from the breasts.

21:12.headline: 'Listen to her voice': Sarah ranks above Abraham in prophecy
21:12.body: God tells Abraham to do whatever Sarah says. Rashi learns from this that Abraham ranked below Sarah in prophecy.

sources.quote: למדנו שהיה אברהם טפל לשרה בנביאות
sources.says: Rashi says we learn that Abraham was secondary to Sarah in prophecy.

21:14.headline: ותתע: Hagar lost her way, or went back to idols
21:14.body: The verb means to wander off course. Radak says she lost the road in the desert. Rashi says she went back to the idols of her father's house.

sources.quote: כי לא ידעה הדרך משנכנסה במדבר
sources.says: Radak says she wandered because she did not know the way once she entered the desert.

sources.quote: חזרה לגלולי בית אביה
sources.says: Rashi says she returned to the idols of her father's house.

21:17.headline: 'Where he is' or 'as he is now'?
21:17.body: In the plain reading, God heard the boy in the place where he lay. Rashi, quoting the sages, reads it as 'as he is now': a person is judged by what he is now, not by what he will become.

sources.quote: לפי מעשים שהוא עושה עכשו הוא נדון, ולא לפי מה שהוא עתיד לעשות
sources.says: Rashi says he is judged by what he does now, and not by what he will do.

sources.quote: הוצרך לומר במקום אשר הוא שם נתן לו את המים
sources.says: Rashbam says the verse needed to say that God gave him the water in the place where he was.

sources.quote: באותו מקום שהשלכת אותו, כי חשבת שימות שם שמע אלהים את קולו
sources.says: Radak says it means in that very place where she left him, thinking he would die there.

21:19.headline: God 'opened her eyes': she was not blind, she was shown
21:19.body: Maimonides says פקח is used for waking up understanding, not for restoring sight. Sforno agrees: God gave her the knowledge to see the water that was there, since she had not been blind before.

sources.quote: משמשת רק במשמעות של גילוי הבחנה, לא של התחדשות של ראייה חושית
sources.says: Maimonides says the word פקח is used only for the opening of discernment, not for renewed physical sight, and gives this verse as an example.

sources.quote: נתן בה דעת להכיר מקום מים שהיה שם, כי לא היתה סומא קודם לכן
sources.says: Sforno says God gave her the understanding to recognise the water that was there, for she had not been blind before.

21:20.headline: קשת names a trade: 'bowman'
21:20.body: Rashi says it is named for the craft, like חמר 'donkey driver' and גמל 'camel driver', and Ibn Ezra says it is a descriptive word like גנב 'thief'.

sources.quote: על שם האמנות, כמו חמר, גמל, ציד
sources.says: Rashi says it is named for the craft, like חמר, גמל and ציד.

sources.quote: קשת. שם התואר, כמו גנב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says קשת is a describing word, like גנב.

21:21.headline: Paran sounds like the 'wild man' Ishmael was promised to be
21:21.body: Rashbam ties the desert of Paran to the earlier prophecy that Ishmael would be a פרא אדם, a wild man.

sources.quote: במדבר פארן - כדכתיב: והוא יהיה פרא אדם
sources.says: Rashbam says Paran fits what was written, 'he will be a wild man'.

21:31.headline: Beer-sheba means both 'well of seven' and 'well of the oath'
21:31.body: The verse says they named it because there they both swore. Radak says the same word means seven and oath, so the seven ewes and the oath are both in the name. Ibn Ezra says the word for an oath comes from שבע, 'seven'.

sources.quote: לפי שלשון המספר הזה ולשון השבועה אחד
sources.says: Radak says the word for this number and the word for an oath are the same.

sources.quote: קראו למקום ההוא שבע, ונשתתף באר עם שבע
sources.says: Radak says they called the place 'seven' for the two things, and 'well' was joined to 'seven' for the well Abraham dug.

sources.quote: ודע כי מלת שבועה עקרה שבעה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the root of the word שבועה is שבעה.

21:33.headline: אשל is a rare word. The sages read it as 'ask'
21:33.body: Rashi gives two views from the Talmud: an orchard, or an inn. The midrash and Rabbeinu Bahya also hear the word שאל, 'ask', because Abraham told every passer-by to ask for whatever he wanted.

sources.quote: חד אמר פרדס להביא ממנו פרות לאורחים בסעודה, וחד אמר פנדק לאכסניא
sources.says: Rashi says one rabbi called it an orchard for fruit for guests, and the other an inn.

sources.quote: רבי יהודה אמר אשל פרדס, שאל מה תשאל, תאנים וענבים ורמונים
sources.says: The midrash says Rabbi Yehuda calls it an orchard and reads 'ask what you want': figs, grapes and pomegranates.

sources.quote: אברהם היה אומר לכל עובר ושב: ״שאל מה אתן לך״
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the letters of אשל are those of שאל, because Abraham told everyone who passed to ask what he would give.

21:33.headline: 'He called in the name of the Lord': prayed, proclaimed, or called guests to bless?
21:33.body: Onkelos reads it as prayer. Rabbeinu Bahya says it means to call out and announce. Rashi says Abraham told his guests to bless the one whose food they ate.

sources.quote: וצלי תמן בשמא דיי אלהא דעלמא
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'and he prayed there in the name of the Lord, God of the world'.

sources.quote: לשון קריאה והכרזה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says it is a word of calling out and announcing.

sources.quote: אומר להם ברכו למי שאכלתם משלו
sources.says: Rashi says he told his guests to bless the one whose food they had eaten.

22:1.headline: נסה 'tested' also sounds like נס, a banner raised high
22:1.body: The midrash hears נס, a banner or mast, in נסה. God tested Abraham in order to raise him up for the whole world to see.

sources.quote: נסיון אחר נסיון, וגדולין אחר גדולין, בשביל לנסותן בעולם, בשביל לגדלן בעולם, כנס הזה של ספינה
sources.says: The midrash says trial after trial, greatness after greatness: God tests them in the world to raise them in the world, like the mast-banner of a ship.

sources.quote: נסה את אברהם - קנתרו וצערו
sources.says: Rashbam says נסה means that God provoked and troubled Abraham.

22:1.headline: 'Here I am' is a word of humility and readiness
22:1.body: Rashi says הנני is what the pious say, and it carries both humility and being ready. The midrash adds that it means 'here I am for the priesthood, and here for the kingship', and that Abraham received both.

sources.quote: כך היא עניתם של חסידים, לשון ענוה הוא ולשון זמון
sources.says: Rashi says this is how the pious answer: it is a word of humility and of readiness.

sources.quote: אברהם אמר הנני, הנני לכהנה, הנני למלכות, זכה לכהנה וזכה למלכות
sources.says: The midrash says Abraham's 'here I am' meant 'here for the priesthood, here for the kingship', and he won both.

22:2.headline: 'Your only son': Ishmael was also a son
22:2.body: The word יחיד means 'only'. The midrash has Abraham answer that each son is the only one of his mother. Ramban says Isaac is called 'only' because he alone is the son of the wife and the one called 'seed'.

sources.quote: זה יחיד לאמו וזה יחיד לאמו
sources.says: Rashi has Abraham reply that this one is the only one of his mother and that one is the only one of his mother.

sources.quote: בעבור היותו בן הגבירה והוא לבדו אשר יקרא לו זרע, קראו יחידו
sources.says: Ramban says Isaac is called his only son because he is the son of the lady of the house and the only one who would be called his seed.

22:2.headline: והעלהו means 'bring him up', not 'slaughter him'
22:2.body: The word can mean 'offer up' or just 'take up'. Rashi says God never told Abraham to slaughter Isaac. He told him to bring him up the mountain as an offering, and afterward to bring him down.

sources.quote: אלא להעלהו להר לעשותו עולה, ומשהעלהו אמר לו הורידהו
sources.says: Rashi says God wanted him only to bring him up the mountain to make him an offering, and once he brought him up, told him to bring him down.

22:3.headline: Abraham saddled the donkey himself, because love bends the rules
22:3.body: A man of his rank would have told a servant to do it. Rashi and the midrash say love overrides the normal order, and that hatred does too.

sources.quote: הוא בעצמו, ולא צוה לאחד מעבדיו, שהאהבה מקלקלת השורה
sources.says: Rashi says he saddled it himself and did not tell a servant, since love breaks the usual order.

sources.quote: אהבה מקלקלת את השורה ושנאה מקלקלת את השורה
sources.says: The midrash says love breaks the line, and hatred breaks the line.

22:4.headline: He 'saw the place': a cloud on the mountain, or just the land
22:4.body: Rashi says Abraham saw a cloud bound to the mountain. Ramban says that, in the plain reading, he just recognized the land of Moriah from far away.

sources.quote: ראה ענן קשור על ההר
sources.says: Rashi says he saw a cloud tied to the mountain.

sources.quote: ויתכן על דרך הפשט וירא את המקום מרחק, שראה ארץ המוריה
sources.says: Ramban says the plain meaning is that he saw the land of Moriah from far off.

sources.quote: ושלטה בו עינו לראות מקום מרחוק ברצון האל יתברך
sources.says: Sforno says his eye was given power to see a faraway place, by God's will.

22:5.headline: 'As far as there' echoes God's 'so shall your children be'
22:5.body: Abraham says he will go עד כה, 'as far as there'. Rashi says he is also thinking, 'I will see how God's promise כה יהיה זרעך, so shall your seed be, will come true.'

sources.quote: אראה היכן הוא מה שאמר לי המקום כה יהיה זרעך
sources.says: Rashi says 'I will see where is what he told me, so shall your seed be'.

22:6.headline: מאכלת, the knife, is named for eating
22:6.body: The word appears only a few times. Rashi says the knife is called this because it 'eats' the flesh, as in 'my sword shall eat flesh'. The midrash adds that it makes meat fit to eat.

sources.quote: על שם שאוכלת את הבשר, כמה דתימא וחרבי תאכל בשר
sources.says: Rashi says it is called מאכלת because it eats the flesh, as in 'my sword shall eat flesh'.

sources.quote: למה נקראת סכין מאכלת, לפי שמכשר אוכלים
sources.says: The midrash says the knife is called מאכלת because it makes food fit to eat.

22:12.headline: 'Now I know': God did not learn something new
22:12.body: A reader may ask how God could not know. Ramban says Abraham's fear of God was only potential and now became real. Maimonides says it shows everyone how far the fear of God goes.

sources.quote: מתחלה היתה יראתו בכח לא יצא לפעל במעשה הגדול הזה, ועתה נודעה במעשה
sources.says: Ramban says at first his fear of God was only potential and had not yet come out into action, and now it was shown in the act.

sources.quote: עתה אני רואה ונתפרסם לכל העולם
sources.says: Rashbam says it means 'now I see, and it is made known to the whole world'.

sources.quote: מעתה יש לי מה להשיב לשטן ולאמות התמהים מה היא חבתי אצלך
sources.says: Rashi says now God has an answer for Satan and for the astonished nations about why Abraham is dear to him.

sources.quote: במעשה זה, שבגללו תיקרא ירא אלהים, ידעו כל בני האדם עד היכן מגיעה יראת ה'
sources.says: Maimonides says that through this act, for which he is called a God-fearer, all people will know how far the fear of God goes.

22:13.headline: בסבך 'in the thicket': Satan tangles the ram
22:13.body: בסבך means a tangle of trees. Rashi says the ram was running toward Abraham and Satan tangled it up in the trees.

sources.quote: שהיה רץ אצל אברהם, והשטן סובכו ומערבבו באילנות
sources.says: Rashi says the ram was running toward Abraham and Satan tangled and confused it among the trees.

sources.quote: ומלת בסבך תורה שהיה המקום ההוא יער ושם אילנות
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the word teaches that the place was a forest with trees.

22:13.headline: 'Instead of his son': as if it were his son
22:13.body: The verse already said Abraham offered it. Rashi asks why it adds 'in place of his son', and says it means that with each step Abraham prayed that it be counted as if done to his son.

sources.quote: על כל עבודה שעשה ממנו היה מתפלל ואומר יהי רצון שתהא זו כאלו היא עשויה בבני
sources.says: Rashi says that at every act he did with the ram he prayed that it count as if done to his son.

sources.quote: תחת בנו. תמורת מה שהיה בלבו לזבח את בנו
sources.says: Sforno says תחת בנו means in exchange for what was in his heart, to sacrifice his son.

22:14.headline: Abraham names the place 'The Lord will see'. What does that mean?
22:14.body: The name echoes Abraham's earlier words about the lamb. Rashi, following Onkelos, reads it as God choosing this place. Onkelos reads 'here generations will worship'.

sources.quote: פשוטו כתרגומו, ה' יבחר ויראה לו את המקום הזה להשרות בו שכינתו ולהקריב כאן קרבנות
sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is as Onkelos translates: the Lord will choose and show himself this place, to rest his presence there and to bring offerings.

sources.quote: הכא יהון פלחן דריא
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'here the generations will worship'.

sources.quote: על שם שאמר אלהים יראה לו השה
sources.says: Radak says the name is because Abraham had said 'God will see to the lamb'.

22:17.headline: The doubled 'bless, I will bless': one blessing for father, one for son
22:17.body: Rashi and the midrash count each doubled word twice. One part is for Abraham and one for Isaac. Radak says every doubling strengthens the promise.

sources.quote: ברך אברכך. אחת לאב ואחת לבן
sources.says: Rashi says one blessing is for the father and one for the son.

sources.quote: ברכה לאב, ברכה לבן
sources.says: The midrash says a blessing for the father and a blessing for the son.

sources.quote: כי כל כפל הוא לחזק הדבר
sources.says: Radak says every doubling is to strengthen the matter.

22:18.headline: עקב means 'because', but also 'heel': reward comes at the end
22:18.body: Radak says עקב means 'reward' and comes from 'heel', the end of the body. Reward comes at the end, as the heel does.

sources.quote: עקב. פרושו שכר, והוא מענין עקב, כמו שהעקב סוף הגוף, כן השכר סוף
sources.says: Radak says עקב means reward, and comes from עקב 'heel': as the heel is the end of the body, so the reward comes at the end.

sources.quote: עקב. שכר באחרית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עקב means reward in the end.

22:18.headline: והתברכו: 'bless themselves', not 'be blessed'
22:18.body: In Genesis 12:3 the verb is passive, 'will be blessed'. Radak says here it means the nations will bless themselves by saying, 'May God bless us as he blessed Abraham's children'.

sources.quote: והתברכו. פרושו אינו כמו ונברכו
sources.says: Radak says והתברכו does not mean the same as ונברכו in Genesis 12:3.

sources.quote: כי פרשנו שהם יסבבו הברכה לעצמם בתפלתם ויאמרו: האל יברכנו כמו שברך זרע אברהם
sources.says: Radak says the nations will bring the blessing to themselves by their prayer, saying that God should bless us as he blessed Abraham's seed.

sources.quote: כשיקראו כלם בשם ה' לעבדו שכם אחד, כלם יתברכו בזרעך
sources.says: Sforno says when they all call on the Lord's name to serve him together, all will be blessed through your seed.

23:3.headline: 'His dead' for a woman: the word means the body
23:3.body: The verse says מתו, 'his dead', though Sarah is a woman. Radak and Rabbeinu Bahya say it means the dead body, which is a masculine word. Ibn Ezra says the phrase 'before his dead' points to the body.

sources.quote: ואמר מתו, ואם היא אשה, כי על הגוף המת אמר
sources.says: Radak says he says 'his dead' although she was a woman because he is speaking of the dead body.

sources.quote: מפני שהגוף לשון זכר, ומה שימות מן האדם הוא הגוף לא הנפש
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says it is because 'body' is masculine, and what dies in a person is the body, not the soul.

sources.quote: פני מתו. רמז לגוף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'before his dead' is a hint at the body.

23:6.headline: 'A prince of God': a great prince, or one God has lifted up
23:6.body: The Hittites call Abraham נשיא אלהים. Radak reads it as 'God has lifted you up', and Ibn Ezra reads it as a mark of greatness, since you are a prophet. Rashbam says it means you are no stranger and need not buy.

sources.quote: שאלהים נשאך ואנחנו חושבים אותך כן בתוכנו
sources.says: Radak says it means that God lifted you up, and we think of you that way among us.

sources.quote: דרך גדולה בעבור כי אתה נביא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a way of saying greatness, because you are a prophet.

sources.quote: ולא גר ותושב ואין אתה צריך לקנות
sources.says: Rashbam says they mean he is not a stranger and settler, and does not need to buy.

23:6.headline: לא יכלה means 'will not hold back', not 'will not finish'
23:6.body: The root usually means to finish. Rashi, Ibn Ezra and Radak read it here as to hold back or refuse, as in 'do not withhold your mercies'.

sources.quote: לא ימנע כמו לא תכלא רחמיך
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'will not withhold', like 'do not withhold your mercies' in Psalms 40.

sources.quote: יכלה. ימנע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יכלה means 'will withhold'.

sources.quote: לא יכלה. לא ימנע
sources.says: Radak says לא יכלה means 'will not withhold'.

23:8.headline: 'If it is your נפש' means 'if it is your will'
23:8.body: נפש usually means soul. Here it means will or wish. Maimonides lists this verse among his examples of that sense.

sources.quote: נפשכם. רצונכם
sources.says: Rashi says נפשכם means 'your will'.

sources.quote: ברצונכם, כמו אל תתנני בנפש צרי
sources.says: Radak says it means 'by your will', like 'do not give me over to the will of my foes'.

sources.quote: כלומר אם דבר זה בכוונתכם וברצונכם
sources.says: Maimonides lists this verse as an example of נפש meaning will, 'if this is in your intention and will'.

23:8.headline: ופגעו usually means 'struck', but here it means 'plead for me'
23:8.body: The verb פגע usually means to meet or hit. Here Abraham asks them to intercede with Ephron for him.

sources.quote: לשון בקשה כמו אל תפגעי בי
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of request, like 'do not press me' in Ruth 1.

sources.quote: התחננו בעבורי
sources.says: Radak says it means to plead on my behalf.

sources.quote: פגעוני לי, סרסרוני לי, ואם לאו צלו לי עילויה
sources.says: The midrash reads it as 'be my go-between, and if not, pray for me about it'.

23:11.headline: 'I have given' means 'I give it to you now'
23:11.body: Ephron uses the past tense for something he is only now offering. Rashi says it counts as if already given. Abraham later answers with 'I have given the price of the field', in the same way.

sources.quote: הרי הוא כמו שנתתיה לך
sources.says: Rashi says it is as if I have already given it to you.

sources.quote: מעתה נתתיה לך
sources.says: Radak says it means 'from now, I have given it to you'.

sources.quote: ולשון נתתי ירצה בו הרי הוא כאלו נתתי
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the word 'I have given' means it is as if I gave.

23:16.headline: Ephron's name is spelled short: he said much and did little
23:16.body: The name is written without a ו in this verse. The sages say the Torah shortened it because he promised the field for free, then took a large sum.

sources.quote: חסר וי"ו; לפי שאמר הרבה, ואפלו מעט לא עשה
sources.says: Rashi says the name is missing a ו because he said a lot and did not do even a little.

sources.quote: זה עפרון, שהכניס עין רע בממונו של צדיק
sources.says: The midrash applies 'a man of evil eye hurries after wealth' to Ephron, who cast an evil eye on a righteous man's money, and the Torah shortened his name.

23:16.headline: 'Silver that passes to the merchant': accepted anywhere
23:16.body: The word עבר means 'passing'. Rashbam says it means silver that passes, accepted for all kinds of trade. Radak says it is silver of full weight, as merchants demand.

sources.quote: כסף צרוף ומתקבל לכל מיני סחורה
sources.says: Rashbam says it is refined silver, accepted for every kind of trade.

sources.quote: כסף מלא במשקלו, כמו שנושאים ונותנים בו הסוחרים
sources.says: Radak says it is silver of full weight, as merchants trade with it.

sources.quote: שמתקבלים בשקל בכל מקום
sources.says: Rashi says these were large shekels that are accepted everywhere.

23:17.headline: ויקם, 'rose', means the field was confirmed as Abraham's
23:17.body: קום usually means to stand up. Here it means to stand firm, as a sale does. Maimonides gives this verse as an example, and the midrash says the field rose in status as well.

sources.quote: ויש בו גם משמעות קיום הדבר ונכונותו
sources.says: Maimonides says קימה also means the confirming and firmness of a matter, and gives 'the field of Ephron was confirmed' as an example.

sources.quote: תקומה היתה לו, שיצא מיד הדיוט ליד מלך
sources.says: Rashi says it was a rise for the field, since it passed from an ordinary person to a king.

sources.quote: דהות נפילה וקמת
sources.says: The midrash says the field had fallen and now rose.

24:1.headline: The sages read זקן, 'old', as זה קנה, 'this one acquired'
24:1.body: The midrash splits the word: זה קנה, 'this one acquired two worlds'. Radak notes only that זקן can be read as a past-tense verb or as an adjective.

sources.quote: זקן זה קנה שני עולמות
sources.says: The midrash says זקן means זה קנה, 'this one acquired two worlds'.

sources.quote: ואברהם זקן. פעל עבר או תאר
sources.says: Radak says זקן may be a past-tense verb or a describing word.

24:2.headline: 'Elder of his house': old in years, or senior in the household?
24:2.body: Radak says it means either that the servant grew old in Abraham's house or that he was the eldest of the whole household. The midrash says he looked just like Abraham.

sources.quote: וענינו שגדל בביתו עד שזקן, או פירושו זקן מכל ביתו
sources.says: Radak says it means he grew up in his house until he was old, or that he was the oldest of the whole household.

sources.quote: שהיה זיו איקונין שלו דומה לו
sources.says: The midrash says the glow of his face was like Abraham's.

24:7.headline: Abraham says 'God of heaven' and leaves out 'of the earth'
24:7.body: A few verses earlier he said both. Rashi says God is now known on earth, but when he took Abraham from his father's house, he was God of heaven only.

sources.quote: אבל כשלקחני מבית אבי היה אלהי השמים ולא אלהי הארץ, שלא היו באי עולם מכירים בו
sources.says: Rashi says that when he took me from my father's house he was God of heaven and not of the earth, since people did not know him.

sources.quote: עד שלא הודעתי אותו לבריותיו, אלהי השמים, וכיון שהודעתי אותו לבריותיו, אלהי הארץ
sources.says: Rabbi Pinchas says before I made him known to people he was God of heaven, and once I made him known he was God of the earth.

24:10.headline: Abraham's camels were known because they went muzzled
24:10.body: Rashi says Abraham's camels stood out from other camels. They went out muzzled so they would not graze in other people's fields.

sources.quote: נכרין היו משאר גמלים, שהיו יוצאין זמומין מפני הגזל
sources.says: Rashi says they were recognizable from other camels, because they went out muzzled to avoid theft.

sources.quote: גמליו של אברהם אבינו היו נכרים, בכל מקום שהיו יוצאים, יוצאים זמומים
sources.says: The midrash says Abraham's camels were recognizable, and wherever they went they went muzzled.

24:10.headline: 'All the good of his master' may mean goods, or a deed of gift
24:10.body: Radak says it means a great deal of goods, as 'all the land' that came to Egypt does not mean literally all. Rashi and the midrash say it was a written deed giving Isaac everything, so that people would be eager to send their daughter.

sources.quote: וכל טוב. רב טוב, כמו וכל הארץ באו מצרימה
sources.says: Radak says וכל טוב means 'much good', like 'all the land came to Egypt'.

sources.quote: שטר מתנה כתב ליצחק על כל אשר לו, כדי שיקפצו לשלח לו בתם
sources.says: Rashi says he wrote Isaac a deed of gift for all that he had, so they would be quick to send their daughter.

sources.quote: וכל טוב אדניו בידו, רבי חלבו אמר זו דיאתיקי
sources.says: Rabbi Chelbo says 'all the good of his master in his hand' is a will.

24:12.headline: הקרה means 'arrange for me', not 'let it happen by chance'
24:12.body: The root קרה usually means to happen. Ibn Ezra and Radak read it here as 'prepare' or 'set up', and Onkelos translates it that way too.

sources.quote: הקרה נא לפני. כטעם הכן הפצי לפני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הקרה means the same as 'prepare what I want before me'.

sources.quote: זמן לפני כפי שאומר
sources.says: Radak says it means arrange before me what I am about to say.

sources.quote: זמין כען קדמי יומא דין
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as 'prepare for me today'.

24:14.headline: הכחת: 'you have chosen' or 'you have taught'?
24:14.body: The root usually means to rebuke. Rashi reads it as 'chosen', Radak as 'appointed', and Sforno as 'taught', meaning you trained her in good character.

sources.quote: ולשון הכחת בררת
sources.says: Rashi says הכחת means 'you chose'.

sources.quote: כי אותה זמנת ליצחק ואותה אקח לו לאשה
sources.says: Radak says it means you arranged for her for Isaac, and I will take her to be his wife.

sources.quote: יסרת והורית אותה מוסר השכל
sources.says: Sforno says it means you disciplined her and taught her understanding.

24:19.headline: 'Until אם they finish' where אם means 'when'
24:19.body: The word אם usually means 'if'. Rashi and Radak read it here as 'when', the same as אשר.

sources.quote: הרי אם משמש בלשון אשר
sources.says: Rashi says אם is used here in the sense of אשר, 'when'.

sources.quote: או יהיה אם במקום אשר, עד אשר יכלו לשתות
sources.says: Radak says אם may stand in place of אשר, meaning 'until they finish drinking'.

24:20.headline: ותער, 'she emptied', is a rare word for pouring out
24:20.body: Rashi says it means pouring, as in the later Hebrew word for pouring from one vessel into another. Radak says it means she emptied it into the trough.

sources.quote: לשון נפיצה, והרבה יש בלשון משנה המערה מכלי אל כלי
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for pouring out, and that the Mishnah often uses it for pouring from one vessel to another.

sources.quote: ותער כדה. ותריק אל השקת
sources.says: Radak says ותער כדה means she emptied her jar into the trough.

sources.quote: ותער - כמו ותערה
sources.says: Rashbam says ותער is like ותערה.

24:21.headline: משתאה is used only here: amazed, or waiting?
24:21.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra tie it to the root for desolate and stunned, so the servant was amazed. Onkelos reads it as 'waiting' and watching to see whether God had made the trip succeed.

sources.quote: משתומם ומתבהל על שראה דברו קרוב להצליח
sources.says: Rashi says he was astonished and hurried at seeing his mission close to success.

sources.quote: כמו משתומם מגזרת שאו ערים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'astonished', from the same root as 'cities lie desolate'.

sources.quote: וגברא שהי בה מסתכל שתיק למידע
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as 'and the man waited, looking at her silently, to know'.

24:22.headline: בקע, a half-shekel, appears twice and hints at Israel's shekels
24:22.body: Ibn Ezra says it comes from 'split': half a shekel. Rashi says the weight hints at the half-shekel each Israelite later gave.

sources.quote: חצי שקל מגזרת נבקע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is half a shekel, from the root for split.

sources.quote: חצי שקל, כמו: נטה ידך על הים ובקעהו
sources.says: Rashbam says it is half a shekel, like 'split it' in the Red Sea story.

sources.quote: רמז לשקלי ישראל בקע לגלגלת
sources.says: Rashi says it hints at the shekels of Israel, a בקע for each head.

24:22.headline: צמידים, 'bracelets', hints at the two joined tablets
24:22.body: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from 'bound together', like a lid bound to a vessel. Rashi hears in the two bracelets a hint of the two tablets of the law joined together.

sources.quote: רמז לשני לוחות מצמדות
sources.says: Rashi says the two bracelets hint at the two tablets, which are joined.

sources.quote: מגזרת צמיד פתיל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from the same root as 'a lid fastened with a cord'.

24:23.headline: Eliezer asks for one night. Rebekah answers with many.
24:23.body: He says ללין, 'to lodge', a word that means one night. She answers ללון, which can mean any number of nights.

sources.quote: ללין. לינה אחת, לין שם דבר; והיא אמרה ללון – כמה לינות
sources.says: Rashi says ללין means a single night and is a noun, but she said ללון, which means many nights.

sources.quote: ללין שם דבר, ומשמעותו לינה אחת
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says ללין is a noun, and its meaning is a single night.

24:27.headline: 'In the way': the right way, and the earth leapt for him
24:27.body: Rashi says 'the way' means the way that was prepared for him, the right road. Rabbeinu Bahya says it may hint that the road was shortened.

sources.quote: דרך המזמן, דרך הישר, באותו דרך שהייתי צריך
sources.says: Rashi says it means the prepared way, the straight way, the way I needed.

sources.quote: יתכן לפרש כי הכתוב הזה ירמז שקפצה לו הארץ
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says this verse may hint that the earth leapt for him, shortening the road.

24:29.headline: Why did Laban run? Rashi says: he saw the ring
24:29.body: The verse does not say why Laban ran. Rashi says he saw the gold ring and thought the man was rich. Sforno says he ran to look at a rich guest, not to bring him home.

sources.quote: ויהי כראות את הנזם, אמר עשיר הוא זה, ונתן עיניו בממון
sources.says: Rashi says that when he saw the ring he said this man is rich, and set his eyes on the money.

sources.quote: לראות אורח עשיר שבא לעיר, לא להכניסו לביתו
sources.says: Sforno says he ran to see a rich guest who came to the city, not to bring him in.

24:31.headline: 'I have cleared the house': of idols, or just made room?
24:31.body: The plain reading is that Laban made room in the house. Rashi, quoting the midrash, says he cleared it of idols.

sources.quote: פניתי הבית. מעבודת אלילים
sources.says: Rashi says 'I cleared the house' means of idol worship.

sources.quote: לך ולאנשיך, ופניתי גם מקום לגמלים
sources.says: Radak says I cleared it for you and your men, and also cleared a place for the camels.

24:32.headline: 'He opened the camels' means he took off their muzzles
24:32.body: Rashi says the verb means he undid the muzzle that stopped them from grazing. Ramban says it was Laban who did it, not Eliezer.

sources.quote: התיר זמם שלהם, שהיה סותם את פיהם שלא ירעו בדרך בשדות אחרים
sources.says: Rashi says he removed their muzzle, which had stopped their mouths so they would not graze in others' fields.

sources.quote: אל יתהלל חוגר כמפתח, התיר חבישתם
sources.says: Rashbam says it is like 'let not him who girds boast like him who loosens', that is, he loosened their bindings.

sources.quote: ויפתח הגמלים יחזר על לבן, שעשה עם אורחיו דרך מוסר
sources.says: Ramban says 'he unloosed the camels' refers back to Laban, who treated his guests with good manners.

24:42.headline: 'I came today': the road was shortened for him
24:42.body: Eliezer says he came to the well today. The sages read this as a miracle: he left that day and arrived that day, because the earth leapt for him.

sources.quote: היום יצאתי והיום באתי, מכאן שקפצה לו הארץ
sources.says: Rashi says 'today I left and today I came', so we learn the earth leapt for him.

sources.quote: ואבא היום אל העין, היום יצאתי והיום באתי
sources.says: The midrash says 'I came today to the spring' means today I left and today I came.

24:44.headline: הוכיח means 'made clear' or 'declared', not 'rebuked'
24:44.body: The root usually means to rebuke. Rashi says it means to make clear. Sforno ties it to the heavenly voice that announces 'the daughter of so-and-so for so-and-so'.

sources.quote: ברר והודיע, וכן כל הוכחה שבמקרא ברור דבר
sources.says: Rashi says it means to make clear and make known, and so every הוכחה in Scripture is the clearing up of a matter.

sources.quote: בת קול מכרזת ואומרת: בת פלוני לפלוני
sources.says: Sforno cites our sages: a heavenly voice announces 'the daughter of so-and-so for so-and-so'.

24:49.headline: 'To the right or to the left': Ishmael's family, or Lot's
24:49.body: The servant says he will turn right or left for a bride. Rashi says right is Ishmael's daughters and left is Lot's. Radak says it means a bride from a greater or lesser family.

sources.quote: על ימין. מבנות ישמעאל
sources.says: Rashi says 'to the right' means the daughters of Ishmael.

sources.quote: על שמאל. מבנות לוט, שהיה יושב לשמאלו של אברהם
sources.says: Rashi says 'to the left' means Lot's daughters, because Lot sat on Abraham's left.

sources.quote: או גדולה מכם או פחותה מכם אקח לבנו אשה בארץ הזאת
sources.says: Radak says it means that, whether greater than you or lesser, I will take a wife for his son in this land.

24:50.headline: 'Laban and Bethuel answered': why is Laban named first?
24:50.body: Rashi says Laban was wicked and jumped in to answer before his father. Radak says it was because Bethuel was old and the household was Laban's to manage.

sources.quote: רשע היה, וקפץ להשיב לפני אביו
sources.says: Rashi says Laban was wicked and rushed to answer before his father.

sources.quote: הקדים לבן לבתואל כי בתואל היה זקן ודברי הבית מוטלים על לבן
sources.says: Radak says he names Laban before Bethuel because Bethuel was old and household matters fell on Laban.

24:53.headline: מגדנות is a rare word for choice gifts
24:53.body: Rashi ties it to מגדים, choice fruits, and says the servant brought fruits of the Land of Israel. Ibn Ezra offers a second meaning: fine garments.

sources.quote: ומגדנות. לשון מגדים, שהביא עמו מיני פרות של ארץ ישראל
sources.says: Rashi says ומגדנות comes from מגדים and means kinds of fruit from the Land of Israel that he brought.

sources.quote: או פי' מלבושים נכבדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says another meaning is fine garments.

sources.quote: זאת המלה כוללת כל דבר משבח שבפרות כלים ובגדים
sources.says: Radak says the word covers anything praised, whether fruit, vessels or clothing.

24:55.headline: 'He said': one verb for her brother and her mother, but where is Bethuel?
24:55.body: The verb is singular, 'he said', though two people speak. Rashi asks where Bethuel was and says an angel killed him. Radak says it just joins the main speaker to the other.

sources.quote: ובתואל היכן היה? היה רוצה לעכב ובא מלאך והמיתו
sources.says: Rashi says Bethuel wanted to delay, and an angel came and killed him.

sources.quote: ספור הפעלה על הדבק בה, וכן ותדבר מרים ואהרן
sources.says: Radak says the verb goes with the person closest to it, like 'Miriam and Aaron spoke'.

sources.quote: הם שקיבלו המתנות והאב מחריש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was they who received the gifts while the father was silent.

24:58.headline: 'I will go': even if you do not want me to
24:58.body: Rashi says Rebekah answered from herself and would go even if the family objected. Rashbam says she was not troubled about delaying to dress herself up.

sources.quote: מעצמי, ואף אם אינכם רוצים
sources.says: Rashi says it means 'on my own, even if you are not willing'.

sources.quote: איני חושש להתעכב בשביל קישוט עצמי
sources.says: Rashbam says it means 'I am not worried about being delayed for the sake of dressing up'.

24:63.headline: לשוח, used only here: to pray, or to stroll among the bushes
24:63.body: Rashi and the midrash say it means prayer, as in 'he pours out his שיח before the Lord'. Ibn Ezra and Radak say it means walking among the bushes.

sources.quote: לשוח. לשון תפלה (בראשית רבה), כמו ישפך שיחו
sources.says: Rashi says לשוח is a word for prayer, like 'he pours out his complaint'.

sources.quote: אין שיחה אלא תפלה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the midrash that שיחה means nothing other than prayer.

sources.quote: לשוח. ללכת בין השיחים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says לשוח means to walk among the bushes.

sources.quote: כלומר לטיל בין השיחים
sources.says: Radak says it means to stroll among the bushes.

24:67.headline: 'Into the tent, Sarah his mother': a short phrase or she was Sarah
24:67.body: Ibn Ezra and Ramban read it as 'into the tent of Sarah his mother', with a word left out. Rashi reads it as 'into the tent, and she became like Sarah his mother'.

sources.quote: ויביאה האהלה ונעשית דגמת שרה אמו, כלומר והרי היא שרה אמו
sources.says: Rashi says he brought her into the tent and she became like his mother Sarah, that is, she was Sarah his mother.

sources.quote: דרך קצרה, האהלה אהל שרה אמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a short way of saying 'into the tent of Sarah his mother'.

sources.quote: חסר הנסמך, וכמוהו רבים
sources.says: Ramban says the word that this one depends on is missing, and there are many like it.

25:6.headline: Rashi reads the short spelling of "concubines" as one woman, Hagar
25:6.body: The plural הפילגשים is spelled short, which Rashi takes to mean only one concubine, Hagar, who is also Keturah. Rashbam instead names two women, Hagar and Keturah.

sources.quote: חָסֵר כְּתִיב, שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה אֶלָּא פִּלֶגֶשׁ אַחַת, הִיא הָגָר, הִיא קְטוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the word is written short, so there was only one concubine, Hagar, who is Keturah.

sources.quote: הפילגשים - הגר וקטורה
sources.says: Rashbam says the concubines were Hagar and Keturah.

25:8.headline: The word for Abraham's death is one Rashi saves for the righteous
25:8.body: Ibn Ezra says ויגוע means the spirit leaves the body in one moment, with no long suffering. Rashi, on the same word for Ishmael in verse 17, says it is said only of the righteous.

sources.quote: צאת הרוח מהגוף רגע אחד בלי עינוי ועיכוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means the spirit leaves the body in a single moment, with no suffering or delay.

sources.quote: לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה גְוִיעָה אֶלָּא בְּצַדִּיקִים
sources.says: Rashi, on Ishmael's death in verse 17, says this word is used only of the righteous.

25:8.headline: Abraham was "full" of what? Commentators give two answers
25:8.body: The verse says שבע, "satisfied", but not with what. Ramban says Abraham saw all his heart's wishes come true, while Kli Yakar says it means full of days, even though the verse does not say "days".

sources.quote: שֶׁרָאָה כָּל מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ וְשָׂבַע כָּל טוֹבָה
sources.says: Ramban says Abraham saw all his heart's wishes and was satisfied with every good thing.

sources.quote: שֶׁגַּם בְּאַבְרָהָם קָאֵי ״וְשָׂבֵעַ״ עַל הַיָּמִים
sources.says: Kli Yakar says that for Abraham too, "satisfied" refers to days.

25:21.headline: Isaac's prayer uses a word that means pressing again and again
25:21.body: Rashi says the word means he prayed a great deal and pressed hard. Rashbam says it means piling up words, and points to another verse where the same word is used that way.

sources.quote: הִרְבָּה וְהִפְצִיר בִּתְפִלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says Isaac prayed at length and pressed hard.

sources.quote: ויעתר - רבוי דברים, כדכתיב: העתרתם עלי דבריכם
sources.says: Rashbam says the word means a multiplying of words, and compares "you have multiplied your words against me".

25:22.headline: The twins "struggle" in the womb, but the word may mean "run"
25:22.body: Rashi says the sages read ויתרוצצו as ריצה, running: Jacob ran to get out when his mother passed a house of Torah, and Esau when she passed idol worship. Rashbam also takes the word from running, not from crushing.

sources.quote: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ לְשׁוֹן רִיצָה; כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה עוֹבֶרֶת עַל פִּתְחֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁל שֵׁם וָעֵבֶר יַעֲקֹב רָץ וּמְפַרְכֵּס לָצֵאת, עוֹבֶרֶת עַל פֶּתַח עֲבוֹדַת אֱלִילִים, עֵשָׂו מְפַרְכֵּס לָצֵאת
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read it as running: Jacob ran to leave at a house of Torah, and Esau at an idol house.

sources.quote: לשון רץ לקראת רץ, שהיו רצים ומתנענעים בתוך גופה כדרך עוברים
sources.says: Rashbam says it means one running toward another, as babies move about inside the mother.

25:23.headline: The written spelling of "nations" points to Rabbi and Antoninus
25:23.body: The verse is written גיים but read גוֹיִם, "nations". Radak says the sages read the written form like גאים, "proud ones", and apply it to Rabbi and Antoninus.

sources.quote: גיים כְּתִיב; אֵלּוּ אַנְטוֹנִינוּס וְרַבִּי
sources.says: Rashi says it is written גיים and refers to Antoninus and Rabbi.

sources.quote: וְדָרְשׁוּ (עבודה זרה יא) הַכְּתָב כְּמוֹ גֵּאִים, זֶהוּ רַבִּי וְאַנְטוֹנִינוּס
sources.says: Radak says the sages read the written form as גאים, "proud ones", meaning Rabbi and Antoninus.

25:23.headline: "The older shall serve the younger" can be read either way
25:23.body: The verse has no small word marking who is being served. Radak says it is unclear whether the older serves the younger or the reverse, while Ibn Ezra says the first word is the one doing the action.

sources.quote: לֹא זָכַר עִמָּהֶם מִלַּת ״אֶת״ שֶׁהִיא מוֹרָה עַל הַפָּעוּל. וְהִנֵּה הַדָּבָר מְסֻפָּק וְלֹא בֵּאֵר מִי יַעֲבֹד אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ, הָרַב אֶת הַצָּעִיר אוֹ הַצָּעִיר אֶת הָרַב
sources.says: Radak says the verse leaves out the marker for the object, so it is unclear whether the older serves the younger or the younger the older.

sources.quote: ורב. הוא הפועל וכן "בן יכבד אב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the older (רב) is the doer, as in "a son honors a father".

25:24.headline: "Twins" is spelled short here, because one twin is wicked
25:24.body: Rashi says תומם is written without an aleph, while Tamar's twins are תאומים with one. Both of hers were righteous, but here one twin was righteous and one was not.

sources.quote: חָסֵר, וּבְתָמָר תְּאוֹמִים מָלֵא, לְפִי שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם צַדִּיקִים; אֲבָל כָּאן אֶחָד צַדִּיק וְאֶחָד רָשָׁע
sources.says: Rashi says the word is short here but full for Tamar, because both of hers were righteous and here one is righteous and one wicked.

sources.quote: חָסֵר אָלֶף הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁהוּא עֵי״ן הַפֹּעַל, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָשׁ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאֶחָד צַדִּיק וְהָאֶחָד רָשָׁע
sources.says: Radak says the aleph is missing and there is a teaching in it, because one is righteous and one wicked.

25:25.headline: Esau's red color hints that he will spill blood
25:25.body: Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, says the red color was a sign Esau would shed blood (דמים). Radak notes that many babies are born red, so אדמוני must mean very red.

sources.quote: סִימָן הוּא שֶׁיְּהֵא שׁוֹפֵךְ דָּמִים
sources.says: Rashi says the red color is a sign he will be a shedder of blood.

sources.quote: וּבְרֹב הַנּוֹלָדִים יָצְאוּ אֲדֻמִּים, אֶלָּא רַצָּה לוֹמַר אַדְמוֹנִי חָזָק בְּאַדְמִימוּת
sources.says: Radak says most babies come out red, so this word means strongly red.

25:25.headline: Esau's name means "made", as if he was born fully formed
25:25.body: Rashi says everyone called him Esau because he seemed already made and finished, like a man of many years, with all his hair. Rashbam says the same: a man made and complete, with hair.

sources.quote: הַכֹּל קָרְאוּ לוֹ כֵן, לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה נַעֲשֶׂה וְנִגְמָר בִּשְׂעָרוֹ כְבֶן שָׁנִים הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says everyone called him this because he was already made and finished, with his hair, like a man of many years.

sources.quote: אדם עשוי ונגמר שהיה בעל שער
sources.says: Rashbam says the name means a man made and complete, who had hair.

25:26.headline: Jacob's name comes from the heel his hand was holding
25:26.body: The verse says his hand held Esau's heel (עקב), and then he was named יעקב. Rashi says his father named him for the grip, and Radak says the grip was also a sign that Jacob would come out on top in the end.

sources.quote: אָבִיו קָרָא לוֹ יַעֲקֹב עַל שֵׁם אֲחִיזַת הֶעָקֵב
sources.says: Rashi says one view is that his father named him Jacob for the holding of the heel.

sources.quote: זֶה הָיָה גַם כֵּן סִימָן כִּי בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה יִשְׁלֹט בְּעֵשָׂו, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָדָם שׁוֹלֵט בְּדָבָר שֶׁאוֹחֵז בְּיָדוֹ; וְעָקֵב הוּא סוֹף הַגּוּף
sources.says: Radak says the grip was a sign that Jacob would rule over Esau in the end, since the heel is the end of the body.

25:27.headline: Why "tents" is plural: Jacob sat in more than one
25:27.body: Rashi names the tent of Shem and the tent of Ever, which Bereshit Rabbah calls their houses of study. Sforno says one was a shepherd's tent and the other a tent where he learned about his Creator.

sources.quote: אָהֳלוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם וְאָהֳלוֹ שֶׁל עֵבֶר
sources.says: Rashi says the tents were the tent of Shem and the tent of Ever.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי אֹהָלִים, בֵּית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם וּבֵית מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל עֵבֶר
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says the two tents were the house of study of Shem and the house of study of Ever.

sources.quote: שְׁנֵי מִינֵי אֹהָלִים: הָאֶחָד אֹהֶל רוֹעִים, וְהַשֵּׁנִי אֹהֶל בַּל יִצְעָן (ישעיהו לג:כ), שֶׁבּוֹ הִתְבּוֹנֵן לְהַכִּיר בּוֹרְאו
sources.says: Sforno says there were two kinds of tent: a shepherd's tent and a tent where he came to know his Creator.

25:28.headline: "Game in his mouth": Isaac's mouth, or Esau's mouth?
25:28.body: Rashi follows the Aramaic translation: Isaac liked the meat in his own mouth. But the midrash says it was Esau's mouth: he trapped his father with his words.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ בְּפִיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ בְּפִיו שֶׁל עֵשָׂו, שֶׁהָיָה צָד אוֹתוֹ וּמְרַמֵּהוּ בִדְבָרָיו
sources.says: Rashi says the translation reads it as in Isaac's mouth, but the midrash reads it as Esau's mouth, with which he trapped and tricked his father.

sources.quote: אָמְרוּ הַמְּפָרְשִׁים (הראב"ע והרד"ק) כִּי יִתֵּן צַיִד בְּפִיו שֶׁל יִצְחָק אוֹ יָבִיא
sources.says: Ramban reports that Ibn Ezra and Radak read it as Esau putting or bringing game into Isaac's mouth.

25:29.headline: "Tired": worn out from murder, or just faint with hunger
25:29.body: Rashi, from Bereshit Rabbah, says Esau was "tired" from killing, as in Jeremiah 4:31. Ibn Ezra says it means faint from hunger and thirst.

sources.quote: בִּרְצִיחָה, כְּמָה דְּתֵימָא כִּי עָיְפָה נַפְשִׁי לְהֹרְגִים
sources.says: Rashi says Esau was tired from murder, as in "my soul is faint before murderers".

sources.quote: כטעם "בארץ עיפה" (ישעי, לב ב) רעב וצמא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means hunger and thirst, as in "a weary land".

25:30.headline: The nickname Edom, "red", mocks Esau for selling his birthright
25:30.body: The verse says Esau was called אדום, "red", because of the red stew. Rashbam says the name was given in scorn, and Sforno reads it as an order: "turn red".

sources.quote: הוא אדמוני ונתאווה לאכול אדום. ובשביל רעבתנותו מכר בכורתו ולשם בזיון קרא לו כן
sources.says: Rashbam says Esau was reddish and craved red food, and the name was given in scorn.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי, כְּלוֹמַר הִתְאַדֵּם וֶהְיֵה צָבוּעַ אָדוֹם בְּהַלְעָטַת הָאָדוֹם
sources.says: Sforno says the word is a command: "turn red" by gulping the red stew.

25:31.headline: "As today": "clearly" to Rashi, "right now" to Rashbam
25:31.body: Jacob tells Esau to sell the birthright כיום. Rashi says it means "as clear as day", a clear and firm sale, while Rashbam says it means "at once".

sources.quote: כַּיּוֹם שֶׁהוּא בָרוּר, כָךְ מְכֹר לִי מְכִירָה בְרוּרָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means "as the day is clear", so Esau must make a clear sale.

sources.quote: לאלתר, מיד מכור לי
sources.says: Rashbam says it means "right away, sell me now".

26:2.headline: שכן, 'dwell', also hints at שכינה, God's presence
26:2.body: The midrash splits the command. It means to set up a home in the Land, and also to make God's presence dwell in the Land. Radak says the two commands, 'dwell' and 'live as a stranger', are there to press Isaac not to leave the Land.

sources.quote: דבר אחר שכן בארץ, שכן את השכינה בארץ
sources.says: The midrash gives another reading: 'dwell in the land' means 'make the divine presence dwell in the land'.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר שכן בארץ ואחר כן אמר גור (בראשית כו:ג), לחזק לו המצוה
sources.says: Radak says that what he said, dwell in the land, and then said, 'sojourn', was to strengthen the commandment for him.

26:4.headline: והתברכו: 'bless themselves by your seed', not 'be blessed'
26:4.body: Rashi says people will use Isaac's children as the example in a blessing, saying 'may your children be like Isaac's'. Onkelos translates it as being blessed for the sake of his children.

sources.quote: אדם אומר לבנו יהא זרעך כזרעו של יצחק
sources.says: Rashi says a person says to his son, 'may your seed be like the seed of Isaac'.

sources.quote: ויתברכון בדיל בנך כל עממי ארעא
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'and all the nations of the earth will be blessed for the sake of your sons'.

26:5.headline: חקותי, 'my statutes': laws with no reason, or laws we all know
26:5.body: Rashi says חקות are the laws that have no obvious reason, like not wearing mixed wool and linen. Rashbam says in the plain reading these were the laws people already knew by reason, like theft and hospitality.

sources.quote: דברים שיצר הרע ואמות העולם משיבין עליהם, כגון אכילת חזיר ולבישת שעטנז
sources.says: Rashi says they are the things that the evil urge and the nations of the world argue with, such as eating pork and wearing mixed fabric.

sources.quote: לפי עיקר פשוטו: (מצות) הניכרות (=השכליות) כגון: גזל ועריות, וחימוד, ודינין, והכנסת אורחים
sources.says: Rashbam says that in the plain reading they are the obvious, rational commandments, such as theft, forbidden relations, coveting, courts and hospitality.

26:5.headline: ותורתי, 'my laws', is plural: the written and the oral Torah
26:5.body: The word is written in the plural. Rashi says it comes to include the oral Torah, given to Moses at Sinai. The midrash says it means two Torahs, and that Abraham kept even a small commandment of the oral one.

sources.quote: להביא תורה שבעל פה הלכה למשה מסיני
sources.says: Rashi says it comes to bring in the oral Torah, a law given to Moses at Sinai.

sources.quote: תורתי, שתי תורות, שקים אפלו מצוה קלה שבעל פה
sources.says: The midrash says תורתי means two Torahs, because he kept even a light commandment of the oral law.

26:7.headline: 'They asked him for his wife' means 'about his wife'
26:7.body: The men did not ask Isaac to give his wife. They asked him about her. Rashi and Ibn Ezra read the prefix ל as 'about', as with Abraham in Genesis 20.

sources.quote: לאשתו. על אשתו, כמו אמרי לי אחי הוא
sources.says: Rashi says לאשתו means 'about his wife', like 'say about me, he is my brother'.

sources.quote: לאשתו. בעבור אשתו כמו פן יאמרו לי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says לאשתו means 'on account of his wife', like 'lest they say of me'.

26:8.headline: 'Isaac was laughing' (יצחק מצחק): playing on his own name
26:8.body: Abimelech sees יצחק מצחק with Rebekah. Rashi and Rashbam say the verb means being intimate with his wife, as in Potiphar's wife's 'to laugh at me'. Onkelos simply translates 'laughing'.

sources.quote: וישקף אבימלך וגומר. ראהו משמש מטתו
sources.says: Rashi says Abimelech saw him being intimate with his wife.

sources.quote: מצחק - תשמיש, כדכתיב: בא אלי העבד העברי אשר הבאת לנו לצחק בי
sources.says: Rashbam says מצחק means marital relations, as in 'the Hebrew servant came to me to laugh at me'.

sources.quote: והא יצחק מחייך עם רבקה אתתיה
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'and behold, Isaac was laughing with Rebekah his wife'.

26:10.headline: 'One of the people' means the one special man, the king
26:10.body: Abimelech says one of the people nearly lay with your wife. Rashi and Sforno say 'the one of the people' is the king, the one unique man among them.

sources.quote: אחד העם. המיחד בעם, זה המלך
sources.says: Rashi says אחד העם means the one who stands out among the people, the king.

sources.quote: הוא המלך היחיד בעמו
sources.says: Sforno says it is the king, the only one in his people.

26:12.headline: 'In that land, in that year': a hard land and a hard year
26:12.body: The verse says 'that land' and 'that year', which looks repetitive. The midrash and Rashi say the point is that the land was poor and the year was a famine, and he still reaped a hundredfold.

sources.quote: בארץ ההיא בשנה ההיא. שניהם למה? לומר, שהארץ קשה והשנה קשה
sources.says: Rashi asks why both, and answers: to say the land was hard and the year was hard.

sources.quote: בארץ ההיא, בשנה ההיא, הארץ קשה והשנה קשה
sources.says: The midrash says in that land, in that year: the land was hard and the year was hard.

26:12.headline: מאה שערים, 'a hundredfold', appears only here
26:12.body: Ibn Ezra says שערים means an estimate, and he found a hundred times the amount estimated for the seed. Rashi says the field was estimated for a certain yield and gave a hundred times that.

sources.quote: שאמדוה כמה ראויה לעשות, ועשתה על אחת שאמדוה מאה
sources.says: Rashi says they estimated how much it should yield, and it yielded a hundred for each one estimated.

sources.quote: כי מצא מאה משיעור הזרע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he found a hundred times the estimate for the seed.

sources.quote: שדה ששיערוהו שיוציא כור א' הוציאה מאה כורין
sources.says: Rashbam says a field that they estimated would give one kor gave a hundred kor.

26:19.headline: 'Living water' means a spring that keeps flowing
26:19.body: Ibn Ezra says living water is water that always wells up. Radak says the verse says they found a well, not water, because they found an older well beneath where they dug.

sources.quote: מים חיים. שהם נובעים תמיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says living water is water that always wells up.

sources.quote: אחר שחפרו מצאו מתחת באר חפורה מקדם, והיו נובעים בה מים חיים, זהו שאמר וימצאו באר ולא אמרו ״וימצאו מים״
sources.says: Radak says after digging they found underneath an old dug well, with living water welling in it, which is why the verse says they found a well and not water.

26:22.headline: Rehoboth, 'wide places': the text gives the reason, and the sages go further
26:22.body: Isaac himself explains the name: God has made room for us. Radak says there was no adversary there, so they could grow. Rabbeinu Bahya says the third well points to the third Temple.

sources.quote: וקרא שמה רחבות ואמר ארי כען אפתי יי לנא
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'he called its name Rehoboth and said, for now the Lord has widened for us'.

sources.quote: כי אין שטן ומריב, ונפרה ונרבה במקנה
sources.says: Radak says there is no adversary or quarrel, and we will be fruitful and multiply in livestock.

sources.quote: על שם שכתוב בבית שלישי העתיד (יחזקאל מ״א:ז׳): ״ורחבה ונסבה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the name Rehoboth is because of the future third Temple, of which Ezekiel says it is wide.

26:23.headline: 'He went up to Beersheba': higher ground, or in fear?
26:23.body: Radak says 'went up' because the Land of Israel sits higher than the land of the Philistines. Rashbam says it was because he was afraid of them, which fits God's 'do not be afraid' that night.

sources.quote: ומה שאמר ויעל, כי ארץ ישראל המחזקת היתה גבוה מארץ פלשתים
sources.says: Radak says he said 'went up' because the main Land of Israel was higher than the land of the Philistines.

sources.quote: כי היה מתיירא מהם, שכן מוכיח שא"ל הקב"ה: אל תירא
sources.says: Rashbam says it was because he was afraid of them, as shown by God telling him 'do not fear'.

26:26.headline: אחזת: a man named Ahuzzath, or a group of his friends?
26:26.body: Radak and one sage in the midrash say Ahuzzath was a man's name. Rashi follows Onkelos and says it means a company, a group of his friends.

sources.quote: ואחזת מרעהו. כתרגומו וסיעת מרחמוהי, סיעת מאוהביו
sources.says: Rashi says as Onkelos translates it, 'and a group of his friends'.

sources.quote: שר גדול לאבימלך היה שמו אחזת
sources.says: Radak says it was the name of a great officer of Abimelech.

sources.quote: רבי יהודה אמר אחזת מרעהו היה שמו. רבי נחמיה אמר סיעת מרחמוהי
sources.says: Rabbi Yehuda says Ahuzzath was his friend's name, and Rabbi Nechemiah says it means a group of his friends.

26:28.headline: 'Between us' with an extra plural: your father and ours, and you and us
26:28.body: בינותינו is a double plural, 'between us'. Rashi says it means the oath between us and your father should hold now between us and you.

sources.quote: האלה אשר בינותינו מימי אביך תהי גם עתה בינינו וביניך
sources.says: Rashi says the oath that was between us from your father's days should now be between us and you.

sources.quote: בינותינו. ריבוי אחר רבוי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says בינותינו is a plural on top of a plural.

sources.quote: ביני ובין אביך שתתקיים גם עתה
sources.says: Rashbam says it means the oath between me and your father should be kept now too.

26:29.headline: 'You are now blessed of the Lord': a fact, or a request
26:29.body: Radak reads this as a plain statement: God makes you succeed, and you could harm us if you wanted. Rashi reads אתה as 'you too', meaning that you should do the same for us.

sources.quote: אתה. גם אתה עשה לנו כמו כן
sources.says: Rashi says אתה means you too, do the same for us.

sources.quote: כי האל מצליחך בכל דרכיך ותוכל לעשות לנו רעה אם תרצה
sources.says: Radak says God makes you succeed in all your ways and you could do us harm if you wished.

sources.quote: אתה עתה ברוך ה' - כמו כן: כרות ברית עמנו ושלחתנו בשלום
sources.says: Rashbam says it means: likewise make a pact with us and send us away in peace.

26:35.headline: מרת רוח is a word used once: bitter, rebellious, or lifting up the spirit
26:35.body: The commentators tie it to different roots. Rashi derives it from 'rebel', and Ibn Ezra from 'bitter'. The midrash plays on it too: they lifted up and removed the holy spirit from Isaac and Rebekah.

sources.quote: לשון המראות רוח, כמו ממרים הייתם
sources.says: Rashi says it is from the root for rebellion of spirit, like 'you have been rebels'.

sources.quote: כטעם מרירות נפש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is in the sense of bitterness of soul.

sources.quote: לשון מורת כמו ומורה לא יעלה על ראשו
sources.says: Sforno says מורת is like 'no razor shall come on his head'.

sources.quote: מרת רוח מרימות רוח מסלקות רוח הקדש מיצחק ומרבקה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the midrash: מרת רוח means they raised and removed the holy spirit from Isaac and Rebekah.

27:3.headline: "Lift your weapons" also means "sharpen your weapons"
27:3.body: Rashi says שא נא means "sharpen". Isaac is telling Esau to sharpen his knife and slaughter properly, so he does not feed him an animal that died unslaughtered.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן הַשְׁחָזָה, כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין, אֲבָל מַשִּׂיאָהּ עַל גַּבֵּי חֲבֶרְתָּהּ (ביצה כ"ח), חַדֵּד סַכִּינְךָ וּשְׁחֹט יָפֶה, שֶׁלֹּא תַאֲכִילֵנִי נְבֵלָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means sharpening, so Esau should sharpen his knife and slaughter well and not feed Isaac an unslaughtered carcass.

27:3.headline: תליך is used once, and is either a sword or a quiver
27:3.body: Rashi says it is a sword, since a sword is hung from the belt, and Radak says the Aramaic translation reads it that way too. Rashbam says it is the quiver that hangs with the arrows.

sources.quote: חַרְבְּךָ שֶׁדֶּרֶךְ לִתְלוֹתָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is your sword, which people hang on themselves.

sources.quote: אשפתו שתלויים בה החצים
sources.says: Rashbam says it is his quiver, in which the arrows hang.

sources.quote: וְאֻנְקְלוֹס תִּרְגֵּם ״סַיְפָך
sources.says: Radak says Onkelos translated it as "your sword".

27:3.headline: An extra ה in "game" hints at the five laws of slaughter
27:3.body: The verse is written צידה but read צָיִד, "game". Radak says the sages explained the extra ה as a hint to five laws of slaughter.

sources.quote: נִכְתַּב הַהֵ״א לִרְמֹז בָּהּ חָמֵשׁ הֲלָכוֹת שְׁחִיטָה
sources.says: Radak says the written ה hints at the five rules of slaughter, in the known teaching.

27:7.headline: Rebecca adds "before God" to what Isaac asked
27:7.body: Isaac asked only that he might bless Esau, but Rebecca adds "before God". Rashi says it means with God's approval, and Ramban says she meant the blessing would be given by the holy spirit.

sources.quote: בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ, שֶׁיַּסְכִּים עַל יָדִי
sources.says: Rashi says "before God" means with His permission, so that He agrees with me.

sources.quote: לֹא נִזְכַּר בְּכָל הַפָּרָשָׁה לִפְנֵי ה' רַק בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה, כִּי אָמְרָה לוֹ אִמּוֹ הַבְּרָכָה לִפְנֵי ה' תִּהְיֶה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶש
sources.says: Ramban says "before God" appears nowhere else in this account, because Rebecca told Jacob the blessing would be given by the holy spirit.

27:19.headline: "I am Esau your firstborn" can be split into two true statements
27:19.body: Rashi reads it as "I am the one bringing you food, and Esau is your firstborn." Ibn Ezra mentions others who said Jacob spoke softly on אנכי and raised his voice on "Esau your firstborn".

sources.quote: אָנֹכִי הַמֵּבִיא לְךָ וְעֵשָׂו הוּא בְּכוֹרֶך
sources.says: Rashi reads it as "I am the one bringing you food, and Esau is your firstborn".

sources.quote: ואחרים אמרו כי בנחת אמר אנכי, ונשא קול במלת עשו בכורך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says others held that Jacob said "I am" quietly and raised his voice at "Esau your firstborn".

27:22.headline: The "voice of Jacob" is his polite speech, and also his strength
27:22.body: Rashi says Isaac noticed Jacob's pleading words ("please get up"), where Esau would speak harshly. Bereshit Rabbah says Jacob's power is in his voice, and Esau's is in his hands.

sources.quote: שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּחֲנוּנִים קוּם נָא, אֲבָל עֵשָׂו קִנְטוּרְיָא דִּבֵּר יָקֻם אָבִי
sources.says: Rashi says the voice is Jacob's because he spoke in pleading language, "please get up", while Esau would say "let my father rise" harshly.

sources.quote: אֵין יַעֲקֹב שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא בְּקוֹלוֹ, הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו, אֵין עֵשָׂו שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא בַּיָּדָיִם
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Jacob rules only with his voice, and Esau rules only with his hands.

27:27.headline: "See the smell of my son": seeing stands in for smelling
27:27.body: Isaac says רְאֵה, "see", about a smell, and Maimonides says Hebrew often uses one sense for another, with this verse as an example. Ibn Ezra says ראה here means speaking to the heart.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 1, Chapter 46:5
sources.quote: וכן "רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי [כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה']" (בראשית כז,כז), כאילו אמר "אריח ריח בני", כי המכוון הוא השגת ריחו
sources.says: Maimonides says "see the smell of my son" is as if he said "smell", because one sense is used for another.

sources.quote: ראה. דבור עם הלב, והיה ריח טוב בבגדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ראה here is speaking to the heart, and that the clothes had a good smell.

27:28.headline: "The God" in the blessing means God as judge
27:28.body: Rashi asks why the verse says הָאֱלֹהִים, "the Elohim", and answers: God as judge, who gives only if Jacob deserves it. Maimonides notes that אלהים is also the word for judges.

sources.quote: מַהוּ הָאֱלֹהִים? בַּדִּין; אִם רָאוּי לְךָ יִתֵּן לְךָ וְאִם לָאו לֹא יִתֵּן לְך
sources.says: Rashi says "the Elohim" means in judgment: if it is fitting for you He will give, and if not He will not.

sources.ref: Guide for the Perplexed, Part 2, Chapter 6:1
sources.quote: ידוע לך כבר ש"אלהים" הוא שם השופטים
sources.says: Maimonides says אלהים is the name for judges.

27:29.headline: "Sons of your mother", because Isaac had only one wife
27:29.body: Rashi says Jacob later told Judah "sons of your father" because he had children by several wives, while Isaac had only one wife, so he says "sons of your mother". Rashbam says the same.

sources.quote: וְיַעֲקֹב אָמַר לִיהוּדָה בְּנֵי אָבִיךָ, לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָנִים מִכַּמָּה אִמָּהוֹת, וְכָאן, שֶׁלֹּא נָשָׂא אֶלָּא אִשָּׁה אַחַת, אוֹמֵר בְּנֵי אִמֶּך
sources.says: Rashi says Jacob said "sons of your father" to Judah because he had several wives, but here, with one wife, it says "sons of your mother".

sources.quote: אבל ביעקב שהיו לו נשים הרבה, כתוב בו: וישתחוו לך בני אביך
sources.says: Rashbam says Jacob had many wives, and so it says "sons of your father" there.

27:33.headline: Isaac "trembled": amazed, or seeing Gehenna open beneath him
27:33.body: Rashi says the Aramaic translation takes it as amazement, and the midrash says Isaac saw Gehenna open beneath him. Radak says he showed great fear so Esau would not think he had helped trick him.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ וּתְוַהּ, לְשׁוֹן תְּמִיהָ. וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ רָאָה גֵּיהִנֹּם פְּתוּחָה מִתַּחְתָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says the translation reads it as amazement, and the midrash says he saw Gehenna open beneath him.

sources.quote: הֶרְאָה חֲרָדָה גְּדוֹלָה בְּעַצְמוֹ בִּפְנֵי עֵשָׂו, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יַחְשֹׁב עָלָיו עֵשָׂו כִּי בְּכַוָּנָה עָשָׂה יִצְחָק מַה שֶּׁבֵּרַךְ אֶת יַעֲקֹב וְהֵתֵל בּו
sources.says: Radak says Isaac showed great fear in front of Esau so Esau would not think he had blessed Jacob on purpose and mocked him.

27:33.headline: "Who then?" or "who, where?": the little word אפוא
27:33.body: Rashi says אפוא is made of איה פה, "where here", so Isaac asks "who is he, and where?" Sforno says that spelled with an aleph it means "if so", so Isaac asks "if so, who was it?"

sources.quote: אֵיפֹה – אַיֵּה פֹה, מִי הוּא וְאֵיפֹה הוּא הַצָּד צַיִד
sources.says: Rashi says "where" is "where here", so it means "who is he and where is he, the one who hunted game".

sources.quote: כִּי אָמְנָם מִלַּת אֵיפוֹא כְּשֶׁתָּבֹא עִם אָלֶ"ף בְּסוֹף הַתֵּיבָה מְשַׁמֶּשֶׁת בִּמְקוֹם אִם כֵּן
sources.says: Sforno says that with an aleph at the end the word stands for "if so", while with a ה it means "where".

27:35.headline: "Deceit" or "wisdom"? Commentators read מרמה different ways
27:35.body: Isaac says Jacob came בְּמִרְמָה: Bereshit Rabbah has Rabbi Yochanan read it as "with the wisdom of his Torah". Ibn Ezra reads it as "not telling the truth", and Radak says it means he made his hands hairy.

sources.quote: בָּא אָחִיךָ בְּמִרְמָה, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר בָּא בְּחָכְמַת תּוֹרָתו
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says Rabbi Yochanan read "he came with deceit" as "he came with the wisdom of his Torah".

sources.quote: שלא דבר אמת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he did not speak truth.

sources.quote: שֶׁעָשָׂה יָדָיו שְׂעִירוֹת
sources.says: Radak says the deceit was that he made his hands hairy.

27:36.headline: "Is that why he is called Jacob?" or "Truly he is"
27:36.body: Rashi says הכי is a question of wonder: is it because he was named Jacob that he has now tripped me up? Ibn Ezra and Radak say it means "truly", as in "he is rightly named Jacob".

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן תֵּמַהּ הוּא, כְּמוֹ הֲכִי אָחִי אַתָּה
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of wonder, like "are you my brother?".

sources.quote: כמו אמת וכן "הכי אחי אתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means "truly", and compares it with "are you indeed my brother".

sources.quote: עַל נָכוֹן קָרָא הַקּוֹרֵא שְׁמוֹ יַעֲקֹב
sources.says: Radak says Esau means "he was rightly named Jacob".

27:36.headline: Esau hears Jacob's name inside the word "he cheated me"
27:36.body: Radak says the name יעקב holds two ideas, "heel" and "deceit", and Esau says both came true. Rashi adds that the Aramaic translation reads ויעקבני as "he lay in wait for me", and some read "he outwitted me".

sources.quote: כִּי יַעֲקֹב יֵשׁ בּוֹ שְׁנֵי עִנְיָנִים: מִן עָקֵב וּמִרְמָה, כְּמוֹ ״עָקֹב הַלֵּב״ (ירמיה יז:ט), ״כִּי כָל אָח עָקוֹב יַעְקֹב״ (ירמיה ט:ג), וּשְׁנֵיהֶם הָיוּ בו
sources.says: Radak says the name Jacob has two senses, "heel" and "deceit", and both were in him.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ וּכְמַנִי – אֲרָבַנִי; וְאָרַב – וּכְמַן. וְיֵשׁ מְתַרְגְּמִין וְחַכְּמַנִי, נִתְחַכֵּם לִי
sources.says: Rashi says the translation reads "he lay in ambush for me", and some translate "he outwitted me".

sources.quote: כמו מרמה וכן "בעקבה" (מ"ב י יט), ויתכן היותו מגזרת "עקוב הלב" (ירמי' יז ט), והעקוב הפך המישור
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means deceit, and may come from "the heart is crooked", since crooked is the opposite of straight.

27:37.headline: Isaac calls Jacob "master", so what Esau gains is Jacob's
27:37.body: Rashi says that since Isaac made Jacob a master over Esau, whatever Esau acquires belongs to Jacob, as a slave's gains belong to his master. Ramban says a master need not make others slaves.

sources.quote: אִם תִּקְנֶה נְכָסִים, שֶׁלּוֹ הֵם, שֶׁהֲרֵי גְּבִיר שַׂמְתִּיו לָךְ, וּמַה שֶּׁקָּנָה עֶבֶד קָנָה רַבּו
sources.says: Rashi says if Esau acquires property it is Jacob's, since Isaac made Jacob a master, and what a slave acquires his master acquires.

sources.quote: אֲבָל יִתָּכֵן שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הוּא הַגְּבִיר וְלֹא יִהְיוּ הֵם עֲבָדִים
sources.says: Ramban says it is possible that Jacob would be the master without the brothers being slaves.

27:40.headline: תריד can mean "you rule" or "you grieve"
27:40.body: Rashi says תריד means to be distressed, as in אריד בשיחי, "I moan in my complaint". Ibn Ezra says it is either like תרדה, "you will rule", or the same sense Rashi gives.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן צַעַר כְּמוֹ אָרִיד בְּשִׂיחִי
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of distress, like "I will moan in my complaint".

sources.quote: כמו תרדה והם ב' שרשים, וי"א כמו "אריד בשיחי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like תרדה, from a different root, and others say it is like "I moan in my complaint".

27:42.headline: Esau "consoles himself" with the thought of killing Jacob
27:42.body: נחם can mean comfort or a change of heart. Rashi gives several readings, including a change of heart about being a brother and comfort in the killing, and Ibn Ezra says his comfort is that he can kill you.

sources.quote: נִחָם עַל הָאַחְוָה לַחֲשֹׁב מַחֲשָׁבָה אַחֶרֶת לְהִתְנַכֵּר לְךָ וּלְהָרְגְּךָ. וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה כְּבָר אַתָּה מֵת בְּעֵינָיו וְשָׁתָה עָלֶיךָ כּוֹס שֶׁל תַּנְחוּמִים. וּלְפִי פְּשׁוּטוֹ לְשׁוֹן תַּנְחוּמִים, מִתְנַחֵם הוּא עַל הַבְּרָכוֹת בַּהֲרִיגָתְך
sources.says: Rashi gives several readings: a change of heart about brotherhood, the cup of consolation for one already dead, or comfort over the blessings by killing him.

sources.quote: זאת היא נחמתו שיוכל להרגך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says his comfort is that he will be able to kill you.

28:3.headline: Rashi hears the name שדי as 'the one who has enough'
28:3.body: Rashi splits שדי into two small words, ש (who) and די (enough). So Isaac blesses Jacob in the name of the God who has enough for everyone He blesses.

sources.quote: ואל שדי. מִי שֶׁדַּי בְּבִרְכוֹתָיו לַמִּתְבָּרְכִין מִפִּיו
sources.says: Rashi reads שדי as 'the one who has enough (די) in His blessings for those blessed by His word'.

sources.quote: מי שיש די באלהותו לכל הבריות יברך אותך
sources.says: Chizkuni reads it the same way: the one who has enough in His divinity for all creatures.

28:5.headline: Rashi cannot say why 'mother of Jacob and Esau' is added
28:5.body: Rashi says he does not know why 'mother of Jacob and Esau' is added after Rebecca. Chizkuni answers that most sons take after their mother's brother, and Esau took after Laban.

sources.quote: אם יעקב ועשו. אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַה מְּלַמְּדֵנוּ
sources.says: Rashi says he does not know what the words 'mother of Jacob and Esau' teach us.

sources.quote: רוב הבנים דומים לאחי האם, עשו דומה אל לבן אחי אמו
sources.says: Chizkuni says most sons resemble their mother's brother, and Esau resembled his mother's brother Laban.

28:10.headline: Why the verse says Jacob 'went out' and not just 'went'
28:10.body: The verse could have said only that Jacob went to Haran. Rashi says the extra 'went out' shows that when a righteous person leaves a town, the town loses its glory and beauty.

sources.quote: מַגִּיד שֶׁיְּצִיאַת צַדִּיק מִן הַמָּקוֹם עוֹשָׂה רֹשֶׁם, שֶׁבִּזְמַן שֶׁהַצַּדִּיק בָּעִיר, הוּא הוֹדָהּ הוּא זִיוָהּ הוּא הֲדָרָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says the departure of a righteous person leaves a mark, because while he is in the city he is its splendor, its radiance and its glory.

28:11.headline: Rashi: the sun set suddenly and early, only for Jacob
28:11.body: The verse could have said 'the sun set'. Rashi says the wording 'the sun came' means it set suddenly, before its time, so that Jacob would have to stay the night.

sources.quote: כִּי בָא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ מַשְׁמַע שֶׁשָּׁקְעָה לוֹ חַמָּה פִּתְאוֹם, שֶׁלֹּא בְּעוֹנָתָהּ, כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּלִין שָׁם
sources.says: Rashi says the wording means the sun set on him suddenly, out of its time, so that he would stay there overnight.

28:11.headline: 'He lay down in that place' hints he lay down nowhere else
28:11.body: Rashi and Bahya both read the wording as limiting. Jacob lay down in that place, but in the fourteen years he spent studying in the house of Eber he did not lie down at night.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן מִעוּט; בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם שָׁכַב אֲבָל י"ד שָׁנִים שֶׁשִּׁמֵּשׁ בְּבֵית עֵבֶר לֹא שָׁכַב בַּלַּיְלָה, שֶׁהָיָה עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the wording is one of limiting: he lay in that place, but not in the fourteen years at Eber's house, because he was busy with Torah.

sources.quote: הָיָה רָאוּי לוֹמַר ״וַיִּשְׁכַּב שָׁם״ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר ״וַיָּלֶן שָׁם״, אֲבָל לְשׁוֹן מִעוּט הוּא
sources.says: Bahya says the verse should have said 'lay there', as it said 'stayed there', so the wording is a limiting one.

28:14.headline: ונברכו may mean 'will be grafted in', not only 'will be blessed'
28:14.body: Rashbam links the verb to the words for layering and grafting a vine. So the families of the earth will mix into Jacob's family.

sources.quote: ונברכו - לשון מבריך ומרכיב. כלומר: יתערבו במשפחתך משפחות האדמה
sources.says: Rashbam says the word is of the kind meaning to layer and graft, that is, the families of the earth will mix into your family.

28:15.headline: In 'until I have done', the word אם does not mean 'if'
28:15.body: אם usually means 'if', but Rashi says here it works like כי, so God means 'until I have done what I promised'. Radak says the doubled words אשר אם make the promise stronger.

sources.quote: אִם מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בִּלְשׁוֹן כִּי
sources.says: Rashi says אם is used here in the sense of כי.

sources.quote: כֶּפֶל עִנְיָן לְחַזֵּק הַדָּבָר, כִּי דַּי לוֹ בַּאֲשֶׁר אוֹ בְּאִם
sources.says: Radak says the two words repeat the same idea to strengthen the statement, since either אשר or אם alone would be enough.

28:19.headline: Why the verse tells us the city was first called לוז
