sources.says: Maimonides quotes the sages telling of Manasseh the wicked, who said Moses should only have written 'and Lotan's sister was Timna'.

36:24.headline: הימם is a word found only here: mules, giants, or fierce beasts?
36:24.body: Rashi says it means mules, since Anah bred a donkey with a mare, and Ibn Ezra links it to the Emim, an old race of giants in Deuteronomy. Rashbam says it means heroes or wild beasts that Anah beat.

sources.quote: פְּרָדִים, הִרְבִּיעַ חֲמוֹר עַל סוּס נְקֵבָה וְיָלְדָה פֶּרֶד
sources.says: Rashi says it means mules: he bred a donkey with a female horse, and she bore a mule.

sources.quote: הימים., כמו "האימים לפנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הימים is like 'the Emim of old'.

sources.quote: הגיבורים או חיות רעות ונצחם
sources.says: Rashbam says it means the heroes or the wild animals, and he defeated them.

36:31.headline: Why list the kings of Edom?
36:31.body: Maimonides says it is tied to the law that Israel may not set a foreigner as king, since none of Edom's kings came from Edom itself, and Radak says they were men brought in from other places. Rashi counts eight Edomite kings against eight kings of Jacob's line.

sources.quote: והמלכים הללו שהזכיר – אין מהם אחד מאדום
sources.says: Maimonides says that of these kings he mentioned, not one is from Edom.

sources.quote: וְהַמְּלָכִים לֹא הָיוּ מֶלֶךְ בֶּן מֶלֶךְ, אֶלָּא שֶׁהָיוּ מוֹלִיכִים עֲלֵיהֶם מְלָכִים מִמְּקוֹמוֹת אֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Radak says the kings were not each the son of a king, but they brought kings over themselves from other places.

sources.quote: שְׁמוֹנָה הָיוּ וּכְנֶגְדָּן הֶעֱמִיד יַעֲקֹב וּבִטֵּל מַלְכוּת עֵשָׂו בִּימֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says there were eight, and against them Jacob raised up eight and ended Esau's kingship in their days.

36:39.headline: מי זהב: a man so rich that gold meant nothing
36:39.body: Rashi says the man behind the name מי זהב was so rich that gold was worth nothing to him, and Bahya says he spent his life refining gold, which flowed through his house like water. Ibn Ezra says it was simply his name.

sources.quote: מַהוּ זָהָב? עָשִׁיר הָיָה, וְאֵין זָהָב חָשׁוּב בְּעֵינָיו לִכְלוּם
sources.says: Rashi asks what 'gold' is, and answers that he was rich and gold meant nothing to him.

sources.quote: בַּת עָשִׁיר שֶׁהָיָה כָּל יָמָיו טָרוּד לְצָרֵף זָהָב וְהָיָה הַזָּהָב הוֹלֵךְ בְּבֵיתוֹ כַּמַּיִם
sources.says: Bahya says she was a rich man's daughter, who was busy all his days refining gold, and the gold went through his house like water.

sources.quote: מי זהב. כן שמו והגאון אמר צורף זהב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was his name, and the Gaon said it means a refiner of gold.

36:43.headline: Rashi says מגדיאל is Rome; Ramban says he does not follow
36:43.body: In the list of Edom's chiefs, Rashi says מגדיאל is the name for Rome, but Ramban says he does not understand this, since Rome is a great empire and not a chief. He then says the name hints at a later kingdom that will grow great.

sources.quote: מגדיאל. הִיא רוֹמִי
sources.says: Rashi says מגדיאל is Rome.

sources.quote: מַגְדִּיאֵל זוֹ רוֹמִי, לְשׁוֹן רַשִׁ"י. וְלֹא הֲבִינוֹתִי זֶה
sources.says: Ramban says: 'Magdiel is Rome', as Rashi wrote, and says he did not understand it.

sources.quote: וְלָזֶה יִרְמֹז שֵׁם מַגְדִּיאֵל, שֶׁיִּתְגַּדֵּל עַל כָּל אֵל
sources.says: Ramban says the name מגדיאל hints that it will grow great above every god.

37:1.headline: 'Settled' hints that Jacob wanted to settle in peace
37:1.body: Rashi passes on a teaching that וישב, 'he settled,' also means Jacob wanted to settle in ease. Then Joseph's trouble leapt on him.

sources.quote: וְעוֹד נִדְרָשׁ בּוֹ וישב, בִּקֵּשׁ יַעֲקֹב לֵישֵׁב בְּשַׁלְוָה, קָפַץ עָלָיו רָגְזוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read וישב as Jacob seeking to settle in peace, and Joseph's trouble jumped on him.

37:2.headline: 'Toldot' here means what happened to Jacob, not only his children
37:2.body: Radak says תולדות here means קורות, the events of a life, as in 'you do not know what a day will bring.' Ibn Ezra reads it the same way.

sources.quote: תּוֹלְדוֹת זֶה, פֵּרוּשׁוֹ קוֹרוֹת
sources.says: Radak says תולדות here means קורות, events.

sources.quote: אלו המאורעות שאירעו לו, והמקרים שבאו עליו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says these are the events and happenings that came on Jacob.

37:2.headline: 'Lad' describes how Joseph acted, not only how old he was
37:2.body: Joseph was seventeen. Rashi says נער also tells how he behaved: like a boy, fixing his hair and touching up his eyes to look good.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה עוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֵׂה נַעֲרוּת, מְתַקֵּן בִּשְׂעָרוֹ, מְמַשְׁמֵשׁ בְּעֵינָיו, כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נִרְאֶה יָפֶה
sources.says: Rashi says Joseph acted like a boy, fixing his hair and touching his eyes so he would look handsome.

37:2.headline: Rashi ties דבה, 'bad report,' to a verb for moving the lips
37:2.body: Rashi says דבה comes from דובב, as in 'moving the lips of those who sleep' in Song of Songs. It is about talk: Joseph told his father whatever bad he could say of them.

sources.quote: דבה. לְשׁוֹן דּוֹבֵב שִׂפְתֵי יְשֵׁנִים
sources.says: Rashi says דבה is a form of דובב, as in 'moving the lips of sleepers.'

sources.quote: כָּל מַה שֶּׁהָיָה יָכוֹל לְדַבֵּר בָּהֶם רָעָה, הָיָה מְסַפֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says Joseph reported anything bad he could say about them.

37:3.headline: 'Son of old age' may mean 'a wise son'
37:3.body: Rashi says it means Jacob had him in old age, and also quotes Onkelos, who has 'a wise son.' Radak asks how Joseph was a son of old age when his brothers were born within seven years of him, and answers: he was as wise as an old man.

sources.quote: וְאֻנְקְלוֹס תִּרְגֵּם בַּר חַכִּים הוּא לֵהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Onkelos translates it 'he is a wise son to him.'

sources.quote: כִּי הָיָה מוֹצְאוֹ חָכָם בְּכָל דְּבָרָיו כְּמוֹ אִם הָיָה זָקֵן
sources.says: Radak says Joseph turned out wise in everything, as if he were old.

37:4.headline: 'Dabbero' means 'speak to him,' and shows the brothers were honest
37:4.body: The ending ו here means 'to him,' not 'his.' Rashi says the brothers' hatred still teaches something good about them: they did not say one thing and mean another.

sources.quote: דברו. לְדַבֵּר עִמּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says דברו means to speak with him.

sources.quote: דברו. כמו דבר לו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says דברו is like 'to speak to him.'

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא דִבְּרוּ אַחַת בַּפֶּה וְאַחַת בַּלֵּב
sources.says: Rashi says from their faults we learn their good: they did not speak one thing with the mouth and another with the heart.

37:10.headline: 'He rebuked him' can mean shame, or ruin, depending on one letter
37:10.body: Ibn Ezra says גערה with the letter ב means shaming, and without it means ruining, as in Malachi 2:3. Here the verse says גער בו, with ב.

sources.quote: גערה אם בי"ת דרך קלון, ובלא בי"ת לשון השחתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says גערה with a ב is a way of disgrace, and without a ב it means destruction.

37:11.headline: 'Kept the matter' means kept in mind, or waited for it
37:11.body: Jacob scolded Joseph but still 'kept' the dream. Rashi says שמר means he waited and watched for it to come, while Ibn Ezra says he kept it in his heart.

sources.quote: הָיָה מַמְתִּין וּמְצַפֶּה מָתַי יָבֹא, וְכֵן שֹׁמֵר אֱמֻנִים
sources.says: Rashi says Jacob was waiting and watching for when the dream would come.

sources.quote: שמר את הדבר. בלבו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he kept the matter in his heart.

37:12.headline: Dots over the word את hint the brothers fed only themselves
37:12.body: The Torah scroll puts dots over את, 'the' marker before 'the flock.' Rashi reads them as a hint: the brothers went to feed themselves, not their father's sheep.

sources.quote: נָקוּד עַל אֶת, שֶׁלֹּא הָלְכוּ אֶלָּא לִרְעוֹת אֶת עַצְמָן
sources.says: Rashi says there are dots over את, because they went only to feed themselves.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא הָלְכוּ אֶלָּא לִרְעוֹת אֶת עַצְמָם
sources.says: Radak quotes Bereshit Rabbah that they went only to feed themselves.

37:14.headline: 'From the valley of Hebron' hints at a deep plan
37:14.body: Hebron is on a mountain, so why a valley (עמק)? Rashi hears עמוקה, deep: Joseph was sent from the deep plan of the righteous man buried in Hebron, Abraham, that his children would be strangers.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא מֵעֵצָה עֲמֻקָּה שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק הַקָּבוּר בְּחֶבְרוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the 'valley' hints at the deep counsel of the righteous man buried in Hebron.

37:14.headline: Shechem is a place where trouble keeps happening
37:14.body: Rashi calls Shechem a place 'ready for punishment.' The tribes went wrong there, Dinah was abused there, and David's kingdom split there.

sources.quote: מָקוֹם מוּכָן לְפֻרְעָנוּת, שָׁם קִלְקְלוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים, שָׁם עִנּוּ אֶת דִּינָה, שָׁם נֶחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד
sources.says: Rashi says Shechem is a place ready for punishment: the tribes sinned there, Dinah was abused there, and David's kingdom was divided there.

37:15.headline: The unnamed 'man' who finds Joseph is the angel Gabriel
37:15.body: The verse only says a man found him wandering. Rashi says this was Gabriel; Maimonides, in the Guide for the Perplexed, sets it beside the angel who found Hagar and says all the midrashim call him an angel.

sources.quote: זֶה גַּבְרִיאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְהָאִישׁ גַּבְרִיאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says the man is Gabriel, as it says 'the man Gabriel.'

sources.quote: וַיִּמְצָאֵהוּ אִישׁ וְהִנֵּה תֹעֶה בַּשָּׂדֶה [וַיִּשְׁאָלֵהוּ הָאִישׁ לֵאמֹר מַה תְּבַקֵּשׁ]" (שם לז,טו), ולשון כל המדרשות, שהוא מלאך
sources.says: Maimonides cites 'a man found him wandering' and says the language of all the midrashim is that he was an angel.

37:17.headline: 'They have journeyed' also means they left brotherhood
37:17.body: The man says the brothers 'journeyed from here.' Rashi hears more: they pulled themselves away from brotherhood.

sources.quote: נסעו מזה. הִסִּיעוּ עַצְמָן מִן הָאַחְוָה
sources.says: Rashi says they moved themselves away from the brotherhood.

37:17.headline: 'To Dothan' also sounds like 'by legal tricks'
37:17.body: Rashi hears דתות, laws or decrees, inside דתינה: they were going to look for legal schemes to put Joseph to death. He adds that the plain sense is a place name.

sources.quote: לְבַקֵּשׁ לְךָ נִכְלֵי דָתוֹת שֶׁיְּמִיתוּךָ בָהֶם. וּלְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ שֵׁם מָקוֹם הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says they were seeking schemes of decrees to kill him, but the plain meaning is that it is a place name.

37:19.headline: 'That one over there' is used for someone seen far away
37:19.body: The brothers see Joseph coming from a distance. Rashbam says הלזה is used when you see someone from afar, while הזה is for someone close.

sources.quote: כל הלזה כשרואים אותו מרחוק
sources.says: Rashbam says הלזה is used when you see someone from a distance.

37:24.headline: 'Empty' does not mean the pit had nothing in it
37:24.body: The verse says the pit was empty, then adds there was no water. Rashi asks why, and answers: no water, but snakes and scorpions were there.

sources.quote: מַיִם אֵין בּוֹ, אֲבָל נְחָשִׁים וְעַקְרַבִּים יֵשׁ בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says there was no water in it, but there were snakes and scorpions.

37:25.headline: The verse lists the cargo to show how God rewards the righteous
37:25.body: Rashi asks why the Torah tells what the camels carried. His answer: Arab caravans usually carry foul-smelling goods, but this one carried spices, so Joseph was spared a bad smell.

sources.quote: לְהוֹדִיעַ מַתַּן שְׂכָרָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים, שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכָּן שֶׁל עַרְבִיִּים לָשֵׂאת אֶלָּא נֵפְטְ וְעִטְרָן, שֶׁרֵיחָן רַע
sources.says: Rashi says it shows the reward of the righteous, since Arab caravans carry only naphtha and tar, which smell bad.

37:28.headline: Midianites or Ishmaelites? Joseph may have been sold more than once
37:28.body: Rashi says the Midianites were a second caravan, so Joseph was sold several times. Ibn Ezra says Midianites are also called Ishmaelites, so the verse speaks of one group.

sources.quote: זוֹ הִיא שַׁיָּרָה אַחֶרֶת, וְהוֹדִיעֲךָ הַכָּתוּב שֶׁנִּמְכַּר פְּעָמִים הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says this is another caravan, and the verse teaches that Joseph was sold many times.

sources.quote: כי המדינים יקראו ישמעאלים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Midianites are called Ishmaelites.

37:29.headline: 'Reuben returned' shows he was away when Joseph was sold
37:29.body: The verb 'returned' implies Reuben had left. Rashi says he was away serving his father, or fasting in sackcloth for disturbing his father's bed.

sources.quote: בִּמְכִירָתוֹ לֹא הָיָה שָׁם, שֶׁהִגִּיעַ יוֹמוֹ לֵילֵךְ וּלְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת אָבִיו
sources.says: Rashi says Reuben was not there for the sale, because his day had come to go and serve his father.

sources.quote: עָסוּק הָיָה בְשַׂקּוֹ וּבְתַעֲנִיתוֹ עַל שֶׁבִּלְבֵּל יְצוּעֵי אָבִיו
sources.says: Rashi says another view is that he was busy with his sackcloth and fasting for having disturbed his father's bed.

37:31.headline: Why a goat? Its blood looks like human blood
37:31.body: Rashi says the brothers chose a goat because its blood looks like a man's. In the Guide for the Perplexed, Maimonides reports the sages' view that Israel's sin offerings are goats because the first sin of the whole people involved a goat: the sale of Joseph.

sources.quote: דָּמוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְשֶׁל אָדָם
sources.says: Rashi says its blood looks like a man's.

sources.quote: חטאם של כל עדת ישראל היה תחילה בשעיר עזים, ברמיזה למכירת יוסף הצדיק
sources.says: Maimonides says the sages explain that the sin of all Israel began with a goat, a hint at the sale of Joseph.

37:32.headline: Judah's 'please identify' comes back to him through Tamar
37:32.body: Judah tells Jacob הכר נא, 'please identify this.' The sages say God answered: you said it to your father, and Tamar will say הכר נא to you. That happens in Genesis 38:25.

sources.quote: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִיהוּדָה אַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says God said to Judah, in effect, that he was the one who said 'please identify' to his father.

sources.quote: חַיֶּיךָ שֶׁתָּמָר אוֹמֶרֶת לְךָ
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says God told Judah, 'by your life,' Tamar would say it to him.

sources.quote: אַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ לְאָבִיךָ הַכֶּר־נָא, חַיֶּיךָ שֶׁתֹּאמַר לְךָ ״הַכֶּר־נָא
sources.says: Radak repeats this saying from Bereshit Rabbah.

37:33.headline: Jacob's 'wild animal' hints at Potiphar's wife
37:33.body: Jacob says a wild beast ate Joseph. The sages say holy spirit flashed in his words: the 'beast' was Potiphar's wife, who would later go after Joseph.

sources.quote: נִצְנְצָה בוֹ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, סוֹפוֹ שֶׁתִּתְגָּרֶה בוֹ אֵשֶׁת פּוֹטִיפַר
sources.says: Rashi says holy spirit flashed in him, since in the end Potiphar's wife would provoke Joseph.

sources.quote: חַיָּה רָעָה אֲכָלָתְהוּ, זוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁל פּוֹטִיפַר
sources.says: Bereshit Rabbah says the wild beast that ate him is Potiphar's wife.

37:35.headline: Jacob has one known daughter, so who are 'all his daughters'?
37:35.body: Rabbi Judah says twin sisters were born with each tribe. Rabbi Nehemiah says it means his sons' wives, since people call a daughter-in-law 'daughter.'

sources.quote: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֲחָיוֹת תְּאוֹמוֹת נוֹלְדוּ עִם כָּל שֵׁבֶט וָשֵׁבֶט וּנְשָׂאוּם
sources.says: Rashi says Rabbi Judah held that twin sisters were born with each tribe, and the brothers married them.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵין אָדָם נִמְנָע מִלִּקְרֹא לַחֲתָנוֹ בְּנוֹ וּלְכַלָּתוֹ בִתּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says Rabbi Nehemiah's view is that no one refrains from calling a son-in-law 'son' and a daughter-in-law 'daughter.'

37:35.headline: שאלה can mean the grave, or Gehenna
37:35.body: Rashi says the plain sense is the grave, and the midrash reads it as Gehenna. Ibn Ezra says it means the grave, and says the translator who wrote Gehenna erred.

sources.quote: כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ לְשׁוֹן קֶבֶר הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says that in its plain sense the word means a grave.

sources.quote: והטעם הקבר ופה טעה המתרגם לתועים שתרגם שאולה גיהנם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning is the grave, and that the translator who rendered it Gehenna erred.

37:35.headline: 'His father wept' means Isaac, not Jacob
37:35.body: The verse says 'his father wept.' Rashi says this is Isaac, who wept at Jacob's pain but did not mourn, because he knew Joseph was alive.

sources.quote: יִצְחָק, בּוֹכֶה הָיָה מִפְּנֵי צָרָתוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב אֲבָל לֹא הָיָה מִתְאַבֵּל, שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא חַי
sources.says: Rashi says Isaac wept for Jacob's trouble but did not mourn, since he knew Joseph was alive.

37:36.headline: 'Chief of the butchers' can mean cooks or executioners
37:36.body: Rashi says it means slaughterers of the king's animals, and Ibn Ezra says the word is used for killing and for cooking. Onkelos has 'chief of the killers.'

sources.quote: שׁוֹחֲטֵי בְּהֵמוֹת הַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it means slaughterers of the king's animals.

sources.quote: תמצא זה הלשון על הרג ועל בישול
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says you find this word for killing and for cooking.

sources.quote: רַבָּא דְפַרְעֹה רַב קָטוֹלַיָּא
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as chief of the killers.

38:1.headline: 'Judah went down' also means he fell from his standing
38:1.body: Adullam lies lower than where Judah was, so Radak says וירד fits the land. The midrash adds that his brothers brought him down from his greatness after he talked them into selling Joseph.

sources.quote: לְלַמֵּד שֶׁהוֹרִידוּהוּ אֶחָיו מִגְּדֻלָּתוֹ כְּשֶׁרָאוּ בְצָרַת אֲבִיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that his brothers brought him down from his greatness when they saw their father's grief.

sources.quote: וּבְאָמְרוֹ וַיֵּרֶד נִרְאֶה כִּי מִדּוֹתָן לַעֲדֻלָּם הוּא יְרִידָה
sources.says: Radak says the word וירד shows that the way to Adullam is a descent.

38:2.headline: 'A Canaanite' may mean 'a merchant'
38:2.body: Onkelos translates כנעני as תגרא, a trader. Rashi follows this, and so does Rashbam, who points to 'Canaan, in his hand are false scales' in Hosea 12:8.

sources.quote: כנעני. תַּגְרָא
sources.says: Rashi says כנעני means a merchant.

sources.quote: כתרגומו תגרא. כמו: כנעניה נכבדי ארץ
sources.says: Rashbam says it is as Onkelos translates, a merchant, like 'her merchants are the honored of the land.'

38:3.headline: The name Er means 'stir up' and hints at his death
38:3.body: Ramban says Judah named him ער from עוררה, 'stir up your might,' in Psalms. The sages also hear 'he was cut off from the world,' though Ramban says Judah did not mean that.

sources.quote: יְהוּדָה קָרָא לִבְנוֹ עֵר, מִלְּשׁוֹן "עוֹרְרָה אֶת גְּבוּרָתֶךָ
sources.says: Ramban says Judah named his son ער from the phrase 'stir up your might.'

sources.quote: אָמְרוּ, עֵר שֶׁהוּעַר מִן הָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Ramban says Bereshit Rabbah reads ער as one who was uprooted from the world.

38:5.headline: Shelah may be a sad name, from 'do not deceive'
38:5.body: Sforno ties שלה to אל תשלה, 'do not deceive me,' in Kings. He calls it an unfitting name, one Judah would not have agreed to if he had been there.

sources.quote: וְהַטַּעַם שֶׁקְּרָאַתּוּ שֵׁלָה לְשׁוֹן "אַל תַּשְׁלֶה
sources.says: Sforno says she called him שלה from the phrase 'do not deceive.'

38:7.headline: Er's 'evil' is named: he wasted his seed
38:7.body: The verse only says Er was evil in God's eyes. Rashi says his evil was like Onan's: he destroyed his seed so that his wife would not conceive and lose her beauty.

sources.quote: וְלָמָּה הָיָה עֵר מַשְׁחִית זַרְעוֹ? כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תִּתְעַבֵּר וְיַכְחִישׁ יָפְיָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Er destroyed his seed so she would not become pregnant and lose her beauty.

38:8.headline: 'Marry her as brother-in-law' was an old custom before the Torah
38:8.body: Judah tells Onan to marry his brother's widow. Radak and Maimonides both say this was an old custom before the Torah, which the Torah kept.

sources.quote: נִרְאֶה כִּי הַדָּבָר שֶׁל יִבּוּם הָיָה מִשְׁפַּט הַקַּדְמוֹנִים קֹדֶם שֶׁנִּתְּנָה הַתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Radak says it seems that levirate marriage was the law of the ancients before the Torah was given.

sources.quote: מפורש במקרא (בראשית לח,ח) שהיה זה מנהג קדום לפני מתן תורה, שהתורה השאירה אותו
sources.says: Maimonides says it is stated in Scripture that this was an ancient custom before the Torah was given, which the Torah left in place.

38:13.headline: 'Went up' to Timnah, but Samson 'went down' to Timnah
38:13.body: Rashi notices that Samson is said to go down to Timnah, but Judah goes up. His answer: Timnah sat on a mountain slope, so you go up from one side and down from the other.

sources.quote: בְּשִׁפּוּעַ הָהָר הָיְתָה יוֹשֶׁבֶת, עוֹלִין לָהּ מִכָּאן וְיוֹרְדִין לָהּ מִכָּאן
sources.says: Rashi says Timnah sat on the slope of a hill, so people go up to it from one side and down to it from the other.

sources.quote: וַיֵּרֶד תִּמְנָתָה״ (שופטים יד:א), כָּל אֶחָד לְפִי הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ
sources.says: Radak says Samson 'went down' to Timnah, each according to where he came from.

38:14.headline: The rare verb ותתעלף means she hid her face
38:14.body: Rashi says she covered her face so Judah would not know her. Ibn Ezra says the same and compares it to Jonah 4:8, where a man hides his face in his clothes.

sources.quote: כִּסְּתָה פָנֶיהָ, שֶׁלֹּא יַכִּיר בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says she covered her face so that he would not recognize her.

sources.quote: טעמו שהסתירה פניה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says its meaning is that she hid her face.

38:14.headline: 'Opening of the eyes': a crossroads, a spring, or a place
38:14.body: Rashi reads it as an open crossroads, and adds that the sages heard in it Abraham's doorway, where all eyes looked for him. Ibn Ezra says it may be a place name or two springs, and Rashbam says it is not a city.

sources.quote: בִּפְתִיחַת עֵינַיִם, בְּפָרָשַׁת דְּרָכִים שֶׁעַל דֶּרֶךְ תִּמְנָתָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means an opening of eyes, at a crossroads on the way to Timnah.

sources.quote: שם מקום, וי"א כי שני מעינות מים הי' בדרך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a place name, and some say there were two springs of water on the road.

sources.quote: בשער של פרשת דרכים שהכל עוברים ונראים לעינים דרך שם
sources.says: Rashbam says it is a gateway at a crossroads, where everyone passes and is seen.

38:15.headline: Why would a covered face make Judah think 'harlot'?
38:15.body: Rashi gives the plain sense: he could not see her face to know her. The sages add that she had been modest in her father-in-law's house, so he never suspected her.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁהָיְתָה בְּבֵית חָמִיהָ הָיְתָה צְנוּעָה, לְפִיכָךְ לֹא חֲשָׁדָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says that when she was in her father-in-law's house she was modest, so he did not suspect her.

38:18.headline: פתיל, Judah's pledge, is a cloak, a belt, or a scarf
38:18.body: Rashi says it is a garment you wrap yourself in, and Rashbam says it is a belt. Ramban asks how a cloak could be called פתיל, and offers a small head scarf.

sources.quote: עִזְקְתָךְ וְשׁוֹשִׁיפָּךְ – טַבַּעַת שֶׁאַתָה חוֹתֵם בָּהּ וְשִׂמְלָתְךָ שֶׁאַתָּה מִתְכַּסֶּה בָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is your ring you seal with and your garment you cover yourself with.

sources.quote: פתילך - אזור
sources.says: Rashbam says פתילך means a belt.

sources.quote: וְאֵיךְ תִּקָּרֵא הַשִּׂמְלָה פְּתִיל
sources.says: Ramban asks how a garment could be called a פתיל.

38:21.headline: קדשה, a woman set apart for hire, is a rare word
38:21.body: Rashi says it means a woman set aside and ready for immoral use. Rashbam says she is set aside for anyone who comes, and adds that such a woman should not be among Israel's daughters.

sources.quote: מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת וּמְזֻמֶּנֶת לִזְנוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it means one set apart and made ready for immorality.

sources.quote: מיועדת ומזומנת לכל באיה
sources.says: Rashbam says she is set aside and ready for all who come to her.

38:23.headline: Judah fooled his father with a goat, and a goat fools him
38:23.body: Judah had dipped Joseph's coat in goat's blood to deceive Jacob. The sages say Judah is now deceived through a young goat of his own.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁרִמָּה יְהוּדָה אֶת אָבִיו בִּגְדִי עִזִּים שֶׁהִטְבִּיל כְּתֹנֶת יוֹסֵף בְּדָמוֹ, רִמּוּהוּ גַּם הוּא בִּגְדִי עִזִּים
sources.says: Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, says that because Judah deceived his father with goats, he too was deceived with goats.

38:23.headline: 'Lest we be shamed': Judah prefers losing the pledge to gossip
38:23.body: Rashi says that if he kept searching, the matter would become public and a disgrace. Maimonides reads Judah's words as a lesson in modesty: it is shameful to talk about such matters, even permitted ones, even at a loss of money.

sources.quote: אִם תְּבַקְּשֶׁנָּה עוֹד יִתְפַּרְסֵם הַדָּבָר וְיִהְיֶה גְּנַאי
sources.says: Rashi says if he searched for her more, the matter would become known and be shameful.

sources.quote: שחרפה היא לנו לדבר על כל ענייני יחסי המין, אפילו המותרים מהם
sources.says: Maimonides says Judah's words teach that it is a disgrace to speak of all matters of intimacy, even permitted ones.

38:24.headline: Why burning? The sages say Tamar was a priest's daughter
38:24.body: Rashi says Tamar was the daughter of Shem, who was a priest, and a priest's daughter is burned. Rashbam gives a plain reason: it was their custom, since she was waiting for a brother-in-law.

sources.quote: בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם הָיְתָה, שֶׁהוּא כֹהֵן, לְפִיכָךְ דָּנוּהָ בִשְׂרֵפָה
sources.says: Rashi says she was the daughter of Shem, who was a priest, so they judged her to be burned.

sources.quote: מאחר שזקוקה ליבם
sources.says: Rashbam says it was their custom, since she was bound to a brother-in-law.

38:25.headline: Tamar will not name Judah, so she will not shame him
38:25.body: Tamar sends the pledges with 'to the man whose these are.' Rashi says she would not shame Judah by naming him: if he admitted it, fine, and if not, she would be burned.

sources.quote: לֹא רָצְתָה לְהַלְבִּין פָּנָיו וְלוֹמַר מִמְּךָ אֲנִי מְעֻבֶּרֶת, אֶלָּא לְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אֵלֶּה לּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says she did not want to shame him by saying she was pregnant by him, so she said 'by the man whose these are.'

38:25.headline: Tamar says to Judah the same words he said to Jacob
38:25.body: Tamar says הכר נא, 'please identify,' the very words Judah said to Jacob over Joseph's coat. The sages say the Torah repays him in kind, and Rashi adds that נא is a plea: 'recognize your Creator.'

sources.quote: אַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ לְאָבִיךָ ״הַכֶּר־נָא
sources.says: Radak quotes Bereshit Rabbah that the Torah, in effect, says: you said 'please identify' to your father.

sources.quote: אֵין נָא אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן בַּקָּשָׁה – הַכֵּר נָא בוֹרַאֲךָ, וְאַל תְּאַבֵּד שָׁלֹשׁ נְפָשׁוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says נא is only a word of request, and reads it as 'recognize your Creator and do not destroy three souls.'

38:26.headline: 'She is right, from me' can mean 'more right than I'
38:26.body: Rashi reads ממני as 'she is pregnant by me,' and the sages add that a heavenly voice said 'from me came these things.' Rashbam reads it as 'more righteous than I.'

sources.quote: ממני. הִיא מְעֻבֶּרֶת. וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ ז"ל דָּרְשׁוּ שֶׁיָּצְאָה בַת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה מִמֶּנִּי וּמֵאִתִּי יָצְאוּ הַדְּבָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says ממני means 'she is pregnant by me,' and the sages say a heavenly voice said 'from me came these things.'

sources.quote: צדקה ממני - יותר ממני
sources.says: Rashbam says it means 'more than I.'

38:26.headline: 'Did not add again' can also mean 'did not stop'
38:26.body: Rashi gives two readings of ולא יסף: 'he did not add' (he never knew her again), or 'he did not stop.' Rashbam says the first is right, because 'did not stop' would use a different form.

sources.quote: יֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים לֹא הוֹסִיף, וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים לֹא פָסַק
sources.says: Rashi says some say 'he did not add,' and some say 'he did not stop.'

sources.quote: ולא הוסיף שאם אתה מפרשו ולא פסק היה לו לכתוב ולא יסף
sources.says: Rashbam says it means 'did not add,' since if it meant 'did not stop' the verse would be written differently.

38:27.headline: Spelling hints that Tamar's twins were both righteous
38:27.body: Here תאומים is spelled in full, and for Rebekah's twins it is spelled short. Rashi says the sages read this as a hint: one of Rebekah's twins was wicked, but both of Tamar's were righteous.

sources.quote: והנה תאומים. מָלֵא, וּלְהַלָּן תּוֹמִם חָסֵר, לְפִי שֶׁהָאֶחָד רָשָׁע, אֲבָל אֵלּוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם צַדִּיקִים
sources.says: Rashi says here תאומים is spelled in full and there תומם is short, because one was wicked but these two were both righteous.

38:30.headline: The name Zerah comes from the shining red thread
38:30.body: Rashi says Zerah is named for the shining look of the red thread. Rashbam says זרח means redness, as in the sun at dawn and dusk.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם זְרִיחַת מַרְאִית הַשָּׁנִי
sources.says: Rashi says he was named for the shining of the look of the scarlet thread.

sources.quote: וזרח לשון אדמומית הוא
sources.says: Rashbam says זרח is a word for redness.

39:1.headline: 'Joseph was brought down' echoes 'Judah went down'
39:1.body: The story of Joseph breaks off for Judah and Tamar, then returns here. Rashi says the break puts Judah's going down next to Joseph's being sold, because Judah was brought down from his greatness over it.

sources.quote: כְּדֵי לִסְמֹךְ יְרִידָתוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה לִמְכִירָתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף לוֹמַר שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילוֹ הוֹרִידוּהוּ מִגְּדֻלָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the break places Judah's going down beside Joseph's sale, to say they brought Judah down from his greatness because of it.

39:2.headline: Maimonides: Joseph's success shows what 'God was with him' means
39:2.body: In the Guide for the Perplexed, Maimonides says 'God was with him' is not said of any ordinary success. It is said of help toward a great good, and he names Joseph's success in the Egyptian's house as a first cause of great things.

sources.quote: כמו הצלחת יוסף בבית המצרי (בראשית לט,ב), שהיתה סיבה ראשונה לדברים גדולים שאירעו לאחר מכן
sources.says: Maimonides gives Joseph's success in the Egyptian's house as an example of help that was a first cause of great events later.

39:3.headline: Did Potiphar hear God's name on Joseph's lips, or see him succeed?
39:3.body: Rashi says God's name was always in Joseph's mouth, so his master saw that God was with him. Ramban disagrees: Potiphar saw Joseph succeed more than anyone and knew it came from God.

sources.quote: שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שָׁגוּר בְּפִיו
sources.says: Rashi says the name of Heaven was fluent in his mouth.

sources.quote: כִּי יַצְלִיחוּ מַעֲשָׂיו בְּכָל עֵת יוֹתֵר מִכָּל אָדָם, וְיָדַע כִּי מֵאֵת אֱלֹהִים הוּא לוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says his deeds always succeeded more than anyone's, and his master knew it was from God.

39:6.headline: 'He knew nothing but the bread' may mean his wife
39:6.body: Rashi says 'the bread' is a polite word for Potiphar's wife. Ibn Ezra calls that far-fetched and reads it plainly: Joseph's master left everything in his hands except the bread, which Joseph would not touch because he was a Hebrew.

sources.quote: הִיא אִשְׁתּוֹ, אֶלָּא שֶׁדִּבֵּר בְּלָשׁוֹן נְקִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi says the bread is his wife, but the verse speaks in clean language.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני שכל אשר לו היה בידו חוץ מן הלחם שלא היה אפילו נוגע בו בעבור היותו עברי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is that all he had was in Joseph's hand except the bread, which Joseph did not even touch because he was a Hebrew.

39:6.headline: Maimonides: תאר means outward shape, a word he keeps from God
39:6.body: In the Guide for the Perplexed, Maimonides quotes 'beautiful of תאר' from this verse. He says תאר is the outward shape of a thing as people see it, and that it cannot be said of God.

sources.quote: נאמר: "יְפֵה תֹאַר וִיפֵה מַרְאֶה" (בראשית לט,ו
sources.says: Maimonides cites 'beautiful of form and beautiful of appearance' as an example of the word תאר.

sources.quote: המונח הזה אינו חל על האלוה יתעלה כלל
sources.says: Maimonides says this term does not apply to God at all.

39:6.headline: Why does the verse mention Joseph's beauty just here?
39:6.body: Ramban says it explains why his master's wife looked at him. Rashi gives a different answer: once Joseph saw himself in charge, he started eating, drinking and curling his hair.

sources.quote: כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה עַצְמוֹ מוֹשֵׁל, הִתְחִיל אוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה וּמְסַלְסֵל בְּשַׂעֲרוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says that when he saw himself ruling, he began to eat, drink and curl his hair.

sources.quote: כִּי בַּעֲבוּר יָפְיוֹ נָשְׂאָה אֵשֶׁת אֲדוֹנָיו אֵלָיו אֶת עֵינֶיהָ
sources.says: Ramban says the verse mentions his beauty to say that because of it his master's wife raised her eyes to him.

39:10.headline: 'Lie beside her' means even lying near her
39:10.body: Rashi says לשכב אצלה refers even to lying beside her without intimacy. Ibn Ezra, as Ramban reports, says the word אצלה is never used for the act itself, which uses עמה or אותה.

sources.quote: לשכב אצלה. אֲפִלּוּ בְלֹא תַשְׁמִישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says 'to lie beside her' means even without intimacy.

sources.quote: כִּי לֹא מָצָאנוּ "אֶצְלָהּ" עַל הַמִּשְׁגָּל, רַק עִמָּהּ אוֹ אוֹתָהּ
sources.says: Ramban says we do not find אצלה used for intimacy, only עמה or אותה.

39:10.headline: 'To be with her' hints at the world to come
39:10.body: Ibn Ezra reads להיות עמה as 'to talk with her.' The sages split the two verbs: 'to lie with her' is for this world, and 'to be with her' is for the world to come.

sources.quote: או להיות עמה לדבר שיחות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'to be with her' can mean to talk with her.

sources.quote: לִשְׁכַּב עִמָּהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִהְיוֹת עִמָּהּ בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages: to lie with her in this world and be with her in the world to come.

39:11.headline: 'On a day like this': a particular day, or a year later?
39:11.body: Rashi says it was a special day, an idol festival when everyone went to the temple. Ibn Ezra says it could be a week, a month, or a year after she first spoke to him, and thinks a full year is right.

sources.quote: יוֹם צְחוֹק, יוֹם אֵיד שֶׁלָּהֶם, שֶׁהָלְכוּ כֻּלָּם לְבֵית עֲ"זָ
sources.says: Rashi says it was a day of laughter, their festival day, when they all went to the idol's house.

sources.quote: אחר שנה תמימה והוא הנכון בעיני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is after a full year.

39:20.headline: The rare word סהר, prison, has several explanations
39:20.body: Ibn Ezra says it may be an Egyptian word, since the verse explains it. Ramban reports that grammarians read it as a round vault, but thinks it means a pit built underground with an opening above.

sources.quote: לא נדע אם הוא לשון הקדש, או לשון מצרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says we do not know if it is Hebrew or an Egyptian word.

sources.quote: יְפָרְשׁוּ "סַהַר" כִּפָּה עֲגֻלָּה, מִלְּשׁוֹן "אַגַּן הַסַּהַר
sources.says: Ramban says the grammarians explain סהר as a round vault, from 'the round bowl.'

sources.quote: וּלְפִי דַּעְתִּי שֶׁהוּא הַבּוֹר
sources.says: Ramban says that in his view it is the pit.

39:21.headline: חסד here means that people liked him
39:21.body: Rashi says ויט אליו חסד means he was well received by everyone who saw him. He points to the Mishnaic word חסודה in 'a bride who is lovely and graceful.'

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה מְקֻבָּל לְכָל רוֹאָיו, לְשׁוֹן "כַּלָּה נָאָה וַחֲסוּדָה" שֶׁבַּמִּשְׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says he was welcomed by all who saw him, like the Mishnah's 'a lovely and gracious bride.'

4:7.headline: שאת: 'forgiven', or 'lifted face'?
4:7.body: The word שאת can mean 'forgiveness' or 'lifting up'. Onkelos reads 'it will be forgiven you', while Ibn Ezra prefers 'lifting your face', since Cain's face had just fallen.

sources.says: Onkelos puts it as 'if you do good your deeds, it will be forgiven you'.
sources.quote: הֲלָא אִם תּוֹטִיב עוֹבָדָךְ יִשְׁתְּבֵק לָךְ

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says many read שאת as 'lifting your sin', but he reads it as 'lifting the face'.
sources.quote: ופי' שאת על דעת מפרשים רבים שאת עונך, והנכון בעיני שאת פנים,

4:8.headline: 'Cain said to Hevel', but the verse never says what
4:8.body: The verse says Cain spoke, then gives no words. Rashi says he picked a quarrel to find a reason to kill Hevel, and Ibn Ezra says he repeated the rebukes God had given him.

sources.says: Rashi says Cain picked a fight with Hevel in order to kill him.
sources.quote: נִכְנַס עִמּוֹ בְּדִבְרֵי רִיב וּמַצָּה לְהִתְעוֹלֵל עָלָיו לְהָרְגוֹ.

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the likeliest meaning is that Cain told Hevel all the rebukes God had given him.
sources.quote: הקרוב אלי שאמר לו כל התוכחות שהוכיחו השם.

4:10.headline: דמי is plural: 'the bloods of your brother'
4:10.body: Rashi says the plural covers Hevel's blood and the blood of the children he would have had. Radak says the plural form is an ordinary one for blood.

sources.says: Rashi says it means his blood and the blood of his descendants.
sources.quote: דָּמוֹ וְדַם זַרְעִיּוֹתָיו.

sources.says: Radak says the plural דמי is an ordinary plural of דם.
sources.quote: וְרִבּוּי דְּמֵי כְּמוֹהוּ רַבִּים,

4:13.headline: עוני מנשוא: 'too great to forgive', or 'too great to bear'?
4:13.body: The verb נשא can mean 'forgive' or 'carry'. Ibn Ezra and Onkelos read 'too great to forgive', while Rashi reads a question: can the One who carries heaven and earth not carry my sin?

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the commentators read נשוא as 'forgive', like 'נושא עון'.
sources.quote: ופי' על דעת כל המפרשים שהודה חטאו, ופי' נשוא כטעם סלוח

sources.says: Onkelos renders it as 'my sin is too great to forgive'.
sources.quote: סַגִּי חוֹבִי מִלְּמִשְׁבָּק:

sources.says: Rashi reads it as a question: you carry heaven and earth, and my sin you cannot carry?
sources.quote: בִּתְמִיהָ, אַתָּה טוֹעֵן עֶלְיוֹנִים וְתַחְתּוֹנִים, וַעֲוֹנִי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִטְעֹן?

4:15.headline: God 'set' a sign on Cain, not 'gave' one
4:15.body: Ramban notes the verse says וישם, 'set', not 'gave' or 'made', and takes it to mean the sign was fixed on Cain. Rashi says God engraved a letter of His name on Cain's forehead.

sources.says: Ramban says the wording shows the sign was fixed and stayed with Cain.
sources.quote: וְלֹא אָמַר "וַיִּתֵּן" לוֹ הַשֵּׁם אוֹת אוֹ "וַיַּעַשׂ", יוֹרֶה שֶׁשָּׂם לוֹ הָאוֹת קָבוּעַ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה עִמּוֹ תָּמִיד,

sources.says: Rashi says God engraved a letter of His name on Cain's forehead.
sources.quote: חָקַק לוֹ אוֹת מִשְּׁמוֹ בְּמִצְחוֹ.

40:1.headline: 'They sinned' is spelled out: a fly and a pebble
40:1.body: The verse does not say what the butler and baker did. Rashi, from the sages, says a fly was found in the butler's cup and a stone in the baker's bread, while Ibn Ezra says only that they broke a rule of the royal court.

sources.quote: זֶה נִמְצָא זְבוּב בְּפַיְילִי פּוֹטֵירִין שֶׁלּוֹ, וְזֶה נִמְצָא צְרוֹר בִּגְלוּסְקִין שֶׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says one was found with a fly in his cup, and the other with a pebble in his bread.

sources.quote: חטא מוסר המלוכה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they sinned against the custom of the royal court.

40:2.headline: 'Pharaoh's סריסים' means eunuchs, or simply high officials
40:2.body: Ramban says the butler and baker served in the women's quarters, where kings made such servants eunuchs. But Onkelos translates סריסים as 'officials and great men,' and Ramban notes Onkelos translated Potiphar's title as 'chief.'

sources.quote: הָיוּ אֵלֶּה הַשָּׂרִים שְׁנֵיהֶם סָרִיסִים, כִּי הָיוּ שָׂרֵי הַמַּשְׁקִים וְהָאוֹפִים גַּם בְּבֵית הַנָּשִׁים אֲשֶׁר לַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Ramban says both of these officers were eunuchs, because they served also in the king's women's house.

sources.quote: כִּי סָרִיסִים – שָׂרִים וּגְדוֹלִים
sources.says: Ramban says Onkelos holds that סריסים means officers and great men.

sources.quote: וּרְגֵז פַּרְעֹה עַל תְּרֵין רַבְרְבָנוֹהִי
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'Pharaoh was angry at his two officials.'

40:4.headline: 'Days in the prison' means a full year
40:4.body: The verse says only that they were there for 'days.' Rashi says it was twelve months. Rashbam agrees and points to 'days shall be its redemption' in Leviticus, where days means a year.

sources.quote: ויהיו ימים במשמר. שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says 'days in the prison' means twelve months.

sources.quote: שנה שלימה, כדכתיב: ימים תהיה גאולתו
sources.says: Rashbam says a whole year, as it is written 'days shall be its redemption.'

40:5.headline: 'Both of them dreamed a dream' can mean each dreamed both
40:5.body: Rashi says the plain sense is that the two men each dreamed a dream. The midrash reads it as: each one dreamed his own dream and also the meaning of his friend's.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ כָּל א' חָלַם חֲלוֹם שְׁנֵיהֶם – שֶׁחָלַם אֶת חֲלוֹמוֹ וּפִתְרוֹן חֲבֵרוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the midrash reads it that each one dreamed the dream of both, his own dream and the meaning of his friend's.

40:6.headline: The rare word זעפים means upset, like a stormy sea
40:6.body: Rashi says it means sad or gloomy, like 'sullen and troubled' in Kings. Ibn Ezra says it means shaken, as in 'the sea stood from its raging' in Jonah.

sources.quote: זעפים. עֲצֵבִים כְּמוֹ סַר וְזָעֵף
sources.says: Rashi says זעפים means sad, as in 'sullen and troubled.'

sources.quote: מתרעשים כטעם "ויעמד הים מזעפו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means shaken, in the sense of 'the sea stood still from its raging.'

40:8.headline: 'Interpretations belong to God': is it humility or a skill?
40:8.body: Ibn Ezra reads it as Joseph saying the future is God's, so his words cannot help or hurt them. Sforno says the skill of interpreting is in people, since they are made in God's image.

sources.quote: כי פתרון החלומות לשם הוא כי הוא יודע העתיד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says interpreting dreams belongs to God, since he knows the future.

sources.quote: חָכְמַת הַפִּתְרוֹן הִיא בָּאָדָם מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁהוּא בְּצֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים
sources.says: Sforno says the wisdom of interpretation is in a person because he is in God's image.

40:11.headline: The rare verb ואשחט means 'I squeezed' the grapes
40:11.body: This is the only time the Bible uses the verb. Rashi and Radak read it as 'squeezed,' a word common in the Mishnah, but Ibn Ezra compares it to 'slaughterers of the children' in Isaiah.

sources.quote: ואשחט. כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ וַעֲצָרִית, וְהַרְבֵּה יֵשׁ בִּלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says it is as Onkelos translates, 'and I pressed,' and that it is common in the language of the Mishnah.

sources.quote: וָאֶשְׂחַט. עִנְיַן עָצוּר
sources.says: Radak says ואשחט is about pressing.

sources.quote: כמו שוחטי הילדים (ישעי' נז ה) ולא כאשר פי' הגאון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like 'slaughterers of the children,' and not as the Gaon explained.

40:13.headline: 'Pharaoh will lift up your head' means he will count you
40:13.body: Rashi says ישא את ראשך is a way of counting: Pharaoh will count you among his servants, and Ibn Ezra agrees. Joseph then tells the baker the same words, with a darker meaning.

sources.quote: לְ' חֶשְׁבּוֹן, כְּשֶׁיִּפְקֹד שְׁאָר עֲבָדָיו לְשָׁרֵת לְפָנָיו בַּסְּעוּדָה, יִמְנֶה אוֹתְךָ עִמָּהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for counting: when he assigns his other servants to serve at the feast, he will count you with them.

sources.quote: הנכון שהוא בדרך מספר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the right reading is that it is a way of numbering.

40:15.headline: 'Land of the Hebrews' is where Abraham's family lived
40:15.body: Ramban says it means Hebron, where Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lived, since Abraham was called the Hebrew and so were his children. Joseph used the name so that no one would take him for a Canaanite.

sources.quote: כִּי אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהָיָה רֹאשׁ הַיַּחַס נִקְרָא אַבְרָהָם הָעִבְרִי
sources.says: Ramban says Abraham, the head of the family, was called Abraham the Hebrew.

sources.quote: כִּי יְדוּעָה הָיְתָה מִשְׁפַּחַת הָעִבְרִים שֶׁהֵם הָאָבוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ גָּרִים בְּאֶרֶץ כְּנַעַן
sources.says: Radak says the family of the Hebrews, the forefathers, were known as those living in the land of Canaan.

40:16.headline: 'Interpreted well' can mean 'rightly' or 'in his favor'
40:16.body: Onkelos reads כי טוב פתר as 'he interpreted nicely,' meaning correctly. Ramban also offers that the baker saw it was interpreted for the good, and Radak says the baker took it as favorable.

sources.quote: כִּי יָפֶה פָּתָר, וְכֵן "טוּב טַעַם וָדַעַת לַמְּדֵנִי
sources.says: Ramban says Onkelos reads it 'he interpreted nicely,' like 'teach me good sense and knowledge.'

sources.quote: אוֹ יֹאמַר, וַיַּרְא שַׂר הָאֹפִים כִּי לְטוֹבָה פָּתַר לוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says the other reading is that the baker saw he interpreted for the good.

sources.quote: רָאָה בְּלִבּוֹ לְהַשְׁמָעוּת אָזְנָיו כִּי הַפִּתְרוֹן טוֹב הוּא
sources.says: Radak says he saw, from what he heard, that the interpretation was good.

40:16.headline: The one-time word חרי means holes, or white bread
40:16.body: Rashi and Rashbam say the baskets had holes, being made of peeled twigs. Ibn Ezra reports that Saadia Gaon called it white bread, and Ramban says that view is the right one.

sources.quote: סַלִּים שֶׁל נְצָרִים קְלוּפִים חוֹרִין חוֹרִין
sources.says: Rashi says baskets of peeled twigs, full of holes.

sources.quote: סלי חורי - מנוקבים
sources.says: Rashbam says סלי חורי means perforated baskets.

sources.quote: אמר הגאון שהוא לחם לבן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Gaon said it is white bread.

sources.quote: וְהוּא הַנָּכוֹן, כִּי הָיָה בְּכָל הַסַּלִּים מִלֶּחֶם הַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Ramban says this is the right view, since all the baskets held some of the king's bread.

40:19.headline: The same words as before now mean taking his head off
40:19.body: This is the same phrase Joseph used for the butler. Rashbam says here it is a lifting of the head for hanging, not counting, and Ibn Ezra says it means he will remove it or raise it on a tree.

sources.quote: וזה אינו נשיאה של חשבון אלא של זקיפת תלייה
sources.says: Rashbam says this is not a lifting of counting but a lifting for hanging.

sources.quote: ישאנו ממקומו, וטעמו יסירנו או ירימנו על עץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he will lift it from its place, meaning remove it or raise it on a tree.

40:20.headline: הלדת is a rare form for a birthday
40:20.body: Rashi says it is the day of Pharaoh's birth, and the form means being born through others, as a midwife delivers a child. Radak says it may mean the day a son was born to Pharaoh.

sources.quote: וּלְשׁוֹן הֻלֶּדֶת, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַוָּלָד נוֹצָר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says the form הלדת is used because a child is not brought forth except by others.

sources.quote: יוֹם שֶׁנּוֹלַד בֵּן לְפַרְעֹה, אוֹ פֵּרוּשׁוֹ יוֹם שֶׁנּוֹלַד
sources.says: Radak says it is the day a son was born to Pharaoh, or simply the day he was born.

41:1.headline: 'Two years of days' means two full years
41:1.body: The odd phrase is שנתים ימים. Rashbam says it means two whole years, and points to 'days shall be its redemption' in Leviticus, where days means a full year.

sources.quote: שתי שנים שלמות, כדכתיב: ימים תהיה גאולתו
sources.says: Rashbam says it means two whole years, as it is written 'days shall be its redemption.'

41:1.headline: Only the Nile is called a יאר
41:1.body: Rashi says no other river is called יאר except the Nile. Egypt is cut into man-made channels, and the Nile rises into them and waters them, because rain seldom falls there.

sources.quote: כָּל שְׁאָר נְהָרוֹת אֵינָם קְרוּיִין יְאוֹרִים חוּץ מִנִּילוּס
sources.says: Rashi says no other rivers are called יאורים except the Nile.

41:2.headline: The rare word אחו is a marsh, a valley, or a plant
41:2.body: Rashi says אחו is a marsh, like 'will the reed grow without water' in Job, and Ibn Ezra lists a valley of plants or a plant name. Ramban rejects Rashi: אחו is the name of the growing grass.

sources.quote: בָּאֲגַם, מריש"ק בְּלַעַז, כְּמוֹ יִשְׂגֶּא אָחוּ
sources.says: Rashi says באחו means in a marsh, like 'will the reed grow.'

sources.quote: י"א עמק שבו צמחים. וי"א שהוא שם צמח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some say a valley with plants, and some say it is the name of a plant.

sources.quote: וְאֵינֶנּוּ נָכוֹן, כִּי אָחוּ – שֵׁם הָעֵשֶׂב הַגָּדֵל
sources.says: Ramban says Rashi is not right, because אחו is the name of the grass that grows.

41:6.headline: The rare word שדופות is read as 'beaten' and as 'east-wind scorched'
41:6.body: Rashi follows Onkelos: it means beaten, like a doorframe struck over and over by the door. Ibn Ezra says it is damage from the east wind, which is called קדים.

sources.quote: שְׁקִיפָן קִדּוּם, חֲבוּטוֹת, לְשׁוֹן מַשְׁקוֹף הֶחָבוּט תָּמִיד עַל יְדֵי הַדֶּלֶת הַמַּכָּה עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it means beaten, like a lintel always struck by the door.

sources.quote: שארע שדפון מרוח מזרחית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means blight that came from the east wind.

41:7.headline: 'And behold, a dream': a finished dream, or a sudden realization?
41:7.body: Rashi says the phrase means a complete dream had finished before him, and he needed interpreters. Rashbam says Pharaoh only now understood it was a dream: until then he thought he had seen it for real.

sources.quote: וְהִנֵּה נִשְׁלַם חֲלוֹם שָׁלֵם לְפָנָיו וְהֻצְרַךְ לְפוֹתְרִים
sources.says: Rashi says a whole dream was now finished before him, and he needed interpreters.

sources.quote: אבל עד עתה היה סבור שראה ממש ולא חלום
sources.says: Rashbam says that until now he thought he had really seen it, not a dream.

41:8.headline: חרטמים are explained as people who consult bones
41:8.body: Rashi splits the word: those who 'devote' themselves (הנחרים) to the bones of the dead and ask them questions. Ibn Ezra says it is a four-letter word, perhaps Aramaic or Egyptian, for those who study nature.

sources.quote: הַנֵּחָרִים בְּטִימֵי מֵתִים, שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִין בַּעֲצָמוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they are those who devote themselves to the bones of the dead, asking the bones.

sources.quote: מלה מרובעת ויתכן להיותה ארמית או מצרית
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a four-letter word that may be Aramaic or Egyptian.

41:8.headline: 'No one could interpret for Pharaoh' does not mean no one tried
41:8.body: Rashi says they did interpret, but not in a way Pharaoh could accept. They said things like: you will have seven daughters and bury seven daughters.

sources.quote: פּוֹתְרִים הָיוּ אוֹתָם, אֲבָל לֹא לְפַרְעֹה, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה קוֹלָן נִכְנָס בְּאָזְנָיו
sources.says: Rashi says they were interpreting, but not for Pharaoh, because their voice did not enter his ears.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹמְרִים שֶׁבַע בָּנוֹת אַתָּה מוֹלִיד וְשֶׁבַע בָּנוֹת אַתָּה קוֹבֵר
sources.says: Rashi says they were saying: you will father seven daughters and bury seven daughters.

41:12.headline: 'Lad': a put-down here, though Joseph was thirty
41:12.body: Rashi says the butler picks insulting words: a 'lad' means a fool unfit for greatness. In the Guide for the Perplexed, Maimonides notes that Joseph is called נער at age thirty, so the word is not only about children.

sources.quote: נער. שׁוֹטֶה וְאֵין רָאוּי לִגְדֻלָּה
sources.says: Rashi says נער here means a fool, not fit for greatness.

sources.quote: יוסף הצדיק נקרא בעברית "נַעַר" (בראשית מא,יב) בהיותו בן שלושים שנה
sources.says: Maimonides says Joseph the righteous is called נער in Hebrew when he was thirty years old.

41:16.headline: 'Not me': Joseph gives credit to God, or doubts he is alone?
41:16.body: Rashi reads בלעדי as 'the wisdom is not mine.' Sforno reads it differently: Joseph says there is surely another interpreter besides him, though Pharaoh said there is none.

sources.quote: אֵין הַחָכְמָה מִשֶּׁלִּי, אֶלָּא אֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶה
sources.says: Rashi says the wisdom is not from me, but God will answer.

sources.quote: אֲנִי חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּלִי סָפֵק פּוֹתֵר בִּלְעָדַי
sources.says: Sforno says Joseph thinks there is surely an interpreter besides him.

41:23.headline: The one-time word צנמות means hard and dry, like rock
41:23.body: Rashi ties צנמות to the Aramaic word for rock: the ears were like wood with no moisture, hard as stone. Ibn Ezra says there is no other use in Scripture and that it means 'empty.'

sources.quote: צוּנְמָא בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי סֶלַע, הֲרֵי הֵן כְּעֵץ בְּלִי לִחְלוּחַ וְקָשׁוֹת כְּסֶלַע
sources.says: Rashi says צונמא in Aramaic is a rock, so they are like wood with no moisture, hard as rock.

sources.quote: אין לו חבר במקרא, וטעמו כמו ריקות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it has no partner in Scripture and means something like empty.

41:28.headline: God 'told' Pharaoh about the plenty but 'showed' him the famine
41:28.body: Joseph first says God 'told' Pharaoh, then that God 'showed' him. Rashi says the plenty was near, so 'told.' The famine was far off and spread out, so 'showed.'

sources.quote: בְּשֶׁבַע שָׁנִים הַטּוֹבוֹת נֶאֱמַר הגיד לפרעה לְפִי שֶׁהָיָה סָמוּךְ וּבְשֶׁבַע שְׁנֵי רָעָב נֶאֱמַר הראה את פרעה
sources.says: Rashi says of the good years it says 'told Pharaoh' because it was near, and of the famine years it says 'showed Pharaoh.'

41:31.headline: 'Plenty will not be known' answers 'it was not known'
41:31.body: In the dream, the fat cows went into the thin ones and 'it was not known.' Rashi says Joseph's words are the meaning of that line: the plenty would be forgotten in the famine.

sources.quote: הוּא פִּתְרוֹן "ולא נודע כי באו אל קרבנה
sources.says: Rashi says this is the interpretation of 'it was not known that they had come inside them.'

sources.quote: דוגמת ולא נודע כי באו אל קרבנה
sources.says: Rashbam says it is like 'it was not known that they had come inside them.'

41:34.headline: 'And take a fifth' may really mean 'and prepare'
41:34.body: Radak and Ibn Ezra read וחמש as taking a fifth of the grain. Rashi follows Onkelos instead: it means to hasten or arm, as in the 'armed' Israelites in Exodus.

sources.quote: כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ וִיזָרְזוּן; וְכֵן וַחֲמֻשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says it is as Onkelos translates, 'and they shall hasten,' and like 'armed' in Exodus.

sources.quote: יִקַּח אֶחָד מִן חֲמִשָּׁה
sources.says: Radak says he will take one of five.

sources.quote: וחמש שיקנה החומש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says וחמש means that he will acquire the fifth.

41:38.headline: 'A spirit of God' is prophecy, or wisdom in practical matters?
41:38.body: Onkelos reads רוח אלהים as a spirit of prophecy from the Lord. Rashbam says it means a spirit of dream interpretation, and even more so of practical wisdom.

sources.quote: דִּי רוּחַ נְבוּאָה מִן קֳדָם יְיָ בֵּיהּ
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'in whom is a spirit of prophecy from before the Lord.'

sources.quote: בפתרון חלומות וכל שכן בחכמת דרך ארץ
sources.says: Rashbam says it means in interpreting dreams and even more so in practical wisdom.

41:40.headline: 'By your word will all my people be ישק' has three readings
41:40.body: Rashi says it means they will be fed and provided for, and Rashbam says they will hurry with weapons of war. Ibn Ezra reports an opinion that it comes from the word for a kiss.

sources.quote: ישק. יִתְּזַן, יִתְפַּרְנֵס
sources.says: Rashi says ישק means will be fed, will be supported.

sources.quote: יזדרזו בכלי קרב של מלחמה לצאת על האויבים
sources.says: Rashbam says they will hurry with weapons of war to go out against enemies.

sources.quote: וי"א שהוא מגזירת נשיקה בדרך רחוקה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some say it is from the root for kissing, in a distant way.

41:42.headline: The rare word רביד, a gold chain, is tied to spread-out bedding
41:42.body: Rashi says רביד means a chain, named for being strung with links, and ties it to 'I have spread my bed with coverings' in Proverbs. Ibn Ezra makes the same link.

sources.quote: וְעַל שֶׁהוּא רָצוּף בְּטַבָּעוֹת קָרוּי רְבִיד
sources.says: Rashi says it is called רביד because it is strung with rings.

sources.quote: רביד הזהב. כמו "מרבדים רבדתי ערשי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says רביד is like 'I have spread coverings on my couch.'

41:43.headline: Maimonides: מרכבה means a team of animals, not just one chariot
41:43.body: In the Guide for the Perplexed, Maimonides cites 'chariot of the second' to show that מרכבה means a group of riding animals, which is why the sages called the throne of glory a מרכבה. Rashi says 'second' means the chariot beside Pharaoh's own.

sources.quote: ודע שקבוצה של בהמות נרכבות נקראת "מרכבה
sources.says: Maimonides says a group of riding animals is called a מרכבה.

sources.quote: הַשְּׁנִיָּה לְמֶרְכַּבְתּוֹ, הַמְהַלֶּכֶת אֵצֶל שֶׁלּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the second to his own chariot, which travels beside his.

41:43.headline: 'Avrekh', the cry before Joseph, is read as 'father' and as 'knee'
41:43.body: Onkelos reads it as 'this is a father to the king,' and Rabbi Judah plays on it: אב, a father in wisdom, and רך, tender in years. Rabbi Yose answers that it comes from ברכים, knees, since all bent the knee, as Ibn Ezra also says.

sources.quote: אֵין אַבְרֵךְ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן בִּרְכַּיִם, שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיוּ נִכְנָסִין וְיוֹצְאִין תַּחַת יָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says in the sages' view אברך is only about knees, since all came in and out under his hand.

sources.quote: דֵּין אַבָּא לְמַלְכָּא
sources.says: Onkelos translates 'this is a father to the king.'

sources.quote: כל אדם קורא לפניו אכרע ואשתחוה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says everyone called out before him, 'I will kneel and bow.'

41:45.headline: Joseph's Egyptian name צפנת פענח: 'revealer of secrets'?
41:45.body: Rashi says it means one who explains hidden things, though פענח has no match in Hebrew, and Onkelos translates it 'the man for whom hidden things are revealed.' Ibn Ezra says if it is an Egyptian word we do not know what it means.

sources.quote: מְפָרֵשׁ הַצְּפוּנוֹת; וְאֵין לְפַעְנֵחַ דִּמְיוֹן בַּמִּקְרָא
sources.says: Rashi says it means one who explains hidden things, and that פענח has no likeness in Scripture.

sources.quote: אם זו המלה מצרית לא ידענו פירושה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says if this is an Egyptian word, we do not know its meaning.

sources.quote: גַּבְרָא דְמִטַּמְרָן גָּלְיָן לֵיהּ
sources.says: Onkelos translates it 'a man to whom hidden things are revealed.'

41:45.headline: Is Potiphera the same man as Potiphar?
41:45.body: Rashi, following the Talmud, says Potiphera is Potiphar himself, renamed after what happened to him. Rashbam says that on the plain reading they are two different men.

sources.quote: הוּא פּוֹטִיפַר, וְנִקְרָא פּוֹטִיפֶרַע עַל שֶׁנִּסְתָּרֵס מֵאֵלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says he is Potiphar, and was called Potiphera because he was made a eunuch on his own.

sources.quote: אין זה פוטיפר לפי הפשט
sources.says: Rashbam says this is not Potiphar on the plain reading.

41:45.headline: 'Priest of On': a priest, or a ruler of the city?
41:45.body: Ibn Ezra says כהן here might be one who serves God or an idol, since in Scripture it means a servant. Rashbam says it means the ruler of that city, as 'the sons of David were כהנים.' Onkelos has 'chief of On.'

sources.quote: כהן און. עובד השם או עובד עו"ג
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says כהן און means a servant of God or a servant of idols.

sources.quote: כהן און - שר של אותה העיר
sources.says: Rashbam says כהן און is the ruler of that city.

sources.quote: פּוֹטִי פֶרַע רַבָּא דְאוֹן
sources.says: Onkelos translates it as 'Poti-phera, chief of On.'

41:47.headline: 'Handfuls': the grain was stored by the handful, or grew in handfuls
41:47.body: Rashi says לקמצים means handful on top of handful, hand upon hand, as they stored it. Radak says the land made handfuls from each single grain.

sources.quote: קֹמֶץ עַל קֹמֶץ, יָד עַל יָד, הָיוּ אוֹצְרִים
sources.says: Rashi says handful upon handful, hand upon hand, they were storing.

sources.quote: מִגַּרְגַּר אֶחָד הוֹצִיאָה קְמָצִים רַבִּים
sources.says: Radak says from one grain it produced many handfuls.

42:1.headline: 'Jacob saw there was grain': but he only heard it
42:1.body: Jacob did not see Egypt, he heard about it. Rashi says he saw with holy insight, while Ibn Ezra says the senses are traded for one another in Scripture, as in 'see the smell of my son.'

sources.quote: וּמֵהֵיכָן רָאָה? וַהֲלֹא לֹא רָאָה אֶלָּא שָׁמַע
sources.says: Rashi asks how he saw, since he only heard.

sources.quote: בעבור היות ההרגשות נחברות במקום אחר יחליפו זו בזו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says since the senses are joined in one place, they are traded for one another.

42:1.headline: 'Why do you look at each other?' has several readings
42:1.body: Rashi gives three readings: do not look well-fed before Esau's and Ishmael's sons, or why is everyone staring at you, or why grow lean in the famine. Sforno says: why look at one another, each waiting for another to go.

sources.quote: לָמָּה תַּרְאוּ עַצְמְכֶם בִּפְנֵי בְנֵי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וּבְנֵי עֵשָׂו כְּאִלּוּ אַתֶּם שְׂבֵעִים
sources.says: Rashi says: why show yourselves before the sons of Ishmael and Esau as if you were sated.

sources.quote: שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן כְּחִישָׁה, לָמָּה תִּהְיוּ כְּחוּשִׁים בָּרָעָב
sources.says: Rashi says he heard from others that it is a word of wasting: why be thin from hunger.

sources.quote: שיש לכם הון, או אל תהיו מריבים זה עם זה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says either that you have wealth, or do not quarrel with one another.

sources.quote: לָמָּה תַּבִּיטוּ זֶה אֶל זֶה
sources.says: Sforno says: why do you look at one another.

42:2.headline: 'Go down' hints at 210 years in Egypt
42:2.body: Jacob says רדו, 'go down,' not 'go.' Rashi notes that the letters of רדו add up to 210, the number of years Israel would be enslaved in Egypt.

sources.quote: וְלֹא אָמַר לְכוּ, רֶמֶז לְמָאתַיִם וְעֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ לְמִצְרַיִם כְּמִנְיַן רד"ו
sources.says: Rashi says Jacob did not say 'go,' hinting at the two hundred and ten years they were enslaved in Egypt, the value of רד"ו.

42:3.headline: 'Joseph's brothers' went down, not 'Jacob's sons'
42:3.body: The verse calls them Joseph's brothers. Rashi says this shows they regretted the sale and meant to pay any price for him, and Radak says that by going down they fulfilled his dream.

sources.quote: וְלֹא כָתַב בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ מִתְחָרְטִים בִּמְכִירָתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the verse did not write 'sons of Jacob,' which teaches that they regretted the sale.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁבְּסִבָּתוֹ יָרְדוּ, וְעַתָּה בִּירִידָתָם נִפְתַּר חֲלוֹמוֹ
sources.says: Radak says they went down because of him, and now in their going down his dream is fulfilled.

42:7.headline: Joseph 'recognized' them but made himself 'a stranger'
42:7.body: The verse sets two words side by side: ויכרם, he recognized them, and ויתנכר, he made himself foreign. Rashi says he became like a stranger by speaking harshly, and Ibn Ezra says the word comes from נכרי, a foreigner.

sources.quote: נַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם כְּנָכְרִי בִּדְבָרִים לְדַבֵּר קָשׁוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says he became like a stranger to them in his words, speaking harshly.

sources.quote: מגזרת נכרי, הראה שהוא נכרי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from נכרי, he showed that he was a foreigner.

42:8.headline: Why didn't they recognize him? Beard, or brotherhood?
42:8.body: Rashi says Joseph left them beardless and came back with a beard. A second reading: he knew them as brothers and had pity, but they did not know him when they had him in their hands, and failed to treat him as a brother.

sources.quote: שֶׁיָּצָא מֵאֶצְלָם בְּלֹא חֲתִימַת זָקָן, וְעַכְשָׁו בָּא בַחֲתִימַת זָקָן
sources.says: Rashi says he left them without a full beard and now came with one.

sources.quote: הִכִּיר שֶׁהֵם אֶחָיו וְרִחֵם עֲלֵיהֶם, וְהֵם לֹא הִכִּירוּהוּ כְּשֶׁנָּפַל בְּיָדָם לִנְהֹג בּוֹ אַחְוָה
sources.says: Rashi says another reading is that he knew they were his brothers and pitied them, and they did not recognize him when he fell into their hands, to treat him as a brother.

42:9.headline: 'The nakedness of the land' means its weak spot
42:9.body: Rashi says ערוה in Scripture means something uncovered, here where the land is easy to conquer, and Rashbam says it means the breaks in the walls. Ibn Ezra reads it as a figure of speech for the land's hidden secret.

sources.quote: גִּלּוּי הָאָרֶץ – מֵהֵיכָן הִיא נוֹחָה לִכָּבֵשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the land's exposed place, from where it is easy to conquer.

sources.quote: ערות - פרצות החומות ומאיזה מקום נוחה ליכבש
sources.says: Rashbam says ערות means the breaches in the walls, and from which place it is easy to capture.

sources.quote: כך אתם באים לראות סוד הארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says: so you come to see the secret of the land.

42:11.headline: כנים means 'honest,' like 'so you said'
42:11.body: Rashi says כנים means true, from the same root as 'so you spoke.' Ibn Ezra says it means trustworthy and ties it to the same 'so' in Genesis 18:5 or Numbers 26:6.

sources.quote: כנים. אֲמִתִּיִּים, כְּמוֹ כֵּן דִּבַּרְתָּ
sources.says: Rashi says כנים means true, like 'so you spoke.'

sources.quote: כנים. נאמנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says כנים means trustworthy.

42:21.headline: אבל here means 'truly,' not 'but'
42:21.body: Rashi follows Onkelos: אבל means 'in truth.' He adds that in Bereshit Rabbah this is a Roman word for 'but.' Ibn Ezra says it is like 'truly, your wife Sarah' in Genesis 17:19.

sources.quote: אבל. כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ בְּקוּשְׁטָא
sources.says: Rashi says אבל is as Onkelos translates it, 'in truth.'

sources.quote: כמו "אבל שרה אשתך" (בראשית יז יט) כמו אכן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is like 'but Sarah your wife,' meaning 'indeed.'

42:22.headline: The word וגם adds a second blood to be repaid
42:22.body: Reuben says 'and also his blood is being demanded.' Rashi reads the extra word as adding more: his blood, and also the blood of the old man, their father.

sources.quote: אֵתִין וְגַמִּין רִבּוּיִין – דָּמוֹ וְגַם דַּם הַזָּקֵן
sources.says: Rashi says the words את and גם add more: his blood, and also the old man's blood.

42:24.headline: Why did Joseph take Simeon?
42:24.body: Rashi says Simeon was the one who threw Joseph in the pit and told Levi 'here comes the dreamer.' Rashbam says Joseph wanted to keep him away from Levi, so they could not plot together as they did at Shechem. Ibn Ezra says the eldest of the guilty is punished most, and Reuben was spared for saving him.

sources.quote: הוּא הִשְׁלִיכוֹ לַבּוֹר, הוּא שֶׁאָמַר לְלֵוִי הִנֵּה בַּעַל הַחֲלֹמוֹת הַלָּזֶה בָּא
sources.says: Rashi says it was he who threw him in the pit, and who said to Levi, 'Here comes this dreamer.'

sources.quote: להפרידו מלוי שלא יתייעצו בין שניהם לעשות תחבולה
sources.says: Rashbam says to separate him from Levi, so the two would not plot together.

sources.quote: כי כאשר יחטאו רבים הגדול שבהם בשנים יענש יותר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says that when many sin, the oldest among them is punished more.

42:24.headline: 'Bound before their eyes' means only for show
42:24.body: Rashi, quoting Bereshit Rabbah, says Joseph bound Simeon only in front of them. When they left, he took him out and fed him.

sources.quote: לֹא אֲסָרוֹ אֶלָּא לְעֵינֵיהֶם, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁיָּצְאוּ הוֹצִיאוֹ וְהֶאֱכִילוֹ וְהִשְׁקָהוּ
sources.says: Rashi says he was not bound except before their eyes, and once they left he was brought out, fed, and given drink.

42:27.headline: 'The one' who opened his sack: who was he?
42:27.body: Rashi, following the sages, says it was Levi, left alone after Simeon was taken. Ibn Ezra says it may have been Reuben, the firstborn, since 'one' can mean 'first' in counting.

sources.quote: הוּא לֵוִי, שֶׁנִּשְׁאַר יָחִיד מִשִּׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוּגוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it was Levi, who was left alone from Simeon, his partner.

sources.quote: ויתכן להיות ראובן כי הוא הבבור, כמו אחד בחשבון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may be Reuben, since he is the firstborn, like 'one' in counting.

42:34.headline: 'You will trade' comes from the word for going around
42:34.body: Rashi says תסחרו means you will go around. He adds that all words for traders and trade are named for going around and circling after goods.

sources.quote: תְּסוֹבְבוּ; וְכָל לְשׁוֹן סוֹחֲרִים וּסְחוֹרָה עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמְּחַזְרִים וְסוֹבְבִים אַחַר הַפְּרַקְמַטְיָא
sources.says: Rashi says it means you will go around, and that every word for traders and trade is named for going around after merchandise.

42:36.headline: 'You have bereaved me' hints Jacob suspected the brothers
42:36.body: Rashi says the word shows Jacob suspected they killed or sold Simeon as they had Joseph. He adds that anyone whose children are lost is called שכול.

sources.quote: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁחֲשָׁדָן שֶׁמָּא הֲרָגוּהוּ אוֹ מְכָרוּהוּ כְיוֹסֵף
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that he suspected them, lest they killed him or sold him like Joseph.

sources.quote: כָּל מִי שֶׁבָּנָיו אֲבוּדִים קָרוּי שַׁכּוּל
sources.says: Rashi says anyone whose sons are lost is called שכול.

42:37.headline: Reuben says 'kill my two sons.' Can that be literal?
42:37.body: Ibn Ezra reports that some say תמית means 'punish.' Rashi says Jacob rejected the offer as the words of a foolish firstborn: 'He says to kill his sons. Are they his sons and not mine?'

sources.quote: וי"א כי פי' תמית תעניש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some say תמית means 'you shall punish.'

sources.quote: אָמַר בְּכוֹר שׁוֹטֶה הוּא זֶה, הוּא אוֹמֵר לְהָמִית בָּנָיו, וְכִי בָנָיו הֵם וְלֹא בָּנַי
sources.says: Rashi says Jacob said: this is a foolish firstborn, he says to kill his sons, are they his sons and not mine?

43:2.headline: 'Finished eating' means the food ran out, not 'had enough'
43:2.body: Rashi says כלו here means the food was used up. He says the Aramaic reading 'when they had enough' is a mistake, since that fits camels finishing their drink, not people running out of grain.

sources.quote: כַּד שֵׁצִיאוּ, וְהַמְתַרְגֵּם כַּד סַפִּיקוּ טוֹעֶה
sources.says: Rashi says it is 'when they were finished,' and the translator who wrote 'when they had enough' is mistaken.

43:3.headline: The doubled העד העד is a formal warning in front of witnesses
43:3.body: Judah says 'the man warned us, warned us.' Rashi says העד means a warning, since a proper warning is given before witnesses. Radak says the same.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן הַתְרָאָה שֶׁסְּתָם הַתְרָאָה מַתְרֶה בוֹ בִּפְנֵי עֵדִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word of warning, since a plain warning is given before witnesses.

sources.quote: עִנְיַן הַתְרָאָה, לְפִי שֶׁאָדָם מַתְרֶה אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ בִּפְנֵי עֵדִים יֹאמְרוּ הַתְרָאָה בִּלְשׁוֹן הָעֵדָה
sources.says: Radak says it is about warning, since a person warns his friend before witnesses, and they call a warning an 'attesting.'

43:8.headline: 'And we will live' hints that Jacob's spirit will live again
43:8.body: Rashi says a spark of holy spirit spoke through Judah. By this journey, Jacob's spirit would revive, as it says later, 'the spirit of Jacob their father revived.'

sources.quote: נִצְנְצָה בוֹ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, עַל יְדֵי הֲלִיכָה זוֹ תְחִי רוּחֲךָ
sources.says: Rashi says a spark of holy spirit came into him: through this trip your spirit will live.

43:11.headline: 'The land's best' hears the word for singing its praise
43:11.body: This word appears only here. Rashi reads it, as Onkelos does, as the finest things of the land, the ones everyone sings about, and Ibn Ezra ties it to זמירות, songs.

sources.quote: מִדִּמְשַׁבַּח בְּאַרְעָא – שֶׁהַכֹּל מְזַמְּרִים עָלָיו כְּשֶׁהוּא בָא לָעוֹלָם
sources.says: Rashi says it means the best of the land, because everyone sings about it when it comes into the world.

sources.quote: כל דבר משובח מגזרת "זמירות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is anything praised, from the word for songs.

43:11.headline: Rashi admits he does not know what בטנים are
43:11.body: The word appears only here, and Rashi says he does not know what it means; he found a word in a lexicon and guesses peaches. Ibn Ezra says it has no match in Scripture and some say nuts, and Radak says pine nuts.

sources.quote: לֹא יָדַעְתִּי מַה הֵם, וּבְפֵרוּשֵׁי א"ב שֶׁל רַבִּי מָכִיר
sources.says: Rashi says he did not know what they are, and refers to the lexicon of Rabbi Machir.

sources.quote: אין אלו ריע במקרא, וי"א אגוזים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it has no partner in Scripture, and some say nuts.

sources.quote: הֵם הַנִּקְרָאִים צְנוֹבָר
sources.says: Radak says they are called pine nuts.

43:14.headline: 'El Shaddai' hears the word 'enough'
43:14.body: Rashi says שדי means one who has the power to give mercy, and adds the midrash: the one who said 'enough' (די) to the world will say 'enough' to my troubles. Ibn Ezra says it means one who has power.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ מִי שֶׁאָמַר לָעוֹלָם דַּי, יֹאמַר דַּי לְצָרוֹתַי
sources.says: Rashi says the midrash reads it: the one who said 'enough' to the world will say 'enough' to my troubles.

sources.quote: וטעם ואל שדי שיש לו כח לעשות כאלה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning of אל שדי is that he has the power to do such things.

43:14.headline: 'And he will send you your brother' means 'release'
43:14.body: Rashi says ושלח here is not 'send' but 'let go,' as in 'he shall go free.' The brothers are already going to Egypt, so 'send' would make no sense. Radak agrees.

sources.quote: וְיִפְטַר לְכוֹן כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ – יִפְטְרֶנּוּ מֵאֱסוּרָיו, לְשׁוֹן לַחָפְשִׁי יְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says 'and he will release for you,' as the Aramaic has it: he will free him from his bonds, like 'he shall send him free.'

sources.quote: יְשַׁלְּחֶנּוּ מִמַּאֲסָרוֹ
sources.says: Radak says he will release him from his imprisonment.

43:14.headline: 'Your other brother' hints at Joseph
43:14.body: Jacob says 'your other brother' and Benjamin. Rashi says a spark of holy spirit made him say this: the word hints at Joseph as well.

sources.quote: רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ נִזְרְקָה בוֹ, לְרַבּוֹת יוֹסֵף
sources.says: Rashi says the holy spirit was thrown into him, to include Joseph.

43:14.headline: 'As I am bereaved, I am bereaved' covers past and future
43:14.body: Rashi reads it as: until you return I am bereaved in doubt, and if I lose Benjamin I am bereaved of Joseph, Simeon and Benjamin. Rashbam compares it to 'if I am lost, I am lost.'

sources.quote: ואני. עַד שׁוּבְכֶם אֶהְיֶה שַׁכּוּל מִסָּפֵק
sources.says: Rashi says: until you return I will be bereaved in doubt.

sources.quote: כאשר שכלתי. מִיּוֹסֵף וּמִשִּׁמְעוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says 'as I was bereaved' means from Joseph and Simeon.

sources.quote: כמו: וכאשר אבדתי אבדתי
sources.says: Rashbam says it is like 'and if I am lost, I am lost.'

43:16.headline: 'At noon' can mean the first meal of the day
43:16.body: Rashi says Onkelos translates בצהרים as the first meal, though elsewhere the Aramaic for noon is different. Radak says it is midday, when rulers and judges eat.

sources.quote: זֶה מְתֻרְגָּם בְּשֵׁירוּתָא, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן סְעוּדָה רִאשׁוֹנָה בְלָשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
sources.says: Rashi says Onkelos translates it 'at the first meal,' a word for the first meal in Aramaic.

sources.quote: בַּחֲצִי הַיּוֹם שֶׁהוּא עֵת אֲכִילַת הַשָּׂרִים וְהַשּׁוֹפְטִים
sources.says: Radak says it means at midday, which is the time when the officials and judges eat.

43:18.headline: The rare verb להתגלל: roll the blame onto us
43:18.body: Rashi says it means the blame for the money would roll onto them, and Ramban compares it to a man rolled in blood. Ibn Ezra ties it to בגלל, 'because of.'

sources.quote: לִהְיוֹת מִתְגַּלְגֶּלֶת עָלֵינוּ עֲלִילַת הַכֶּסֶף וְלִהְיוֹתָהּ נוֹפֶלֶת עָלֵינוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the accusation about the money rolling onto us and falling on us.

sources.quote: מִן "וַעֲמָשָׂא מִתְגּוֹלֵל בַּדָּם
sources.says: Ramban compares it to 'and Amasa was wallowing in blood.'

sources.quote: מגזרת בגלל הדבר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from the root of 'because of the matter.'

43:18.headline: Why do the brothers fear for their donkeys?
43:18.body: Ramban says they worried that their donkeys would be taken along with their sacks. Maimonides, in the Guide, cites this verse to show that people value their property like their own lives.

sources.quote: וְטַעַם וְלָקַחַת אֹתָנוּ לַעֲבָדִים וְאֶת חֲמֹרֵינוּ כִּי יִדְאֲגוּ עַל חֲמוֹרֵיהֶם
sources.says: Ramban says the meaning of 'to take us as slaves and our donkeys' is that they worried about their donkeys.

sources.quote: וההתייחסות אליהם בשווה היא דבר נפוץ: "וְלָקַחַת אֹתָנוּ לַעֲבָדִים וְאֶת חֲמֹרֵינוּ" (בראשית מג,יח
sources.says: Maimonides says treating the two the same is common, and cites 'to take us for slaves and our donkeys.'

43:20.headline: 'בי אדני' is a plea, not 'in me, my lord'
43:20.body: Rashi says בי is a word of asking and begging, like the Aramaic ביא ביא. Ibn Ezra says it is a short form, like 'on me, my lord, be the guilt,' and means: do with me what you will.

sources.quote: בי אדני. לְשׁוֹן בַּעְיָא וְתַחֲנוּנִים הוּא, בְלָשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי בַּיָּא בַּיָּא
sources.says: Rashi says בי אדני is a word of asking and pleading, in Aramaic ביא ביא.

sources.quote: לשון בקשה, ולפי דעתי שהוא דרך קצרה, כמו בי אני אדני העון
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is a word of request, and in his view a short way of speaking, like 'on me, my lord, be the guilt.'

43:20.headline: 'We came down' also means 'we have come down in the world'
43:20.body: Rashi says ירד ירדנו is a descent in status. They used to feed others, and now they need Joseph.

sources.quote: יְרִידָה הִיא לָנוּ, רְגִילִים הָיִינוּ לְפַרְנֵס אֲחֵרִים, עַכְשָׁו אָנוּ צְרִיכִים לְךָ
sources.says: Rashi says it is a descent for us: we used to feed others, and now we need you.

43:28.headline: 'Bowed their heads and bowed down' are two different bows
43:28.body: Rashi says ויקדו is a bowing of the head, and וישתחוו is lying flat on the ground. Ibn Ezra says ויקדו means they put the head to the ground.

sources.quote: קִידָה – כְּפִיפַת קָדְקֹד; הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה – מִשְׁתַּטֵּחַ לָאָרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says קידה is bending the head, and השתחואה is lying flat on the ground.

sources.quote: שמו הקדקד בארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they put the head on the ground.

43:29.headline: Joseph blesses Benjamin with 'grace,' a blessing the other sons had
43:29.body: Rashi says the other tribes were born with talk of graciousness, as in 'God has graciously given your servant.' Benjamin was not yet born then, so Joseph gave him that blessing.

sources.quote: וּבִנְיָמִין עֲדַיִן לֹא נוֹלַד, לְכָךְ בֵּרְכוֹ יוֹסֵף בַּחֲנִינָה
sources.says: Rashi says Benjamin had not yet been born, so Joseph blessed him with graciousness.

43:30.headline: The rare verb נכמרו means his feelings burned
43:30.body: Rashi says נכמרו means they were heated, like skin shriveling in heat, as in 'our skin is hot as an oven.' Ibn Ezra says they burned and glowed, with the same Lamentations verse.

sources.quote: נכמרו. נִתְחַמְּמוּ, וּבִלְשׁוֹן מִשְׁנָה עַל הַכֹּמֶר שֶׁל זֵתִים
sources.says: Rashi says נכמרו means they were warmed, and in the language of the Mishnah it is used of the pressing of olives.

sources.quote: כי נכמרו. בערו ויקדו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they burned and blazed.

43:31.headline: 'He held himself in' is tied to the word for strong
43:31.body: Rashi says ויתאפק means he strengthened himself, from אפיק, the strong shields in Job. Radak says he held himself back from weeping any more.

sources.quote: ויתאפק. נִתְאַמֵּץ; וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן אֲפִיקֵי מָגִנִּים
sources.says: Rashi says he strengthened himself, a word like 'strong shields.'

sources.quote: הִתְחַזֵּק בְּעַצְמוֹ מִלִּבְכּוֹת עוֹד
sources.says: Radak says he strengthened himself from weeping any more.

43:32.headline: Why was eating with Hebrews 'an abomination' to Egyptians?
43:32.body: Rashi says it was hateful to the Egyptians to eat with Hebrews, and that Onkelos gives the reason: Hebrews eat the animals the Egyptians worship. Rashbam says the Egyptians looked down on people from across the river.
