49:17.body: Rashi says שפיפן is a snake, named for how it 'bruises' the heel, as in 'you shall bruise his heel'. Ibn Ezra links it to a word for crushing the head.

sources.quote: שפיפן. הוּא נָחָשׁ; וְאוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁקָּרוּי כֵּן עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהוּא נוֹשֵׁף
sources.says: Rashi says שפיפן is a snake, and he thinks it is named for its striking.

sources.quote: גם יתכן להיות פי' שפיפון מגזרת הוא ישופך ראש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it may come from the word in 'he shall bruise your head'.

49:18.headline: 'I hope for your salvation, Lord': whose salvation?
49:18.body: Jacob suddenly breaks off to speak to God. Rashi says he foresaw Samson being blinded and praying at the end, Ibn Ezra says he feared for Dan the snake, and Rashbam says it is Dan's own salvation he hopes for.

sources.quote: נִתְנַבֵּא שֶׁיְּנַקְּרוּ פְּלִשְׁתִּים אֶת עֵינָיו
sources.says: Rashi says he prophesied that the Philistines would put out Samson's eyes.

sources.quote: בעבור שהוא נושך עקבי סוס יפחד מרוכב הסוס שלא ישוף ראשו בחרבו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says because he bites the horse's heels, he will fear the rider crushing his head with his sword.

sources.quote: קויתי ה' - שיושיע אותך וישגבך על האומות
sources.says: Rashbam says 'I hope in the Lord' means that He will save you and lift you above the nations.

49:19.headline: 'Gad, a troop shall troop on him': a play on Gad's name
49:19.body: The verse repeats the sound of Gad's name, גד, in the words for troop. Rashi says all of them come from גדוד and cites Menachem's dictionary, and Ibn Ezra says an army will come on Gad, who will beat it in the end.

sources.quote: כֻּלָּם לְשׁוֹן גְּדוּד הֵם, וְכָךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם
sources.says: Rashi says all of them are from the word for troop, and so Menachem grouped them.

sources.quote: התנבא שיבא עליו גדוד, והוא ינצחנו באחרונה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it prophesies that a troop will come on Gad, and he will beat it in the end.

49:19.headline: 'He will troop at the heel': Gad returns on their heels
49:19.body: Rashi says עקב is their path and tracks: Gad's troops will return the way they went, to their land east of the Jordan, with no one lost. Rashbam says Gad guards the rear of Israel's army.

sources.quote: כָּל גְּדוּדָיו יָשׁוּבוּ עַל עֲקֵבָם לְנַחֲלָתָם שֶׁלָּקְחוּ בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן, וְלֹא יִפָּקֵד מֵהֶם אִישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says all his troops will return on their heels to their inheritance across the Jordan, and none of them will be missing.

sources.quote: ובשוב גד מן המלחמה ישובו של גד אחר עקיבן של ישראל
sources.says: Rashbam says that when Gad returns from war, Gad will be behind Israel's heels, as a rearguard.

49:21.headline: 'A doe let loose': a fast-ripening valley, or Deborah
49:21.body: Rashi says the doe is the valley of Gennesaret, whose fruit ripens as quickly as a doe runs. Ibn Ezra says it is a gift, or some say it hints at Deborah.

sources.quote: זוֹ בִקְעַת גִּינוֹסַר שֶׁהִיא קַלָּה לְבַשֵּׁל פֵּרוֹתֶיהָ כְּאַיָּלָה
sources.says: Rashi says this is the Gennesaret valley, which ripens its fruit as quickly as a deer.

sources.quote: וי"א שאילה רמז לדבורה, הנותן אמרי שפר, רמז לשירת ברק עמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some say the doe hints at Deborah, and 'words of beauty' at Barak's song with her.

49:21.headline: 'Words of beauty': a victory song, or words at the burial
49:21.body: Rashi says the words are the song of Deborah and Barak, or, as the rabbis read it, what was said on the day Jacob was buried, when Esau disputed the cave. Rashbam says the fast runners brought good news home from war.

sources.quote: עַל יָדָם שָׁרוּ דְּבוֹרָה וּבָרָק שִׁירָה
sources.says: Rashi says Deborah and Barak sang their song through them.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דְּרָשׁוּהוּ עַל יוֹם קְבוּרַת יַעֲקֹב כְּשֶׁעִרְעֵר עֵשָׂו עַל הַמְּעָרָה
sources.says: Rashi says the rabbis applied it to the day Jacob was buried, when Esau disputed the cave.

sources.quote: בשובם מן המלחמה ממהרים מתוך קלותם לבשר בשורות משופרות של נצחון המלחמה
sources.says: Rashbam says that on returning from war they hurry, in their lightness, to carry good tidings of victory.

49:22.headline: 'Fruitful son' (בן פרת): grace, branches, or growing
49:22.body: Rashi says בן פרת means 'a son of grace', and also fruitfulness, while Ibn Ezra links the word to the 'branches' in Ezekiel. Rashbam says it means a son who is fruitful and grows.

sources.quote: בן פרת. בֶּן חֵן, וְהוּא לְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
sources.says: Rashi says בן פרת means a son of grace, in an Aramaic word.

sources.quote: פֹּרָת לְשׁוֹן פִּרְיָה וּרְבִיָּה
sources.says: Rashi also says פרת is a word of fruitfulness and increase.

sources.quote: ויש מי שפי' אותה מלשון "ותשלח פארות"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some explain it from 'and sent out branches'.

sources.quote: בן פורת יוסף - בן הפורה וגדל יוסף
sources.says: Rashbam says בן פורת means a son who is fruitful and grows.

49:22.headline: 'Over the eye': charm, a shield from the evil eye, or height
49:22.body: Rashi says Joseph's charm is drawn to the eye of whoever sees him, and that it also means no evil eye rules over his descendants. He adds that Joseph stood tall in front of his mother Rachel to shield her from Esau's eye.

sources.quote: חִנּוֹ נָטוּי עַל הָעַיִן הָרוֹאָה אוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says his grace is stretched over the eye of the one who sees him.

sources.quote: אָמַר יוֹסֵף רָשָׁע הַזֶּה עֵינוֹ רָמָה, שֶׁמָּא יִתֵּן עֵינָיו בְּאִמִּי, יָצָא לְפָנֶיהָ וְשִׁרְבֵּב קוֹמָתוֹ לְכַסּוֹתָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says Joseph feared the wicked one's high eye, so he stepped in front of his mother and stretched up to cover her.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלֹט בְּזַרְעוֹ עַיִן הָרָע
sources.says: Rashi says it also means the evil eye will not rule over his descendants.

sources.quote: גדל ורבה על עין להסתכל למעלה מן העין, בקומתו וביופיו
sources.says: Rashbam says he grew great over the eye, so that people look up at him, in his height and beauty.

49:22.headline: The 'daughters': Egyptian women, Zelophehad's daughters, or branches
49:22.body: Rashi says the daughters are the women of Egypt who climbed the walls to see Joseph, and in Onkelos' reading they are Manasseh's daughters, the daughters of Zelophehad. Ibn Ezra says they are the branches of the fruitful plant.

sources.quote: בְּנוֹת מִצְרַיִם הָיוּ צוֹעֲדוֹת (עַל הַחוֹמָה) לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בְּיָפְיוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the women of Egypt used to climb the wall to look at his beauty.

sources.quote: וְכָתַב בָּנוֹת עַל שֵׁם בְּנוֹת מְנַשֶּׁה, בְּנוֹת צְלָפְחָד
sources.says: Rashi reports Onkelos' reading: it says 'daughters' for the daughters of Manasseh, the daughters of Zelophehad.

sources.quote: שיוסף היה כבן פרת, ועשה בנות, צעדה כל אחת ואחת מהן על החומה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Joseph was like a fruitful plant that made daughters, each one climbing on the wall.

49:23.headline: ורבו: they shot arrows, or they quarrelled with him
49:23.body: Rashi says it is not 'shot' but 'became men of strife': his brothers turned into people who quarrelled with him. Rashbam says it repeats the arrows in the verse.

sources.quote: נַעֲשׂוּ לוֹ אֶחָיו אַנְשֵׁי רִיב
sources.says: Rashi says his brothers became men of strife toward him.

sources.quote: ורבו - כפל לשון של חצים שבפסוק
sources.says: Rashbam says ורבו doubles the word for 'arrows' in the verse.

49:23.headline: 'Masters of arrows': those whose tongues hurt like arrows
49:23.body: Rashi says the 'arrows' are tongues, and that the phrase also points to those who had a right to share his inheritance. Rashbam says it is Potiphar's wife's slander.

sources.quote: שֶׁלְּשׁוֹנָם כַּחֵץ
sources.says: Rashi says it means those whose tongue is like an arrow.

sources.quote: ומדמה הפסוק לשון הרע של פוטיפר לחצים
sources.says: Rashbam says the verse compares the slander of Potiphar's wife to arrows.

49:24.headline: ויפזו: golden, scattered, strengthened, or leaping
49:24.body: Rashi says it is from the word for fine gold, the ring Joseph was given, and that the sages read it as 'scattered', the seed that went out from his fingers. Ibn Ezra says it means strengthened, and Rashbam says bent, like David dancing.

sources.quote: זוֹ הִיא נְתִינַת טַבַּעַת עַל יָדוֹ, לְשׁוֹן זָהָב מוּפָז
sources.says: Rashi says this is the giving of a ring on his hand, from the word for refined gold.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ וַיָּפוֹצוּ, שֶׁיָּצָא הַזֶּרַע מִבֵּין אֶצְבְּעוֹת יָדָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is like 'scattered', since the seed went out from between his fingers.

sources.quote: ויפוזו, ויתחזקו והקרוב אלי "מפזז"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means they were strengthened, and that the closest word is 'leaping' in Samuel.

sources.quote: ויפוזו - נכפפו. כמו: ויהי דוד מפזז ומכרכר
sources.says: Rashbam says ויפוזו means they were bent, like 'David was leaping and dancing'.

49:24.headline: 'His bow' stood firm: strength, and seed that shoots like an arrow
49:24.body: Rashi says 'bow' means strength. He also notes the rabbis read the bow as Joseph's restraint in Potiphar's house, since seed is shot like an arrow.

sources.quote: קשתו. חָזְקוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says קשתו means his strength.

sources.quote: וְקוֹרְאוֹ קֶשֶׁת, עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהַזֶּרַע יוֹרֶה כַּחֵץ
sources.says: Rashi says it is called a bow because seed shoots like an arrow.

49:24.headline: 'Stone of Israel' also reads as 'father and son'
49:24.body: Rashi says אבן can be an acronym for אב ובן, 'father and son', Jacob and his sons, and that it also means the head stone, a sign of kingship. Rashbam says אבן means 'father and family'.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן נוֹטָרִיקוֹן אָב וּבֵן, אֲבָהָן וּבְנִין – יַעֲקֹב וּבָנָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it is an acronym of 'father and son', that is, Jacob and his sons.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן הָאֶבֶן הָרֹאשָׁה, לְשׁוֹן מַלְכוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it also means the head stone, a word of kingship.

sources.quote: אבן לשון אב ומשפחה
sources.says: Rashbam says אבן means 'father and family'.

49:25.headline: 'Blessings of breasts and womb': a play on 'shoot'
49:25.body: Rashi says שדים is linked to 'shoot', as seed shoots like an arrow, and Ibn Ezra says the breasts match the heavens and the womb matches the deep. Rashbam says it means the breasts will not dry up.

sources.quote: יָרֹה יִיָּרֶה מְתַּרְגְּמִינַן אִשְׁתְּדָאָה יִשְׁתְּדִי, אַף שָׁדַיִם כָּאן עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהַזֶּרַע יוֹרֶה כַּחֵץ
sources.says: Rashi says 'shoot' is translated with a word like שדי, and so שדים here is because seed shoots like an arrow.

sources.quote: דמה השדים לשמים והרחם לתהום
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he compared the breasts to the heavens and the womb to the deep.

sources.quote: שלא יהא השדים צומקים ולא ימותו הילדים מחוסר חלב
sources.says: Rashbam says it means the breasts will not dry up and the children will not die for lack of milk.

49:26.headline: 'My parents': those who conceived me, or the mountains
49:26.body: Rashi and Ibn Ezra say הורי means those who conceived me, my parents. Rashbam says it matches 'ancient hills' in the same verse, so it means mountains.

sources.quote: הורי. לְשׁוֹן הֵרָיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says הורי is a word of pregnancy.

sources.quote: והורי כמו יולדי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says הורי is like 'those who gave birth to me'.

sources.quote: כי הורי לשון כפל של גבעות עולם
sources.says: Rashbam says הורי repeats the phrase 'ancient hills'.

49:26.headline: תאות is found only here: 'limit', or 'desire'
49:26.body: Rashi says עד תאות means to the ends, like 'you shall mark out for yourselves' in Numbers, and that Onkelos reads it as desire. Ibn Ezra also links it to the Numbers word, and Rashbam says it means 'to the end'.

sources.quote: עד תאות. עַד קְצוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says עד תאות means to the ends.

sources.quote: וְאֻנְקְלוֹס תִּרְגֵּם תַּאֲוַת עוֹלָם לְשׁוֹן תַּאֲוָה וְחֶמְדָה
sources.says: Rashi says Onkelos translates it as desire and longing.

sources.quote: תאות. מגזרת "והתאויתם"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says תאות comes from the word 'and you shall mark out'.

sources.quote: עד תאות - עד סוף
sources.says: Rashbam says עד תאות means to the end.

49:26.headline: 'The נזיר among his brothers': set apart, or crowned
49:26.body: Rashi says it means set apart from his brothers, and Ibn Ezra links it to נזר, a crown. Rashbam says it means a king over his brothers.

sources.quote: פְּרִישָׁא דַּאֲחוֹהִי, שֶׁנִּבְדַּל מֵאֶחָיו
sources.says: Rashi says it means separated from his brothers.

sources.quote: נזיר אחיו. מגזרת נזר והוא סמוך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נזיר comes from נזר, a crown.

sources.quote: נזיר אחיו - מלך על אחיו
sources.says: Rashbam says it means a king over his brothers.

49:27.headline: 'Benjamin is a wolf': the snatchers at Gibeah, or Saul's wars
49:27.body: Rashi says the wolf points to the snatching of wives at Gibeah, and to Saul, who beat his enemies on every side. Ibn Ezra says it shows Benjamin was mighty, as the men of Gibeah showed.

sources.quote: נִבָּא עַל שֶׁיִּהְיוּ עֲתִידִין לִהְיוֹת חַטְפָנִין
sources.says: Rashi says he prophesied that they would become snatchers.

sources.quote: דמהו לזאב כי גבור היה והאות אנשי הגבעה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says he compared him to a wolf because he was mighty, and the sign is the men of Gibeah.

49:27.headline: עד is a rare word here for plunder, not 'until'
49:27.body: In 'in the morning he eats עד', Rashi says עד means plunder, as Onkelos translates, and cites Isaiah. Ibn Ezra says the same.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן בִּזָּה וְשָׁלָל, הַמְתֻרְגָּם עֲדָאָה, וְעוֹד יֵשׁ לוֹ דּוֹמֶה בִּלְשׁוֹן עִבְרִית אָז חֻלַּק עַד שָׁלָל
sources.says: Rashi says it is a word for spoil and plunder, which Onkelos translates, with a Hebrew parallel in 'then the plunder of booty is divided'.

sources.quote: עד, תרגום שלל וכן "אז חלק עד שלל"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says עד is the Aramaic word for plunder, as in Isaiah.

49:27.headline: 'Morning' and 'evening' in Benjamin's blessing: Saul, and then Esther
49:27.body: Rashi says the morning is Saul at the start of Israel's rise, and the evening is after Israel's sun sets in Babylon, when Mordecai and Esther, of Benjamin, take Haman's spoil. Ibn Ezra calls this a homiletic reading.

sources.quote: עָמַד בִּתְחִלַּת פְּרִיחָתָן וּזְרִיחָתָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says the morning is Saul, who arose at the start of Israel's blossoming and rising.

sources.quote: אַף מִשֶּׁתִּשְׁקַע שִׁמְשָׁן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר, שֶׁיַּגְלֵם לְבָבֶל, יחלק שלל, מָרְדְּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר
sources.says: Rashi says even after Israel's sun sets at Nebuchadnezzar's hand, Mordecai and Esther will divide the spoil.

sources.quote: וטעם בבקר בתחלת המלכות ולערב בגלותם על דבר מרדכי וזהו דרך דרש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the morning is the start of the kingdom and the evening their exile, with Mordecai, and that this is the way of homily.

49:28.headline: 'He blessed them': even the sons he rebuked
49:28.body: Rashi asks how this fits, since some sons were only rebuked, and answers that 'blessed' includes all of them. Ibn Ezra says each blessing fit each son, like a dream interpreted for each.

sources.quote: וַהֲלֹא יֵשׁ מֵהֶם שֶׁלֹּא בֵרְכָם אֶלָּא קִנְטְרָן
sources.says: Rashi asks: but are there not some of them whom he did not bless but only rebuked?

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁנָּתַן לִיהוּדָה גְּבוּרַת אֲרִי וּלְבִנְיָמִין חֲטִיפָתוֹ שֶׁל זְאֵב
sources.says: Rashi says it adds 'them' because Judah was given a lion's strength and Benjamin a wolf's snatching.

sources.quote: איש אשר כברכתו. כאשר באה לכל אחד מהברכות כן ברך אותם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says as each of the blessings came to each one, so he blessed them.

49:29.headline: 'Gathered to my people': the soul is brought in
49:29.body: Rashi says אסיפה means bringing something in, as when grain is gathered into the house. So 'gathered to my people' means the souls are brought into their place of rest.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁמַּכְנִיסִין הַנְּפָשׁוֹת אֶל מְקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָן
sources.says: Rashi says it is because souls are brought into the place of their storage.

49:33.headline: The verse says Jacob 'expired', but never that he 'died'
49:33.body: Rashi notes that the verse does not use the word for death. He adds the teaching that Jacob our father did not die.

sources.quote: וּמִיתָה לֹא נֶאֶמְרָה בוֹ, וְאָ"רַ יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת
sources.says: Rashi says death is not said of him, and the saying is that Jacob our father did not die.

5:1.headline: ספר here means a count, not a book
5:1.body: The phrase 'this is the book of the generations of Adam' opens a list of names and ages. Rashi calls it a counting, and Radak says ספר here means a count, since it counts the generations from Adam to Noah.

sources.says: Rashi says this is a counting of the generations of Adam.
sources.quote: זוֹ הִיא סְפִירַת תּוֹלְדוֹת אָדָם,

sources.says: Radak says ספר here means counting, because it counts the generations from Adam to Noah.
sources.quote: עִנְיַן חֶשְׁבּוֹן, כִּי הוּא סוֹפֵר שְׁנֵי הַתּוֹלָדוֹת מֵאָדָם וְעַד נֹחַ,

5:2.headline: אדם is the name God gave to both man and woman
5:2.body: The verse says God called them אדם, meaning both. Radak says the woman is called אדם too, and Ramban says the name covers the whole human kind.

sources.says: Radak says the woman is also called אדם.
sources.quote: וְהָאִשָּׁה נִקְרֵאת אָדָם

sources.says: Ramban says the name אדם covers the whole human kind.
sources.quote: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשֵּׁם אָדָם כְּלָל לְכָל הַמִּין הָאֱנוֹשִׁי,

5:24.headline: 'God took him' may mean Enoch died
5:24.body: The verb לקח can mean 'took away' or 'took in death'. Ibn Ezra says here it means he died, like 'take my life' in Jonah, and Rashi says it means before his time.

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means he died, like 'take my life' in Jonah.
sources.quote: מת וכן "קח נא את נפשי"

sources.says: Rashi says it means before his time, like 'I am taking the delight of your eyes'.
sources.quote: לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ, כְּמוֹ הִנְנִי לֹקֵחַ מִמְּךָ אֶת מַחְמַד עֵינֶיךָ

5:28.headline: 'A son' (בן) sounds like the world being 'built' (נבנה)
5:28.body: The verse says Lemech had 'a son' without naming him yet. Rashi says it is because the world was built from him, and Chizkuni gives the same reason.

sources.says: Rashi says the world was built from him.
sources.quote: שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ נִבְנָה הָעוֹלָם

sources.says: Chizkuni says it was because the world was built from him: all the world was destroyed and only he and his sons were left.
sources.quote: לפי שממנו נבנה העולם שכל העולם חרב והוא ובניו נשארו.

50:3.headline: Why did Egypt weep seventy days for Jacob?
50:3.body: Rashi and Radak say forty days were for embalming and thirty for mourning, and Rashi adds that Egypt wept because the famine ended in Jacob's merit. Chizkuni offers another view: Jacob's seventy descendants each wept one day.

sources.quote: מ' לַחֲנִיטָה וְל' לִבְכִיָּה, לְפִי שֶׁבָּאָה לָהֶם בְּרָכָה לְרַגְלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says forty days were for embalming and thirty for weeping, because blessing came to them at his feet.

sources.quote: אַרְבָּעִים שֶׁל חֲנֻטָּה, וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שֶׁל בְּכִי שֶׁעוֹשִׂין לְכָל אָדָם גָּדוֹל
sources.says: Radak says forty days of embalming and thirty of weeping, which are made for any great person.

sources.quote: ד״א שבעים יוצאי ירכו יורדי מצרים בכוהו איש יומו
sources.says: Chizkuni gives another view: the seventy descendants who went down to Egypt each wept for him a day.

50:5.headline: 'The grave I dug for myself': dug, bought, or piled up?
50:5.body: Rashi says the plain sense is 'dug', as in 'if a man digs a pit'. The sages also read it as 'bought', and as 'a heap', the pile of silver and gold Jacob gave Esau for his share in the cave.

sources.quote: כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ כְּמוֹ כִּי יִכְרֶה אִישׁ
sources.says: Rashi says on the plain sense it is like 'if a man digs'.

sources.quote: וּמִדְרָשׁוֹ עוֹד מִתְיַשֵּׁב עַל הַלָּשׁוֹן, כְּמוֹ אֲשֶׁר קָנִיתִי
sources.says: Rashi says a midrash settles the wording as 'which I bought'.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן כְּרִי דָגוּר, שֶׁנָּטַל יַעֲקֹב כָּל כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב
sources.says: Rashi says another midrash reads it as 'a heap', since Jacob took all his silver and gold and piled it up.

sources.quote: אשר כריתי. חפרתי כמו "כי יכרה איש"
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says אשר כריתי means 'which I dug', as in 'if a man digs'.

50:10.headline: 'The threshing floor of the thorn-bush': the kings hung their crowns
50:10.body: Rashi says the floor was ringed with thorn-bushes. The sages explain the name from the event: the kings of Canaan hung their crowns on Jacob's coffin and surrounded it like a hedge of thorns.

sources.quote: מֻקָּף אֲטָדִין הָיָה, וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ (סוטה י"ג), עַל שֵׁם הַמְּאֹרָע
sources.says: Rashi says it was surrounded by thorn-bushes, and the rabbis explained the name from the event.

sources.quote: תָלוּ בוֹ כִתְרֵיהֶם וְהִקִּיפוּהוּ כְּתָרִים כְּגֹרֶן הַמֻּקָּף סְיָג שֶׁל קוֹצִים
sources.says: Rashi says they hung their crowns on it and surrounded it with crowns, like a threshing floor ringed with a fence of thorns.

50:13.headline: Why only Jacob's sons carried his bier, not his grandsons
50:13.body: Rashi says Jacob ordered it, because his grandsons were partly Canaanite. He says the sons stood on four sides in the order of the tribal camps.

sources.quote: וְלֹא בְנֵי בָנָיו, שֶׁכָּךְ צִוָּם, אַל יִשְׂאוּ מִטָּתִי לֹא אִישׁ מִצְרִי וְלֹא אֶחָד מִבְּנֵיכֶם, שֶׁהֵם מִבְּנוֹת כְּנַעַן
sources.says: Rashi says not his grandsons, since he commanded: let no Egyptian carry my bed, nor any of your sons, who are from Canaanite women.

50:15.headline: 'The brothers saw their father was dead': what did they see?
50:15.body: Rashi says they noticed it at Joseph's table: he used to draw them near for their father's sake, and after Jacob died he stopped. Chizkuni says Joseph passed the pit on the way home and blessed God there, and the brothers feared he was remembering.

sources.quote: הִכִּירוּ בְּמִיתָתוֹ אֵצֶל יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִים לִסְעֹד עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף וְהָיָה מְקָרְבָן בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹד אָבִיו, וּמִשֶּׁמֵּת יַעֲקֹב לֹא קֵרְבָן
sources.says: Rashi says they recognised Jacob's death in Joseph's behaviour, since he used to bring them near for their father's honour, and after he died he did not.

sources.quote: יוסף כששב מקבורת אביו עבר על בור שהשליכוהו אחיו וברך עליו
sources.says: Chizkuni says that when Joseph returned from burying his father he passed the pit they threw him into, and blessed God over it.

50:15.headline: 'Perhaps Joseph will hate us': the small word לו
50:15.body: Rashi says לו can mean 'if only', 'if', or 'perhaps', and here it means 'perhaps', which is found nowhere else in Scripture. Ibn Ezra reads it the same way, 'perhaps he will keep hatred against us'.

sources.quote: לו ישטמנו. שֶׁמָּא יִשְׂטְמֵנוּ; לוּ מִתְחַלֵּק לְעִנְיָנִים הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says לו ישטמנו means 'perhaps he will hate us', and that לו divides into many senses.

sources.quote: לו ישטמנו. שמא יטור לנו איבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says לו ישטמנו means perhaps he will bear us enmity.

50:16.headline: 'They commanded': they sent word through messengers
50:16.body: Rashi says ויצוו means the brothers sent messengers to Joseph, the sons of Bilhah, who were close to him. Sforno says they instructed Jacob's servants or others.

sources.quote: וְאֶת מִי צִוּוּ? אֶת בְּנֵי בִלְהָה, שֶׁהָיוּ רְגִילִין אֶצְלוֹ
sources.says: Rashi asks whom they commanded, and answers: the sons of Bilhah, who were close to him.

sources.quote: צִוּוּ לְעַבְדֵי יַעֲקֹב אוֹ זוּלָתָם עַל אוֹדוֹת יוֹסֵף
sources.says: Sforno says they instructed Jacob's servants or others about Joseph.

50:17.headline: 'Servants of the God of your father': the God who stays
50:17.body: The brothers call themselves servants of Jacob's God. Rashi says the point is that if their father is dead, his God lives, and they are His servants.

sources.quote: אִם אָבִיךָ מֵת, אֱלֹהָיו קַיָּם, וְהֵם עֲבָדָיו
sources.says: Rashi says if your father has died, his God lives, and they are His servants.

50:21.headline: 'He spoke to their heart': words the heart can accept
50:21.body: Rashi says these are words that sink into the heart. Joseph reminded them that the brothers had proved he was a free man, and that killing them would look terrible.

sources.quote: דְּבָרִים הַמִּתְקַבְּלִים עַל הַלֵּב
sources.says: Rashi says these are words that the heart accepts.

50:23.headline: 'Born on Joseph's knees': born, or raised there
50:23.body: Rashi, as Onkelos translates, says Joseph raised them between his knees. Ibn Ezra says ילדו here means 'grew up'.

sources.quote: על ברכי יוסף. כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ גִּדְּלָן בֵּין בִּרְכָּיו
sources.says: Rashi says, as Onkelos translates, he raised them between his knees.

sources.quote: ילדו. גדלו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ילדו means they grew up.

50:26.headline: 'In the ark', with a long vowel: the one prepared for him
50:26.body: Chizkuni says the long vowel under the ב means 'the ark' they had chosen and prepared for him in his lifetime. Ibn Ezra says the same, that he prepared it for himself.

sources.quote: בארון הב׳ בקמץ ללמדך שבחייו בחרוהו לו והכינוהו
sources.says: Chizkuni says the ב has a long vowel to teach that they chose it and prepared it for him in his life.

sources.quote: וטעם בארון בקמצות הבי"ת הוא שהכין לנפשו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the meaning of the long vowel in בארון is that he prepared it for himself.

6:2.headline: 'Sons of God' may mean sons of judges and rulers
6:2.body: The word אלהים can mean 'God' or 'a judge or ruler'. Rashi, Radak and Onkelos read בני האלהים as sons of rulers, and Rashi adds that every אלהים in Scripture can mean authority.

sources.says: Rashi says 'sons of God' means the sons of the rulers and the judges.
sources.quote: בְּנֵי הַשָּׂרִים וְהַשּׁוֹפְטִים.

sources.says: Rashi says every אלהים in Scripture is a word of authority.
sources.quote: כָּל אֱלֹהִים שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן מָרוּת,

sources.says: Onkelos puts it as 'the sons of the great ones'.
sources.quote: וַחֲזוֹ בְנֵי רַבְרְבַיָּא

sources.says: Radak says it means the sons of the judges, the great, and the rulers of the lands.
sources.quote: בְּנֵי הַשּׁוֹפְטִים וְהַגְּדוֹלִים וּמַנְהִיגֵי הַמְּדִינוֹת,

6:3.headline: ידון: God's spirit will not 'quarrel', 'judge', or 'stay sheathed'
6:3.body: The verb ידון is hard to place. Rashi reads it as God's spirit quarreling within Him, while Ibn Ezra gives two other readings: the body as the spirit's sheath, or the spirit as a judge in the body.

sources.says: Rashi says it means God's spirit will not complain and quarrel on account of man.
sources.quote: לֹא יִתְרַעֵם וְיָרִיב רוּחִי עָלַי בִּשְׁבִיל הָאָדָם

sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a reading where the body is a sheath for the spirit.
sources.quote: יש אומר שהוא כמו וישב חרבו אל נדנה (דה"א כא כז) כי הגוף לרוח כנדן

sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a reading from the word for judging: the spirit is a judge in the body.
sources.quote: וי"א שמשקלו כמו "וישב העפר" (קהלת יב ז) והוא מגזרת דין כי הרוח דיין בגוף:

6:11.headline: חמס means robbery, and it sealed the verdict
6:11.body: Rashi says חמס here means robbery, and that the verdict was sealed only because of it. Ibn Ezra says it includes theft, extortion, and taking women by force.

sources.says: Rashi says חמס means robbery.
sources.quote: ותמלא הארץ חמס. גֶּזֶל:

sources.says: Rashi says their verdict was sealed only because of robbery.
sources.quote: לֹא נֶחְתַּם גְּזַר דִּינָם אֶלָּא עַל הַגֶּזֶל

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it includes robbery, extortion, and taking women by force.
sources.quote: בגזל ועשק וקחת גם הנשים בחזקה

6:14.headline: תבה means a box, not a ship
6:14.body: Ibn Ezra says the word is a box or chest, and not a ship, since it has no oars and not the shape of a ship.

sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is called a תיבה, not a ship, because it is not shaped like a ship and has no oars.
sources.quote: ושם תיבה ולא ספינה, כי איננה על צורת אניה ואין לה משוטים:

7:1.headline: God calls Noach 'righteous' but leaves out 'whole'
7:1.body: In chapter 6 Noach is called 'righteous and whole', but here God says only 'righteous'. Rashi says this teaches that you may praise a person in part to his face, and in full only when he is not there.

sources.says: Rashi says the verse leaves out 'whole' to teach that a person's praise is told in part to his face, and in full out of his sight.
sources.quote: וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר צַדִּיק תָּמִים, מִכָּאן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מִקְצַת שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בְּפָנָיו וְכֻלּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו

7:11.headline: Measure for measure: 'great' wickedness met a 'great' deep
7:11.body: The verse says the great deep, תהום רבה, burst open. Rashi hears an echo of 'רבה רעת האדם', 'great was the evil of man': they sinned with great evil and were struck with a great deep.

sources.says: Rashi says it was measure for measure: they sinned with 'great' evil and were struck with a 'great' deep.
sources.quote: מִדָּה כְנֶגֶד מִדָּה, הֵם חָטְאוּ בְּרַבָּה רָעַת הָאָדָם וְלָקוּ בִּתְהוֹם רַבָּה:

7:16.headline: 'God shut him in': protected him, or shut against the water?
7:16.body: The word בעד can mean 'for' or 'against'. Rashi gives two readings, that God protected Noach and that God shut the door against the water, while Radak reads it as protection.

sources.says: Rashi says God protected him so that they could not break the ark.
sources.quote: הֵגֵן עָלָיו שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁבְּרוּהָ,

sources.says: Rashi says the plain sense is that God shut against the water, since בעד in Scripture means 'in front of'.
sources.quote: וּפְשׁוּטוֹ שֶׁל מִקְרָא סָגַר כְּנֶגֶדוֹ מִן הַמַּיִם, וְכֵן כָּל בְּעַד שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן כְּנֶגֶד הוּא,

sources.says: Radak says God protected him, so that not even one hole opened in the ark.
sources.quote: הֵגֵן בַּעֲדוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נִפְתַּח בַּתֵּבָה אֲפִלּוּ נֶקֶב אֶחָד

7:22.headline: נשמת רוח חיים: both words, one meaning, or two?
7:22.body: The verse piles up נשמת and רוח. Rashi reads it as 'a breath of the spirit of life', and Radak says נשמת חיים is for people while רוח חיים is for other living things.

sources.says: Rashi says it means 'a breath of the spirit of life'.
sources.quote: נְשָׁמָה שֶׁל רוּחַ חַיִּים:

sources.says: Radak says נשמת חיים is said of people and רוח חיים of the other living things, since נשמה is said only of people.
sources.quote: וְאָמַר נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים עַל הָאָדָם וְרוּחַ חַיִּים עַל שְׁאָרֵי בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים, כִּי לֹא אָמַר נְשָׁמָה אֶלָּא עַל הָאָדָם.

7:23.headline: אך נח: 'only Noach', or 'groaning'?
7:23.body: The plain meaning is 'only Noach was left'. Rashi also gives a midrash that hears 'groaning' in the name: Noach groaned and coughed blood from the work of tending the animals.

sources.says: Rashi says the plain meaning is 'only Noach', and a midrash reads it as groaning and coughing blood from the work of tending the animals.
sources.quote: לְבַד נֹחַ, זֶהוּ פְּשׁוּטוֹ; וּמִ"אַ גוֹנֵחַ וְכוֹהֶה דָם מִטֹּרַח הַבְּהֵמוֹת וְהַחַיּוֹת.

8:1.headline: Radak: God never forgets, so 'remembered' is a manner of speaking
8:1.body: Remembering normally follows forgetting. Radak says neither happens with God. The Torah speaks in human terms so listeners can follow.

sources.quote: אין שכחה ואין זכרון לפניו יתברך, כי לשון זכרון הוא אחר השכחה
sources.says: Radak says there is no forgetting or remembering before God, because remembering comes after forgetting.

sources.quote: אלא דברה תורה בלשון בני אדם להבין השומעים
sources.says: Radak says the Torah speaks in the language of people so that listeners understand.

8:1.headline: Rashi: here the name אלהים means strict justice, turned to mercy
8:1.body: Rashi says the name אלהים stands for God's attribute of strict justice. The prayers of the righteous turn it into mercy.

sources.quote: זה השם מדת הדין הוא, ונהפכה למדת רחמים על ידי תפלת הצדיקים
sources.says: Rashi says this name is the attribute of justice, and it is turned to mercy by the prayers of the righteous.

8:7.headline: The raven went out and back, but circled the ark instead
8:7.body: Rashi reads יצוא ושוב as the raven flying round and round the ark. It did not go on its errand, because it suspected Noah about its mate.

sources.quote: הולך ומקיף סביבות התבה, ולא הלך בשליחותו, שהיה חושדו על בת זוגו
sources.says: Rashi says it went round the ark and did not go on its errand, because it suspected him about its mate.

8:12.headline: The second 'waited' is spelled differently from the first
8:12.body: Rashi says וייחל is the same verb as ויחל in verse 10, in a different form. ויחל is 'he waited'. וייחל is 'he made himself wait'.

sources.quote: הוא לשון ויחל, אלא שזה לשון ויפעל וזה לשון ויתפעל, ויחל – וימתן; וייחל – ויתמתן
sources.says: Rashi says it is the same word as ויחל but in another form: ויחל means he waited, וייחל means he held himself back.

sources.quote: מבנין נפעל ובא כלעיל כמו וילחם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is from the nifal form, like וילחם.

8:13.headline: Two words for dry: the ground's top first, then all of it
8:13.body: Rashi says חרבו here means the ground was like mud with a crust on top. He says יבשה in verse 14 means it was fully dry.

sources.quote: נעשה כמין טיט, שקרמו פניה של מעלה
sources.says: Rashi says the ground became like mud, with a crust formed on its upper face.

sources.quote: נעשה גריד כהלכתה
sources.says: Rashi says on יבשה that it became dry in the proper way.

sources.quote: כי פניה חרבו לבדם ואחר כך יבשה הארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says only its surface had dried, and afterward the earth became dry.

8:17.headline: Written 'bring them out', but read 'let them go out'
8:17.body: The text is written הוצא but read היצא. Rashi says one means 'tell them to go out'. The other means 'bring them out yourself if they will not go'.

sources.quote: הוצא כתיב, היצא קרי, היצא – אמר להם שיצאו; הוצא – אם אינם רוצים לצאת הוציאם אתה
sources.says: Rashi says it is written הוצא and read היצא, and explains each reading.

sources.quote: כתיב בוי״ו בחלוף היו״ד
sources.says: Radak says it is written with a ו in place of the י.

8:21.headline: 'From his youth' hints at the baby being shaken out at birth
8:21.body: Rashi reads מנעריו from the verb 'to shake'. At birth the baby is shaken out of the womb, and from then the evil urge is in him.

sources.quote: משננער לצאת ממעי אמו נתן בו יצר הרע
sources.says: Rashi says from when he is shaken out of his mother's womb the evil urge is placed in him.

sources.quote: אמר רבי יודן מנעריו כתיב משעה שהוא ננער לעולם
sources.says: Radak quotes Rabbi Yudan, who says the word is written מנעריו, from the moment he is shaken out into the world.

8:22.headline: 'Will not cease' may hint that they did cease during the flood
8:22.body: Rashi says the phrase implies day and night did cease all through the flood. Radak says Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argued about it.

sources.quote: מכלל ששבתו כל ימות המבול
sources.says: Rashi says this implies they stopped throughout the days of the flood.

sources.quote: רבי אליעזר אומר לא ישבתו, לא שבתו, רבי יהושע אומר לא ישבתו מכאן ששבתו
sources.says: Radak records that Rabbi Eliezer reads it as 'did not cease' while Rabbi Yehoshua reads it as 'from here, they did cease'.

9:4.headline: 'With its life' may mean a limb cut from a living animal
9:4.body: Rashi reads בנפשו as 'while its life is still in it', so the verse bans eating a limb from a living animal. Ibn Ezra reads it as flesh together with its life, which is its blood.

sources.quote: אסר להם אבר מן החי, כלומר כל זמן שנפשו בו, לא תאכלו הבשר
sources.says: Rashi says this forbids a limb from a living animal: while its life is in it, you may not eat the flesh.

sources.quote: אך בשר עם נפשו שהוא דמו לא תאכלו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means do not eat flesh together with its life, which is its blood.

9:6.headline: 'באדם' may mean 'by a person' or 'for the person'
9:6.body: Rashi reads it as 'by people': if there are witnesses, they put the killer to death. Ibn Ezra gives other readings: before everyone, or for the sake of the man whose blood was shed.

sources.quote: אם יש עדים המיתוהו אתם
sources.says: Rashi says if there are witnesses, you put him to death.

sources.quote: וטעם באדם בעדים או לעיני הכל או בעבור האדם שנשפך דמו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says באדם means by witnesses, or in front of everyone, or for the sake of the man whose blood was shed.

9:12.headline: לדרת is spelled short, hinting some generations needed no sign
9:12.body: Rashi says לדרת is written short. He reads this to mean some generations did not need the rainbow, because they were completely righteous.

sources.quote: נכתב חסר, שיש דורות שלא הצרכו לאות לפי שצדיקים גמורים היו
sources.says: Rashi says it is written short because some generations did not need the sign, being wholly righteous.

9:15.headline: Radak: God does not forget, so 'remember' is a figure of speech
9:15.body: Radak says there is no forgetting before God's throne. The Torah speaks like people do, so 'remember' here is a way of speaking.

sources.quote: דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם, כי אין שכחה לפני כסא כבודו
sources.says: Radak says the Torah speaks in human language, since there is no forgetting before His throne.

9:20.headline: 'Man of the earth': a master of the land, or a farmer?
9:20.body: Rashi says איש האדמה means 'lord of the earth', as איש נעמי in Ruth. Ibn Ezra says it means a man who knew how to work the earth.

sources.quote: אדוני האדמה כמו איש נעמי
sources.says: Rashi says it means master of the earth, like 'the husband of Naomi'.

sources.quote: יודע עבודת האדמה והיא חכמה גדולה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means one who knows the work of the earth, which is great wisdom.

9:21.headline: אהלה, 'his tent', is spelled like the name Oholah
9:21.body: The word is written with a ה, so it can sound like Oholah. Rashi says this hints at Samaria, called Oholah, whose ten tribes were exiled over wine. Ibn Ezra says the ה here just stands for a ו.

sources.quote: אהלה כתיב, רמז לי' שבטים שנקראו על שם שומרון, שנקראת אהלה שגלו על עסקי היין
sources.says: Rashi says it is written אהלה, hinting at the ten tribes named for Samaria, called Oholah, who were exiled over wine.

sources.quote: וה"א אהלה מקום וי"ו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the ה of אהלה stands in place of a ו.

9:23.headline: Why does 'backwards' appear twice for Shem and Japheth?
9:23.body: Rashi says the second mention teaches that when they came near to cover him, they turned their faces away. Ibn Ezra says the word means the reverse of how a person walks.

sources.quote: מלמד שכשקרבו אצלו והצרכו להפך עצמם לכסותו הפכו פניהם אחורנית
sources.says: Rashi says it teaches that when they came near and needed to turn to cover him, they turned their faces backwards.

sources.quote: הפוך הלוך האדם, כי כל תנועתו לפנים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the reverse of a person's walk, since all his movement is forward.

9:25.headline: 'Slave of slaves' may mean a slave like any other slave
9:25.body: Ibn Ezra says עבד עבדים means a slave like one of the slaves. If it meant a slave to slaves it would be spelled differently. Radak says even Canaan's brothers will be slaves and he will serve them.

sources.quote: טעמו עבד כאחד העבדים ואילו היה עבד העבדים היה עבד לעבדים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a slave like one of the slaves, and that 'slave of the slaves' would mean a slave to slaves.

sources.quote: כי גם אחיו יהיו עבדים, והוא יהיה עבד להם
sources.says: Radak says even his brothers will be slaves, and he will be a slave to them.

9:27.headline: The blessing 'God will widen Japheth' plays on the name Japheth
9:27.body: The name יפת and the verb יפת sound alike. Rashi says the Aramaic translation reads the verb as 'widen'. Radak says it means God will enlarge his borders.

sources.quote: מתרגם יפתי, ירחיב
sources.says: Rashi says the Aramaic translation reads יפת as 'may He widen'.

sources.quote: אמר, האלהים ירחיב את גבולו וברכתו
sources.says: Radak says it means God will widen his border and his blessing.
